We study the impact of increasing input-dependence in the steering edit, moving from a difference of means to a destination retrieved per query --- the mean of the $k$ stored states nearest the query, inside the requested class --- in which the two baselines are endpoints: at $k$ equal to the class size the retrieved rule \emph{is} the class-conditional difference of means. We measure input-dependent steering on six substitution corpora that vary in whether the edit changes a word or a clause, and on an external benchmark, and find that input-dependent steering outperforms fixed-direction steering when the destination varies within the class. Retrieval wins at every layer of every substitution corpus in two models, and the level of input-dependence needed governs how to apply it: word-level edits are best made in the first tenth of the network from a few neighbours, clause-level edits at any depth from the class mean. Where the class already determines the answer the class mean suffices and retrieval only matches it, though a fixed direction still fails there. Four quantities computed from the states alone identify the regime in which the edit should be applied.

title: When Strong Reasoners Join the Pool: Small Union Premiums and Costly Runaway Generations in LLM Routing
summary: Routing benchmarks often judge a router against a hindsight oracle that counts a query as solved whenever any model's recorded answer is correct, but under stochastic decoding that oracle mixes two different objects: the clairvoyant ceiling of committing to one model per query and the premium of calling several models and keeping any correct answer. A companion study measured this premium at 3.5 percentage points (pp) for 11 small open models on MATH-500; how large it is once current reasoning models enter the pool was unknown. We measure it with a fixed-protocol, pre-committed generation on a single NVIDIA B300: all 500 MATH-500 problems, 30 seeded samples per problem, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and NVIDIA's Nemotron Nano 9B v2 and Nemotron Super 49B v1.5 (a NAS derivative of the same 70B) under vendor sampling, a 65,536-token cap, a pinned Math-Verify scorer, and an append-only attempt ledger, for 45,000 scored responses. The two reasoning models both reach 96.1% accuracy against 76.2% for the 70B baseline. The empirical product-coupling premium is 0.215-0.588 pp across all two- and three-model pools; the empirical plug-in selection headroom over always calling Nano is 1.27 pp; and resampling Nano three times gives practically the same empirical any-correct rate as calling all three models once. Only 31 responses reached the cap, 25 of them with exactly periodic tails, yet the capped responses account for up to 60.2% of a model's output-length-squared proxy, and long generations made a fourth planned model, Llama-3.1-8B, too slow to finish. The premium is far below the companion's 3.5 pp, but models, pool size and protocol changed together; an oracle gap should therefore be reported with the pool, the protocol, the samples per cell and the decoding budget that produced it.

title: When the Consumer Is an Agent: Execution-Grounded Service-Level Agreements
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly act as service consumers. They select operations and report whether a task is complete. In an asynchronous distributed service, an accepted call or immediate state read does not establish that the required state became observable by its deadline. We introduce execution-grounded completion contracts, which treat completion as a service-level outcome. An independent control plane observes a deadline-bound service-state predicate, admits completion, and directs recovery while the agent performs the task. We evaluate placement and deletion in a live multi-provider data service with heterogeneous models and an injected transfer delay. Across policies, some tasks that missed the deadline were accepted and some that met it were rejected. Under enforcement, accepted completions remained consistent with later observations; all included healthy tasks completed, and unresolved faulted tasks terminated as unverified. The results show that completion of these tasks can be governed by independent observation of service state rather than by the agent's self-assessment.

title: Where Did the Update Go? Certifying Declared Change Envelopes for Model Updates
summary: Deployed language models are updated continually, and regulators increasingly accept changes that were declared in advance. Showing that an update changed behavior only where it was declared to is a different statistical problem from bounding how much it changed: a useful update is meant to change some decisions, so global disagreement and regression bounds cannot certify it. We formalize the problem with declared change envelopes. Before training, the developer commits to a region of inputs, and every decision that changes outside it counts as leakage. Leakage compares two models, so it can be certified from unlabeled traffic with anytime-valid tests whose sample cost we bound from above and below, and per-update certificates compose into a bound on lifetime drift outside all declared scopes. We measure leakage for LoRA and full fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, and knowledge editing on models from 1.5B to 72B parameters. Narrow updates leak widely: domain and policy LoRA updates keep only about 7-36% of the decisions they change inside the declared scope. Across 256 trained variants, leakage tracks the update's KL divergence to the incumbent on out-of-scope inputs (Spearman 0.94). None of the customary remedies we tested makes a rule-like update certifiable without giving up much of its intended change. Distilling the incumbent's decisions on unlabeled prompts in the deployment format does: anchored LoRA, GRPO, and (at a small learning rate) full fine-tuning updates certify 5% leakage from a few hundred to a few thousand unlabeled samples, and the certificates replicate on held-out traffic and on written answers. The certificates cover decision-like outputs only; on open-ended chat, re-batching alone changes 11-21% of responses and no update certifies. Code: https://github.com/Usama1002/declared-change-envelopes

title: Where Do Distilled Students Store Thinking?
summary: Small students degrade on large reasoning models' (LRMs') long solutions, so recent work shortens them by interpolating an LRM with a short-answer model at ratio $λ$. We ask what student weights retain when this teacher stops thinking, comparing LoRA adapters of three students from three teacher pairs at each $λ$. In each pair, the adapters' update subspace shifts most where the teacher stops thinking and solutions shorten most, locating the change without attributing it. We identify a shared adapter subspace tied to thinking-like behavior (reflective markers, monologue format and long solutions). Shared by adapters before that point, it keeps about half (post hoc) while one pair's teacher halves its solutions but keeps its think tag, and largely empties after thinking stops. Removing it largely turns this behavior off for every pair, student and benchmark. Only in that pair and one other student does it leave clearly fewer markers than removing the update's top components; elsewhere, same-energy random directions often nearly match it. Grafted into a short-answer student at twice its weight, it turns early markers (a post hoc count) on, like the whole update, but the student rarely finishes. Our work identifies a weight subspace tied to distilled thinking-like behavior.

title: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version)
summary: LLM agents often give conflicting answers to the same question, and many deployed agents are variants of one base model, so their errors are correlated. We study truth discovery among such agents: inferring the true answer and each agent's reliability without labels. Classical truth-discovery and crowdsourcing estimators reward an agreeing bloc and can fall below majority vote. We propose BP-TD, which adds per-agent decorrelation weights to mean-field variational inference on a one-coin Dawid-Skene model, so that agents sharing a base model count together as about one vote. Its first iteration is exactly a weighted vote; later iterations estimate agent reliability. With 13 local agents on MMLU, BP-TD beats majority vote without any labels (0.716 vs. 0.624 on 160 questions; 0.707 vs. 0.674 on 10,000) and ranks agents by their true accuracy, which classical estimators invert. The gain depends on the pool: over 2,852 sub-pools of four benchmarks, decorrelation helps when the largest correlated bloc is weaker than the other agents and hurts when it is the strongest, and we found no label-free statistic that tells the two cases apart. Labels change the picture quickly: with 20 labelled questions, selecting the single best agent is more accurate than every aggregator we tested on MMLU, ARC and TruthfulQA.

title: Who is the Pronoun Pro? Comparing LLMs and Humans at Number-Disambiguation of 'they'
summary: This study evaluates whether large language models (LLMs) can reliably replace or complement human research assistants in linguistically complex annotation. In a controlled annotation task, 73 human annotators (local students and crowdworkers with and without a background in linguistics) and more than 40 LLM configurations number-disambiguated 174 authentic uses of 'they' from Reddit, including innovative and context-sensitive cases. The best LLM, Kimi K3, reached 94.5% accuracy, above the human majority vote (86.2%) and the mean of the top half of human annotators (78.5%); only the single best human annotator scored higher (95.7%). LLMs also offer substantial practical advantages in cost and speed. However, qualitative error analysis reveals a crucial complementarity: human reasoning in low-agreement cases exposes inconsistencies in the annotation typology and thereby improves the methodological framework itself. The study contributes (i) a benchmark-style human-LLM comparison for a semantically demanding task, (ii) transparent cost and time evidence, and (iii) a methodological argument against a purely replacement-oriented view of automation. LLMs are viable for large-scale annotation support in linguistics, but their responsible use requires human critical oversight. The dataset with its gold-standard labels, all human and LLM annotations, and the fully reproducible code are openly available as a Quarto-based, public repository.

title: Whose startup does the AI back? An algorithm audit of reputation and demographic signals in LLM-assisted crowdfunding
summary: Large language model (LLM) assistants increasingly advise backers on which crowdfunding campaigns to support. LLMs have known race and gender problems, and it is unsettled whether they reproduce, erase, or reverse the discrimination documented in entrepreneurial finance. We ask when, and through which decision process, LLM assistants use founders' gender and ethnicity. In a pre-specified choice-based conjoint experiment, seven LLMs chose among five synthetic campaigns with independently randomized quality signals and founder names, under three backer personas and a persona-free control (40,248 responses). By default, founder names barely matter: under budget-conscious and delivery-focused personas, gender and Black-name effects are statistically equivalent to zero. When the backer wants to support underrepresented creators, the models favor Black-signaled (+8.1 percentage points; positive in all seven models) and female-signaled (+5.1) founders. They do so most strongly among near-tied campaigns and for the founder who alone carries the signal, and they almost never name gender or ethnicity in their reasons. The results fit an agency account of algorithmic discrimination: an aligned assistant takes its demographic preferences from its user rather than from its training data.

title: Why Pay for Long Reasoning When Rewrite Do Trick? Causal Effects of Reasoning History Compaction on Future Generation and Agent Cost
summary: Reasoning substantially improves language models' ability to solve difficult problems, but long reasoning traces make these gains expensive. Efficient reasoning should express useful analysis in fewer tokens by reducing repetition and text that adds little value to solving the problem. Progress in proprietary models motivates this goal, yet their hidden scratchpads limit direct study of how it is achieved. We investigate whether open-weight models can generate less verbose reasoning by changing the form of their own earlier thoughts, without retraining. Our intervention rewrites prior reasoning into compact state records before pending tool results are revealed, then compares continuations from original and compact histories. Across the tested models, accepted compact histories usually shorten future reasoning; a coding case study also shows less repeated verification after a shared candidate solution. In software-agent deployments, compaction can reduce total spending, although task quality and rewrite-inclusive time depend on the target and compressor. These findings identify reasoning history as one way to reduce future reasoning-token use and motivate model-specific compaction policies evaluated for both efficiency and retained capability.

title: Workload-Static Optical Circuit Switching For Scalable LLM Inference Decode
summary: LLM inference decode executes fine-grained collectives whose latency directly limits per-user interactivity, yet scale-up fabrics are still built from electronic packet switches designed for training. We observe that, for a given model deployment and parallelization, the communication structure of decode is fixed, and propose workload-static optical circuit switching (OCS): circuits are configured once per deployment, co-designed with model parallelism and with topology-aware collective schedules that turn spare accelerator ports into fewer communication phases or higher bandwidth. We evaluate this design with GXNET, a graph-based workload emulator coupled to analytical and flit-level network models grounded in hardware measurements. In a 576-accelerator scale-up domain serving 5T-parameter MoE models with up to 5M tokens of context, all-OCS fabrics improve interactivity by up to 65% and energy efficiency by up to 119% over 4:1 oversubscribed packet-switched fabrics.

title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
summary: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) integrate visual understanding, generation, and editing within a single unified framework. However, existing unified multimodal datasets and benchmarks remain dominated by single-turn tasks. Even in recent multi-turn datasets, many turns can be solved independently without tracking information across turns. Consequently, they provide limited supervision and evaluation for multimodal stateful interaction, which requires models to understand, maintain, update, and faithfully realize evolving dialogue states across turns. To address this gap, we introduce YANAMI, the first large-scale multimodal dialogue dataset and benchmark for stateful interaction, comprising YANAMI-400K and YANAMI-Bench. YANAMI-400K contains 400K multi-turn multimodal dialogues, with more than 2M images and 2.6M dialogue turns. The dialogues span four representative scenarios: Multi-Image Fusion, Image Editing, World Modeling, and Visual Reasoning, and require models to continuously track, preserve, and revise evolving multimodal dialogue states across turns. YANAMI-Bench comprises 400 multi-turn dialogues for systematically evaluating multimodal stateful interaction. It jointly evaluates Dialogue State Understanding and Visual Realization, characterizing the gap between models' ability to understand evolving dialogue states and their ability to faithfully realize them in visual outputs. Experiments show that fine-tuning BAGEL on YANAMI-400K improves image editing, generation, and multimodal stateful interaction by 10.3%, 2.0%, and 13.23%, respectively, while preserving its general visual understanding capabilities. Evaluations on YANAMI-Bench further reveal that existing UMMs still struggle to maintain, update, and visually realize evolving multimodal dialogue states.

title: ZEMA: confidence-calibrated signed descent with only one state
summary: Recent work characterizes the Adam optimizer as sign descent modulated by gradient uncertainty: the update is the sign of the batch gradient, scaled by how strongly the batch supports that sign. We apply this view directly and introduce ZEMA (Z-score Evidence Momentum Adaptation), which measures that support with a per-coordinate $z$-score computed from the per-example gradients in the current batch, converts it into a sign probability, and smooths the resulting update with a single exponential moving average. Because the probability is formed before smoothing rather than after, ZEMA keeps one state per parameter instead of Adam's two, at a $4.6$ increase in per-step time; the per-example variance it requires can also be estimated from a small fraction of the batch. In fine-tuning and pretraining experiments, ZEMA is competitive with Adam, reduces the variability of the validation loss, and in some settings recovers the sign of the full-dataset gradient more consistently. We close with two directions this opens: extending confidence adaptation beyond the sign geometry, to methods such as Muon, and to differentially private training.

title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
summary:
Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity. Computationally modeling this process requires capturing both biologically plausible mutations and antigen-specific selection. However, existing mutation models do not directly optimize binding, while affinity optimization often neglects realistic mutation trajectories.
  We introduce iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning (RL) framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization. Stage 1 learns an SHM mutation prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. Stage 2 initializes an RL policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the frozen prior. To prevent reward exploitation, including repetitive high-reward substitutions and structurally tolerated framework mutations, we introduce a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective. RewardNet smooths the affinity landscape, while TaxNet penalizes reward overexploitation, jointly defining a learned meta-reward for policy optimization.
  We evaluate iGC on mutation prediction, SHM consistency, affinity optimization, and mutation diversity. The mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline in mutation-site prediction. Following RL optimization, iGC maintains SHM sequence structure. It also achieves a strong exploration-exploitation balance, yielding competitive reward-diversity products across candidate-selection cutoffs. These results demonstrate that iGC integrates biologically plausible mutation generation with antigen-specific affinity selection, providing an in silico framework for iterative antibody affinity maturation.

title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
summary: We present a shared framework that adapts Cosmos world foundation models for real-time interactive world simulation in Physical AI. By streaming visual observations in response to actions and scene controls, the framework enables users and embodied agents to interact with evolving virtual environments. It supports both predicting the visual consequences of actions and generating observations from physical state maintained by an external simulator. We demonstrate this approach across camera navigation and robot manipulation, controllable video transfer, and multi-view autonomous vehicle (AV) simulation. These examples provide a shared foundation for developing interactive virtual environments for Physical AI training and evaluation. Our code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/nvidia/cosmos and https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/cosmos3-examples. The project website is available at https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos-simulation.
summary_zh: 我们提出一个共享框架，将Cosmos世界基础模型适配至物理AI中的实时交互式世界模拟。通过响应动作与场景控制，流式传输视觉观察结果，该框架使用户及具身智能体能够与不断演化的虚拟环境进行交互。它既支持预测动作的视觉后果，也支持从外部模拟器维护的物理状态生成观察结果。我们在相机导航与机器人操控、可控视频迁移以及多视角自动驾驶（AV）模拟中演示了这一方法。这些示例为开发用于物理AI训练与评估的交互式虚拟环境提供了共享基础。我们的代码与模型检查点可在https://github.com/nvidia/cosmos 与 https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/cosmos3-examples 获取。项目网站为 https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos-simulation。
tldr: This paper introduces a framework adapting NVIDIA's Cosmos world foundation models for real-time interactive world simulation, enabling action-conditioned visual prediction for robot manipulation, camera navigation, and multi-view autonomous vehicle simulation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一个框架，将NVIDIA的Cosmos世界基础模型用于实时交互式世界模拟，支持针对机器人操作、相机导航和多视角自动驾驶仿真的动作条件视觉预测。

title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
summary: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.
summary_zh: 以自我为中心的人类视频为机器人学习提供了可扩展的操作先验来源，但将原始数据规模转化为泛化的机器人策略需要严格的数据筛选与训练方案。我们提出Open-HumanWAM，这是首个将自我中心预训练扩展至50,000小时的完全开源方案，其核心是Open-HumanWAM-50K——一个经过精心筛选、密集标注手部动作与自然语言的自我中心视频语料库。基于该语料库，我们通过闭环仿真评估系统性地研究了纯人类预训练，并揭示了一条经验性的对数线性缩放定律，将预训练数据时长与下游机器人成功率联系起来。基于这些发现，我们开发了HumanWAM-Vanilla，一个仅在5万小时自我中心人类视频上预训练的世界-动作模型。在机器人后训练阶段，HumanWAM-Vanilla在RoboTwin 2.0的Clean2Clean任务上达到92.08%的成功率，在Clean2Random任务上达到68.88%，同时在RoboDojo上取得14.17%的平均成功率和19.00的平均进度得分。为进一步突破能力边界，我们探索了联合人-机预训练，提出HumanWAM-Goal，一种以视觉目标为条件的的世界-动作模型。混合数据扩展在仿真与物理基准上均实现了广泛的零样本泛化，将后训练的RoboTwin 2.0性能推至新的最优水平：Clean2Clean达到92.70%，Clean2Random大幅跃升至84.60%。在实体机器人上，HumanWAM-Goal进一步展现出涌现的具身上下文学习能力，无需更新参数即可动态调整其操作行为以适应未见过的视觉目标。为支持具身智能领域可复现的扩展研究，我们开源了Open-HumanWAM-50K语料库、数据筛选与预训练流水线，以及预训练和后训练的HumanWAM模型权重、推理代码和仿真评估套件。
tldr: This paper introduces Open-HumanWAM, an open recipe for scaling egocentric human video pretraining to 50k hours for embodied foundation models, and presents HumanWAM world-action models that achieve strong robot manipulation performance in simulation and physical benchmarks, including emergent in-context learning.
tldr_zh: 本文介绍了Open-HumanWAM，一个用于将自我中心人类视频预训练扩展到5万小时以训练具身基础模型的开放方案，并展示了在仿真和物理基准上表现优异、且具有涌现上下文学习能力的HumanWAM世界-动作模型。

title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
summary: Coding agents powered by models such as GPT-6-Astra connect spatial reasoning with executable robot behavior, raising the question of how such agents can produce lasting improvements in robot capabilities from physical interaction. In this work, we study embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) through real-world exploration, code refinement, and deployment using PyRUA-REAL, a framework in which coding agents retain interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable executable skills that inform subsequent exploration and improvement. Our empirical study places physical manipulation at the center of the improvement process, examining how agents collaborate, what kinds of execution feedback support effective code refinement, and how task specifications and previously acquired skills influence robustness and task transfer. We further investigate the efficiency and capability of the resulting programs when deployed without involving an online agent for decision-making. Across eight real-world tasks, PyRUA-REAL achieves an average success rate of 91.1%. In complementary evaluation on 42 tasks from the RoboDojo benchmark, it achieves an average success rate of 84.4%. This study provides empirical guidance for turning physical exploration into reusable robot skills that support continued improvement and robust, efficient deployment.
summary_zh: 由GPT-6-Astra等模型驱动的编程智能体将空间推理与可执行的机器人行为相连接，由此引发了一个问题：此类智能体如何通过物理交互为机器人能力带来持久提升？在本研究中，我们通过真实世界探索、代码精炼和部署，研究了具身递归自我改进（RSI），并提出了PyRUA-REAL框架。在该框架中，编程智能体将交互经验保留为持久记忆，并将其转化为可复用的可执行技能，从而为后续的探索和改进提供指导。我们的实证研究将物理操作置于改进过程的核心，考察了智能体如何协作、何种类型的执行反馈有助于支持有效的代码精炼，以及任务规范与先前习得的技能如何影响鲁棒性和任务迁移。我们进一步评估了在无在线智能体参与决策的情况下，所生成程序在部署时的效率与能力。在八项真实世界任务中，PyRUA-REAL实现了平均91.1%的成功率；在来自RoboDojo基准的42项任务的补充评估中，平均成功率达到84.4%。本研究为将物理探索转化为可复用机器人技能提供了实证指导，以支持持续改进以及鲁棒、高效的部署。
tldr: This paper introduces PyRUA-REAL, a framework for embodied recursive self-improvement where coding agents use real-world interaction, persistent memory, and reusable executable skills to iteratively refine robot manipulation policies. It demonstrates high success rates across real-world and benchmark tasks, providing empirical guidance for turning physical exploration into reusable robot skills.
tldr_zh: 本文介绍了 PyRUA-REAL，一个具身递归自我改进框架，其中编码代理通过真实世界交互、持久记忆和可复用执行技能，迭代改进机器人操作策略。在真实世界和基准任务上展示了高成功率，为将物理探索转化为可复用机器人技能提供了经验指导。

title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
summary: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. This survey reviews work from January 2024 to early November 2026, with earlier studies included to establish technical lineages. We organize the literature into five interdependent layers: hardware; data collection and curation; cross-embodiment transfer; learning and foundation models; and evaluation and applications. Human hand-object understanding and tactile sensing provide two cross-cutting perspectives. A system-level architecture, comparative tables and five case analyses connect design choices across these layers. We distinguish within-study experimental comparisons from heterogeneous corpus statistics, vendor specifications and company-reported results. Three conclusions emerge. First, the value of human data depends on kinematic, visual and contact alignment, not recording volume alone. Second, shared action representations and foundation policies do not remove embodiment-specific constraints on force, latency and contact. Third, task completion is insufficient to establish physical correctness or deployment readiness. Evidence remains limited for zero-shot transfer of contact-rich skills between morphologically different hands, long-duration reliability, and cross-sensor tactile generalization. We identify eleven open problems and propose reporting interfaces and controlled comparisons that can make full-stack progress more measurable. The review is a structured narrative synthesis rather than a pooled performance ranking or an exhaustive systematic review.
summary_zh: 灵巧机器人手正日益与大规模人类数据和基础模型相结合，然而硬件、表示学习和评估方面的进展往往被分别考量。本综述回顾了2024年1月至2026年11月初的相关研究，并纳入更早期的工作以厘清技术脉络。我们将文献组织为五个相互依赖的层次：硬件；数据采集与整理；跨具身迁移；学习与基础模型；以及评估与应用。人类手部-物体理解和触觉感知提供了两个跨领域的交叉视角。系统级架构、对比表格及五个案例研究将各层次之间的设计选择联系起来。我们区分了研究内部的实验比较与异质性语料库统计、供应商规格说明及公司报告结果之间的差异。由此得出三点结论。首先，人类数据的价值取决于运动学、视觉和接触对齐程度，而不仅仅是记录量的大小。其次，共享的动作表示和基础策略并未消除力、延迟和接触方面受具身形态制约的限制。第三，任务完成情况不足以证明物理正确性或部署就绪性。关于形态不同手部之间接触丰富技能的零样本迁移、长时间运行可靠性以及跨传感器触觉泛化的证据仍然有限。我们识别出十一个开放性问题，并提出了报告接口和受控比较方案，以使全栈进展更可量化。本综述是一种结构化的叙事综合，而非汇总式的性能排名或详尽无遗的系统评价。
tldr: A full-stack survey of dexterous robotic hands in the foundation-model era, covering hardware, data, cross-embodiment transfer, learning, and evaluation, identifying open problems and reporting gaps.
tldr_zh: 一篇关于基础模型时代灵巧机械手的全栈综述，涵盖硬件、数据、跨实体迁移、学习和评估，并指出了开放问题和报告缺口。

title: Where Is VLA Inference Time Spent? Bottlenecks and Optimization Interactions Across GPUs
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models map camera observations and language instructions to robot actions. However, their large backbones and repeated action generation can make inference take longer than the robot's real-time requirements for its next action. To reduce the load of VLA computations, researchers have proposed multiple optimization approaches, including quantization and pruning. These optimizations can be combined with other general optimizations such as better kernel compilation or using CUDA graphs instead of the eager mode. However, most of these optimization results are usually reported on a single GPU type, typically for a few VLA models, with no analysis of what the real bottlenecks are for a model on a particular hardware or how these optimizations would generalize beyond the reported results. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive measurement study of seven families of inference optimization methods, from CUDA graphs and compilation to token pruning and quantization, on seven state-of-the-art VLAs evaluated on four GPU families ranging from a datacenter H100 to an embedded Jetson Thor. We analyse how CPU launch overhead, memory bandwidth, and kernel efficiency jointly shape optimization gains, and how applying one method changes the benefit of another. From this analysis, we derive VLA-Triage, guidelines for stacking optimizations under latency budgets. The guidelines identify which stages can provide the required savings and which combinations need testing in the deployed execution mode.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型将摄像头观测与语言指令映射为机器人动作。然而，其庞大的骨干网络以及反复的动作生成过程，可能导致推理耗时超出机器人对下一动作的实时性要求。为减轻VLA计算负担，研究者提出了多种优化方法，包括量化和剪枝。这些优化还可与其他通用优化手段结合使用，例如更优的内核编译，或采用CUDA图替代即时执行模式。然而，大多数优化结果通常仅在单一GPU类型上报告，且仅针对少数VLA模型，未分析特定硬件上模型面临的真实瓶颈，也未评估这些优化在报告结果之外的泛化能力。本文针对七类推理优化方法开展了全面的测量研究，涵盖CUDA图、编译、token剪枝及量化等技术，并在七种最新VLA模型上进行了评估，测试覆盖从数据中心级H100到嵌入式Jetson Thor的四种GPU平台。我们分析了CPU启动开销、内存带宽与内核效率如何共同影响优化收益，以及应用一种优化方法如何改变另一种优化方法的效果。基于此分析，我们提出了VLA-Triage，即在延迟预算下叠加优化策略的指导准则。该准则明确了哪些阶段能够提供所需的性能节约，以及哪些组合需要在实际部署执行模式下进行测试。
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive measurement study of inference optimization methods for vision-language-action (VLA) models across multiple GPU families, analyzing bottlenecks and interactions to derive guidelines for stacking optimizations under latency budgets.
tldr_zh: 本文对视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型的推理优化方法进行了全面的测量研究，分析了多种GPU上的瓶颈及优化间的相互作用，并提出了在延迟预算下叠加优化的指导原则。

title: Which Physical Tactile Cues Matter for Contact-Rich Imitation Learning? A Controlled Real-Robot Study
summary: Vision-based tactile sensors capture multiple aspects of physical interaction within a single image stream, including contact appearance, geometry, indentation depth, and tangential deformation. However, existing visuo-tactile policies often directly process tactile observations as images, making it difficult to determine which physical cues contribute to policy learning. This paper presents a controlled real-robot study that compares physically interpretable tactile signals using the LeRobot platform, enhanced with our visuo-tactile perception system. From the same tactile stream, we derive tactile RGB images, normal/depth maps, and marker-flow fields, representing contact appearance, geometry, and tangential deformation, respectively. Using identical task demonstrations and the same policy backbone, we evaluate the individual and combined contributions of these tactile cues. We further compare tactile encoders and visuo-tactile fusion strategies. Evaluation across 720 real-robot trials yields four key findings: (1) tactile perception substantially improves the overall success rate from 57.8% to 78.9%, although its contribution varies across task stages; (2) marker flow is the most effective individual cue, achieving a success rate of 74.4% and playing a particularly important role in regulating established contact; (3) cue-factorized encoding consistently improves performance, highlighting that different physical cues require tailored processing techniques; and (4) although the effectiveness of tactile fusion is task-dependent, cross-attention offers a lightweight solution with performance comparable to that of pretrained tactile encoders.
summary_zh: 基于视觉的触觉传感器能够在单一图像流中捕捉物理交互的多个方面，包括接触外观、几何形状、压入深度及切向变形。然而，现有的视觉-触觉策略往往直接将触觉观测作为图像处理，难以确定哪些物理线索有助于策略学习。本文提出了一项受控的真实机器人研究，利用LeRobot平台并集成我们开发的视觉-触觉感知系统，对比了具有物理可解释性的触觉信号。从同一触觉流中，我们分别提取了触觉RGB图像、法向/深度图以及标记点流场，分别表征接触外观、几何形状和切向变形。在相同的任务演示和策略主干下，我们评估了这些触觉线索各自及其组合的贡献，并进一步比较了不同的触觉编码器与视觉-触觉融合策略。基于720次真实机器人实验的评估得出四项关键结论：（1）触觉感知将整体成功率从57.8%显著提升至78.9%，但其贡献在不同任务阶段存在差异；（2）标记点流是最有效的单一线索，成功率达到74.4%，在调节已建立接触方面尤为关键；（3）线索分解编码持续提升性能，表明不同物理线索需要针对性的处理技术；（4）尽管触觉融合的有效性与任务相关，但交叉注意力提供了一种轻量级解决方案，其性能可与预训练触觉编码器相媲美。
tldr: This paper presents a controlled real-robot study on the LeRobot platform to evaluate the individual and combined contributions of different physical tactile cues (RGB images, normal/depth maps, marker flow) for contact-rich imitation learning, finding that marker flow is the most effective cue and that cue-factorized encoding improves performance.
tldr_zh: 本文在LeRobot平台上进行了一项受控的真实机器人研究，评估不同物理触觉线索（RGB图像、法向/深度图、标记流）在接触丰富的模仿学习中的单独和组合贡献，发现标记流是最有效的线索，且线索分离编码能提升性能。

title: Compounding Physical RSI: Turning Execution Failure into Inherited Capability
summary:
Generalist robot policies are trained on static offline datasets, yet physical manipulation unfolds sequentially across stages. Because a weakness in a downstream stage remains unobservable until the policy passes earlier ones, each resolved bottleneck exposes the next hidden failure mode. This staged structure calls for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), in which a policy iteratively executes, diagnoses failures, and updates itself. Moreover, because task completion behaves like a product of stage-level pass rates, recursive gains can multiply across generations. In physical environments, three bottlenecks obstruct compounding: terminal execution feedback rarely localizes the stage that caused a failure, failed trajectories do not supply the corrective action, and updating shared parameters can degrade previously mastered skills.
  We propose Compounding Physical RSI, a self-evolving policy framework that turns execution failures into heritable capability. First, automated capability-gap assessment traces failed rollouts to the task stage where progression breaks down and formulates a structured improvement objective. Second, conditioned on this objective, our remedy stage curates validated, stage-relevant experience and refines the policy via behavior-regularized offline reinforcement learning, without requiring costly online rollouts at each optimization step. Third, to safeguard existing skills, our retention stage constructs weight-space candidates between the inherited reference policy and the refined policy, evaluates them across the task suite, and promotes the best candidate as the reference state for the next generation.
  Evaluated across all 42 tasks of the RoboDojo-Sim benchmark, CSU-AI-07 ranks first on the leaderboard with a three-seed mean Overall Score of 26.15 and Success Rate of 20.70%, outperforming the next-best entry by 5.92 points and 5.82 percentage points.
summary_zh:
通用型机器人策略通常在静态离线数据集上训练，然而物理操作任务本身是分阶段递进展开的。由于下游阶段的不足在策略顺利通过前序阶段之前往往无法显现，每一个被解决的瓶颈都会暴露出下一个隐藏的失败模式。这种阶段化结构催生了递归式自我改进（RSI）方法，即策略通过迭代执行、诊断失败并自我更新来不断进步。此外，由于任务完成率可视为各阶段通过率的乘积，递归改进的成效能够在代际间成倍累积。在物理环境中，三个瓶颈阻碍了这种复合式提升：终端执行反馈难以精准定位导致失败的阶段，失败轨迹无法提供修正动作，以及更新共享参数可能导致已有技能退化。
为此，我们提出复合式物理递归自我改进（Compounding Physical RSI）框架，一种将执行失败转化为可遗传能力的自我进化策略体系。首先，自动化能力缺口评估将失败轨迹溯源至任务中断的阶段，并据此构建结构化的改进目标。其次，在该目标引导下，补救阶段筛选经过验证的阶段相关经验，并通过行为正则化的离线强化学习对策略进行精炼，无需在每步优化中依赖昂贵的在线交互。最后，为保障已有技能，保留阶段在继承的参考策略与精炼策略之间构造权重空间候选，在完整任务集上进行评估，并将最优候选提升为下一代的参考状态。
在RoboDojo-Sim基准的全部42项任务中，CSU-AI-07以三粒种子的平均综合得分26.15和成功率20.70%位居排行榜首位，领先次优参赛方案5.92分和5.82个百分点。
tldr: This paper introduces a Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) framework for robot policies, which iteratively identifies and fixes stage-level failures through offline RL, and preserves previous skills via weight-space candidate selection, achieving top performance on the RoboDojo-Sim benchmark.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于机器人策略的递归自我改进（RSI）框架，通过离线强化学习迭代识别并修复阶段级失败，并通过权重空间候选选择保留已有技能，在RoboDojo-Sim基准上取得了最优性能。

title: SCRUB: Contact-Based Surface-Frame Estimation for Force-Motion Control with an Armless Quadruped
summary: Wiping, sanding, and inspection robots press a sliding tool on a surface with controlled force. Controlling that force needs the surface normal, which is unknown on real-world, unmapped surfaces. Surface-normal estimators can help estimate the surface normal, but they either need a friction model or assume that the instantaneous tool velocity lies along the surface; however, walking violates this assumption. We propose SCRUB, a contact-based surface-frame estimator, which lets an armless quadruped slide a body-mounted tool along near-vertical surfaces in the absence of known, axis-aligned, or vision-predicted normals. SCRUB's predictive controller presses and slides the tool using a Kalman-filter estimate of the normal from two cues: 1) A force cue measures the estimate's tilt across the motion. If friction directly opposes the motion, the cue is zero exactly when that tilt is zero, for any friction coefficient. However, if the cue's sliding direction is wrong, friction appears as a false tilt. 2) A velocity cue measures tilt along the motion. Walking and pressing move the tool in and out. SCRUB therefore subtracts the commanded press rate from the tool velocity, averages the result over each gait cycle, and treats this mean as lying along the surface. On Unitree Go1 hardware at nominal speed and load, SCRUB completed every wall traverse and column orbit. No orbit completed with either cue removed, without gait averaging, or with a fixed normal.
summary_zh: 擦拭、打磨及检测机器人会以受控力将滑动工具按压在表面上。控制该力需要表面法向量，而在真实、未测绘的表面上，这一法向量是未知的。表面法向量估计器有助于估算表面法向量，但它们或需依赖摩擦模型，或假设工具瞬时速度沿表面方向；然而，行走过程会破坏这一假设。我们提出SCRUB，一种基于接触的表面坐标系估计器，使无臂四足机器人能够在缺乏已知、轴向对齐或视觉预测法向量的情况下，沿近垂直表面滑动其机身搭载的工具。SCRUB的预测控制器利用卡尔曼滤波器根据两种线索估计法向量，以施压并滑动工具：1）力线索测量估计量在运动过程中的倾斜度。若摩擦力直接与运动方向相反，则当该倾斜度为零时，该线索恰好为零，与摩擦系数无关。然而，若该线索的滑动方向错误，摩擦力将表现为虚假的倾斜度。2）速度线索测量沿运动方向的倾斜度。行走与按压使工具进出移动。因此，SCRUB将指令按压速率从工具速度中减去，对每个步态周期内的结果取平均，并将该均值视为沿表面方向。在Unitree Go1硬件上，以标称速度和负载运行时，SCRUB完成了所有墙面穿越和圆柱环绕任务。在移除任一线索、不进行步态平均或使用固定法向量的情况下，均无法完成任何环绕任务。
tldr: SCRUB is a contact-based surface-frame estimator that enables an armless quadruped to slide a tool along vertical surfaces with force control by estimating the surface normal from force and velocity cues, demonstrated on real hardware.
tldr_zh: SCRUB 是一种基于接触的表面坐标系估计器，通过力和速度线索估计表面法线，使无臂四足机器人能够在垂直表面上进行力控滑动操作，并在真实硬件上得到验证。

title: Playing Soccer Like Humans Do: Learning Versatile and Agile Humanoid Soccer via Latent Motion Priors
summary: Humanoid soccer requires a robot to seamlessly combine agile locomotion, ball manipulation, and impact-rich contact dynamics across a continuous, dynamic behavioral spectrum. Yet existing approaches either cover only a limited set of skills, or forego motion priors entirely and produce unnatural behaviors, leaving the combination of a unified skill set and human-like motion quality unaddressed. We present soccerbot, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that resolves both limitations through a structured latent motion prior distilled from large-scale human soccer motion capture data. By constraining policy learning within this dynamically plausible motion manifold, a single skill-conditioned policy naturally learns to perform moving, dribbling, trapping, and kicking in a unified formulation, while inherently producing human-like motion and fluid transitions during commanded skill switching. Augmented by robustness-oriented simulation design, soccerbot transfers zero-shot to the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, demonstrating agile, natural, and robust execution of the full soccer skill repertoire under real-world conditions.
summary_zh: 类人机器人足球要求机器人在连续、动态的行为谱系中，无缝融合敏捷运动、控球操作以及富含冲击的接触动力学。然而，现有方法要么仅覆盖有限的一组技能，要么完全放弃运动先验并产生不自然的行为，未能解决统一技能集与类人运动质量的结合问题。我们提出了soccerbot，一种层级强化学习框架，通过从大规模人类足球运动捕捉数据中提炼的结构化潜在运动先验，同时解决了上述两个局限。通过将策略学习约束在该动态合理的运动流形内，一个单一技能条件策略自然学会以统一公式执行移动、运球、停球和射门，同时在命令切换时固有地产生类人运动和流畅过渡。辅以面向鲁棒性的仿真设计，soccerbot零样本迁移至Unitree G1人形机器人，在真实世界条件下展示了完整足球技能集的敏捷、自然且鲁棒的执行能力。
tldr: This paper presents soccerbot, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that uses a latent motion prior distilled from human soccer motion capture data to enable a single skill-conditioned policy to perform agile and human-like soccer skills (moving, dribbling, trapping, kicking) on a real humanoid robot with zero-shot transfer.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了 soccerbot，一种层次化强化学习框架，利用从人类足球运动捕捉数据中提炼的潜在运动先验，使单一技能条件策略能够在真实人形机器人上零样本迁移地执行敏捷且类人的足球技能（移动、运球、停球、踢球）。

title: H^2MARL: Hierarchical Heterogeneous Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Humanoid Robot Control
summary: Coordinated whole-body control of humanoid robots remains challenging due to high-dimensional coupled dynamics and substantial physical heterogeneity across joint degrees of freedom (JDoFs). Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods either employ coarse agent partitions or directly apply generic heterogeneous-agent algorithms, while hierarchical controllers commonly optimize high-level planning and low-level execution independently, leading to uncoordinated motion. In this paper, we propose H^2MARL, a hierarchical heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with two key mechanisms. We first formulate humanoid whole-body control using a JDoF-level physical-heterogeneity-aware policy factorization, where each torque-actuated JDoF is conditioned on an explicit descriptor of its actuation, kinematic, and dynamic properties. Moreover, we develop a closed-loop policy-executor co-optimization mechanism that jointly adapts the high-level pose planner and the low-level joint executor using shared interaction trajectories, thereby reducing the distribution mismatch between planning and execution. Extensive experiments in MuJoCo and Isaac Gym demonstrate that H^2MARL consistently improves locomotion stability, gait coordination, and motion quality over homogeneous, coarse-grained, and independently optimized alternatives.
summary_zh: 类人机器人全身协调控制因高维耦合动力学以及各关节自由度在物理特性上的显著异质性而仍具挑战性。现有基于多智能体强化学习的方法要么采用粗略的智能体划分，要么直接应用通用的异质智能体算法，而分层控制器通常将高层规划与低层执行分别独立优化，导致运动缺乏协调性。本文提出H^2MARL，一种分层异构多智能体强化学习框架，包含两个关键机制。首先，我们利用基于关节自由度级别的物理异质性感知策略分解来构建类人机器人全身控制，其中每个力矩驱动的关节自由度均以显式描述符来表征其驱动、运动学及动力学属性。此外，我们开发了闭环策略-执行器协同优化机制，利用共享交互轨迹联合调整高层姿态规划器与低层关节执行器，从而减小规划与执行之间的分布不匹配。在MuJoCo和Isaac Gym中的大量实验表明，H^2MARL在运动稳定性、步态协调性和运动质量方面持续优于同质、粗粒度及独立优化的对比方法。
tldr: H^2MARL introduces a hierarchical heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for humanoid whole-body control, leveraging JDoF-level physical-heterogeneity-aware policy factorization and closed-loop planner-executor co-optimization to improve locomotion stability and gait coordination in simulation.
tldr_zh: H^2MARL 提出了一个用于人形机器人全身控制的分层异构多智能体强化学习框架，通过关节级物理异质性感知策略分解和闭环规划器-执行器协同优化，在仿真中提升了运动稳定性和步态协调性。

title: Beyond Infraction Scores: Failure-Boundary Profiles for Closed-Loop Evaluation of Driving and Robot Navigation Agents
summary: Closed-loop driving benchmarks in CARLA rank agents by a driving score that multiplies route completion by an infraction penalty. This score does not distinguish an agent that stops in front of an obstacle from one that pushes past it. In a corridor closed by two parked cars, for example, one agent that drives through with contact averages 52.2 on the blocked widths, while the agents that stop average between 37.8 and 40.6. We propose failure-boundary profiles, an evaluation in which each scenario family varies one measured factor, such as corridor width or the time gap in oncoming traffic, and each variant is certified from measurement as one where the agent should proceed or one where it should stop. Along this axis we estimate two curves per agent, commitment (the probability of attempting the passage) and competence (the probability of passing without contact), and locate where each crosses one half, with intervals that account for the simulator's run-to-run variance. The certified labels also give a summary metric, decision accuracy, which credits clean passes on passable variants and stops on blocked ones. We evaluate seven driving agents on seven CARLA families. The rule-based expert reaches a decision accuracy of 0.74 and TFv6, the highest-scoring learned agent, 0.60. Agents with similar driving scores fail in different ways, and agents that reliably stop at a blocked corridor still rarely wait for a gap in oncoming traffic. We also apply the method, unchanged, to a warehouse robot in Isaac Sim. The navigation policy we test stops at blocked gaps in only one of three families, and two fine-tuned versions of it pass more gaps cleanly but no longer stop at all.
summary_zh: 闭环驾驶基准测试在CARLA环境中通过驾驶评分对智能体进行排名，该评分将路线完成度乘以违规惩罚系数。这一评分无法区分停在障碍物前的智能体与强行穿越障碍物的智能体。例如，在由两辆停放车辆封闭的走廊场景中，一个带接触穿越的智能体在受阻宽度上的平均得分为52.2，而停车等待的智能体平均得分在37.8至40.6之间。我们提出故障边界剖面（failure-boundary profiles）评估方法：每个场景族中仅改变一个可测量因素，如走廊宽度或对向车流的时距，每个变体根据测量结果被判定为智能体应通行或应停车。沿此轴线，我们为每个智能体估计两条曲线——承诺度（尝试通行的概率）和胜任度（无接触通行的概率），并定位每条曲线跨越0.5的位置，同时给出考虑模拟器运行间方差的置信区间。经过认证的标签还提供了一项汇总指标——决策准确率，该指标对可通过变体中的干净通行和受阻变体中的停车操作分别计分。我们在七个CARLA场景族中评估了七个驾驶智能体。基于规则的专家智能体决策准确率达到0.74，而得分最高的学习型智能体TFv6为0.60。驾驶得分相近的智能体以不同方式失败，且能够可靠地在受阻走廊停车的智能体仍很少等待对向车流的间隙。我们还将该方法原封不动地应用于Isaac Sim中的仓库机器人。所测试的导航策略仅在三个场景族中的一个族中能在受阻间隙处停车，而该策略的两个微调版本虽然能更干净地通过更多间隙，却完全不再停车。
tldr: This paper proposes failure-boundary profiles, a new evaluation method for closed-loop driving and robot navigation agents that measures decision accuracy across scenario variants, and demonstrates it on CARLA driving agents and a warehouse robot in Isaac Sim.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于闭环驾驶和机器人导航智能体的评估方法——故障边界轮廓，通过在不同场景变体上测量决策准确度来评估智能体，并在CARLA驾驶智能体和Isaac Sim中的仓储机器人上进行了验证。

title: $A^3$-VLA: Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation
summary: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) enable robots to perform manipulation tasks by leveraging Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to process visual observations and language instructions. However, the action prediction objective itself lacks fine-grained task-specific perceptual supervision, making it prone to relying on task-irrelevant visual shortcuts, leading attention away from target objects and key interaction areas, thereby limiting its operational performance and generalization ability. To address this, we propose Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation ($A^3$-VLA), a framework that derives task-specific visual guidance from the manipulation process itself. Specifically, $A^3$-VLA first generates heuristic candidate regions for target objects and the robot from interaction-induced visual changes, and refines them with a visual segmentation model offline. These regions serve as explicit perceptual guidance through two complementary objectives: an attention allocation loss that encourages sufficient focus on task-critical regions when language or robot state tokens query the visual input, and a contrastive learning loss that aligns the representations of candidate target regions with language instructions while separating them from task-irrelevant regions. Extensive experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that $A^3$-VLA consistently improves multiple VLA backbones, with an average success rate gain of 6.5% - 25.2% across benchmarks.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作模型（VLAs）通过利用视觉-语言模型（VLMs）处理视觉观察和语言指令，使机器人能够执行操作任务。然而，动作预测目标本身缺乏细粒度的任务特定感知监督，导致其容易依赖与任务无关的视觉捷径，使注意力偏离目标物体和关键交互区域，从而限制了其操作性能和泛化能力。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种用于机器人操作的自动感知引导注意力对齐方法（$A^3$-VLA），该框架从操作过程本身提取任务特定的视觉引导。具体而言，$A^3$-VLA首先根据交互引起的视觉变化，为目标物体和机器人生成启发式候选区域，并通过离线视觉分割模型对其进行优化。这些区域通过两个互补目标作为显式感知引导：一个注意力分配损失，鼓励在语言或机器人状态标记查询视觉输入时，对任务关键区域给予充分关注；一个对比学习损失，将候选目标区域的表示与语言指令对齐，同时将其与任务无关区域分离。在模拟和真实世界操作任务上的大量实验表明，$A^3$-VLA一致性地提升了多种VLA骨干模型的性能，在多个基准上的平均成功率提升幅度为6.5%至25.2%。
tldr: A^3-VLA introduces an automatic perception-guided attention alignment framework that derives task-specific visual guidance from manipulation-induced changes, improving VLA policies via attention allocation and contrastive losses.
tldr_zh: A^3-VLA提出了一种自动感知引导的注意力对齐框架，从操作引起的视觉变化中获取任务特定的视觉指导，通过注意力分配和对比损失提升VLA策略。

title: CoSafe: Cooperative Runtime Safety Assurance for Mixed-Traffic Autonomous Driving
summary:
With the rapid development of autonomous driving systems (ADSes), real-world roads are evolving into mixed-traffic environments where autonomous vehicles (AVs) and other traffic participants (e.g., human-driven vehicles (HDVs), cyclists, and pedestrians) coexist and interact with each other. However, current ADSes still incur various safety violations in mixed traffic scenarios, raising a strong demand for runtime safety assurance frameworks that can continuously monitor hazards and prevent potential violations. Existing ego-centric assurance approaches are insufficient for mixed traffic, where violations often arise from locally reasonable yet jointly incompatible decisions among multiple vehicles and cannot be reliably resolved through independent takeover.
  To bridge this gap, we propose CoSafe, a modular and ADS-agnostic cooperative runtime safety assurance framework for mixed-traffic autonomous driving to extend runtime safety assurance from ego-centric takeover to scene-level cooperative intervention. CoSafe leverages vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication to enable roadside units (RSUs) to monitor scene-level hazards and jointly mitigate hazards involving multiple vehicles. We integrate CoSafe with seven state-of-the-art ADSes, and our evaluation on the InterDrive benchmark demonstrates that CoSafe improves the driving score of AVs by 70.03% on average, reduces safety violations by 87.80%, and accurately identifies unsafe AVs with an F3 score of 0.930, while satisfying real-time constraints.
summary_zh:
随着自动驾驶系统（ADSes）的快速发展，现实道路正逐渐演变为混合交通环境，其中自动驾驶车辆（AVs）与其他交通参与者（如人工驾驶车辆（HDVs）、骑行者及行人）共存并相互交互。然而，当前自动驾驶系统在混合交通场景下仍会出现各类安全违规问题，这催生了对运行时安全保证框架的强烈需求，该框架能够持续监测风险并预防潜在违规行为。现有的以自我为中心的安全保证方法在混合交通中难以奏效，因为此类场景中的违规通常源于多辆车之间局部合理但整体不相容的决策，且无法通过独立接管可靠地解决。

为弥补这一不足，我们提出了CoSafe，一个模块化的、与自动驾驶系统无关的混合交通自动驾驶协作式运行时安全保证框架，将运行时安全保证从以自我为中心的接管扩展至场景级协作干预。CoSafe利用车联万物（V2X）通信，使路侧单元（RSUs）能够监测场景级风险，并针对涉及多辆车的风险进行协同缓解。我们将CoSafe与七个最先进的自动驾驶系统集成，并在InterDrive基准上的评估表明，CoSafe将自动驾驶车辆的平均驾驶得分提升了70.03%，安全违规减少了87.80%，并以0.930的F3分数准确识别不安全的自动驾驶车辆，同时满足实时性约束。
tldr: CoSafe is a cooperative runtime safety assurance framework for mixed-traffic autonomous driving that uses V2X communication and roadside units to monitor scene-level hazards and coordinate interventions across multiple vehicles, improving driving scores by 70% and reducing safety violations by 88%.
tldr_zh: CoSafe 是一个针对混合交通自动驾驶的协作式运行时安全保障框架，利用 V2X 通信和路侧单元来监控场景级危险并协调多车辆干预，将驾驶评分提高 70%，安全违规减少 88%。

title: Can Astra Solve RoboMME without Breaking the Bank?
summary: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering information that is no longer visible, such as an object's location before occlusion or the order of a demonstrated action sequence. A large vision-language planner can read this history, but calling it before every action chunk is slow and costly. We present a three-tier system for the RoboMME benchmark. GPT-6 Astra (System 2) selects a grounded subtask from stored visual history, a $π_{0.5}$ vision-language-action policy (System 1) executes it, and a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B monitor (System 1.5) checks after each action chunk whether the subtask is finished. The instruction is kept until the monitor reports completion or a task-specific event occurs, while the policy keeps acting on new observations. On RoboMME, the system succeeds in 79.13% of episodes with an average of 3.63 Astra calls and 80.84 seconds per episode. This is 34.62 points above the best published non-oracle baseline and 4.95 points below GroundSG+Oracle, which gives the low-level policy ground-truth subgoals.
summary_zh: 机器人操作通常需要记住不再可见的信息，例如物体在被遮挡前的位置，或演示动作序列的顺序。大型视觉语言规划器可以读取这段历史记录，但在每个动作片段之前调用它会既慢又昂贵。我们为RoboMME基准测试提出了一个三层系统。GPT-6 Astra（系统2）从存储的视觉历史中选择一个基于基础子任务，一个$π_{0.5}$视觉-语言-动作策略（系统1）执行该子任务，一个微调的Qwen3-VL-4B监控器（系统1.5）在每个动作片段之后检查子任务是否完成。指令会一直保留，直到监控器报告完成或发生任务特定事件，而策略则持续基于新的观测执行操作。在RoboMME上，该系统在79.13%的情节中成功，平均每次情节调用3.63次Astra，耗时80.84秒。这比已发表的最佳非Oracle基线高出34.62个百分点，比给低层策略提供真实子目标的GroundSG+Oracle低4.95个百分点。
tldr: Introduces a three-tier system using GPT-6 Astra for subtask selection, a pi0.5 VLA policy for execution, and a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B monitor to reduce costly high-level planner calls on the RoboMME benchmark, achieving 79.13% success with fewer Astra calls.
tldr_zh: 提出一个三层系统，利用GPT-6 Astra进行子任务选择、pi0.5 VLA策略执行和微调Qwen3-VL-4B监控，以减少RoboMME基准中成本高昂的高层规划调用，实现79.13%的成功率并减少Astra调用。

title: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation
summary: Embodied video world models predict scene changes caused by robot actions, yet generated object responses may remain inconsistent with task intent and contact dynamics. Critical responses in embodied scenes often concentrate in local regions and specific time intervals. Inspired by chain-of-thought reasoning, we introduce ReactWorld, an embodied video generation model guided by structured interaction anticipation. In the generation backbone's feature space, an interaction response field predictor anticipates how the interaction will unfold, explicitly describing participant roles, future motion response intensity, and local motion changes. A response feedback adapter forms increments to object features from the difference between the object branch's outputs with predicted and zeroed local dynamics inputs. It also converts predicted displacements into positional biases for temporal attention. These two mechanisms guide object feature updates and information retrieval across frames, respectively. Through interaction anticipation and generative feedback, ReactWorld achieves an average score of 77.51 on RBench, outperforming PhysisForcing by 3.29 points with improvements in all nine categories. On EZS-Bench, it achieves a Domain score of 86.98 and an average score of 81.87.
summary_zh: 具身视频世界模型预测由机器人动作引起的场景变化，然而生成的对象响应可能仍与任务意图和接触动力学不一致。具身场景中的关键响应通常集中在局部区域和特定时间区间。受思维链推理的启发，我们引入了ReactWorld，一种由结构化交互预期引导的具身视频生成模型。在生成主干网络的特征空间中，交互响应场预测器预测交互将如何展开，显式描述参与者角色、未来运动响应强度及局部运动变化。响应反馈适配器通过对象分支在预测与置零局部动力学输入下的输出差异，形成对象特征的增量，并将预测位移转化为时间注意力的位置偏置。这两种机制分别引导对象特征更新和跨帧信息检索。通过交互预期与生成反馈，ReactWorld在RBench上平均得分为77.51，相比PhysisForcing提升3.29分，且在全部九个类别上均有改进。在EZS-Bench上，其Domain得分为86.98，平均得分为81.87。
tldr: ReactWorld introduces a structured interaction anticipation mechanism for embodied video generation, predicting response fields and using feedback adapters to generate action-consistent videos, achieving state-of-the-art results on RBench and EZS-Bench.
tldr_zh: ReactWorld 提出了一种结构化交互预期机制，用于具身视频生成，通过预测响应场和使用反馈适配器生成与行动一致的视频，在 RBench 和 EZS-Bench 上取得了领先结果。

title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.
summary_zh: 操控多指灵巧手操作多样物体由于高维度和复杂动力学特性而具有挑战性。人-物交互（HOI）数据集提供了关于任务信息和具身交互的丰富知识。我们的方法并非仅仅模仿人类演示，而是利用这些数据集学习整体预测未来的手-物状态。物体未来状态的预测可以作为强化学习的通用奖励项，减少对特定任务奖励工程设计的依赖，并增强跨任务的泛化能力。我们在仿真和现实世界中针对三个操作任务开展了大量实验。我们的方法在新颖物体的成功率和泛化性方面均优于现有最先进（SOTA）方法。此外，我们通过成功地将技能部署到不同的机器人手上，验证了所提方法的跨具身兼容性。
tldr: This paper presents a method that learns object-centric motion priors from human-object interaction data and uses them as a general reward term for reinforcement learning, improving success rates and generalization in dexterous manipulation across multiple robot hands.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种从人-物交互数据中学习以物体为中心的运动先验，并将其用作强化学习的通用奖励项，从而提升多指灵巧操作的成功率和对新物体的泛化能力，并验证了跨本体部署的兼容性。

title: WayPOP: A Panoramic Open-Set Panoptic Tracking Benchmark
summary: Holistic perception for autonomous agents requires reliably segmenting and associating scene elements across time and camera views, including objects outside a fixed semantic taxonomy. Existing open-set panoptic benchmarks focus on individual images or views, while panoramic tracking benchmarks assume closed-set taxonomies. Consequently, these benchmarks do not evaluate whether unknown objects can be consistently segmented and tracked across synchronized multi-camera sequences. We introduce WayPOP, a panoramic open-set panoptic tracking benchmark built on real Waymo PVPS sequences augmented with diverse out-of-taxonomy 3D assets from Objaverse. Inserted objects are placed at fixed locations in the 3D scene and rendered using calibrated vehicle-mounted cameras as the ego vehicle and surrounding traffic move, providing temporally and cross-view consistent panoptic annotations and auxiliary LiDAR range observations. WayPOP contains approximately 670 curated assets instantiated as 980 unique unknown-object tracks, yielding 53,452 unknown-object mask annotations across 21,300 camera images. Our evaluation protocol defines a hierarchy of tasks from view-independent open-set panoptic segmentation to full panoramic open-set panoptic tracking, using known/unknown PQ and (w)STQ metrics. We benchmark representative open-set and open-vocabulary segmentation methods with temporal and cross-camera association. Our results reveal substantial limitations of current methods in truly open-set scenarios, highlighting robust unknown-object localization and identity association across time and views as major open challenges.
summary_zh: 全景感知要求自主智能体能够跨时间和相机视角可靠地分割并关联场景元素，包括超出固定语义分类体系的对象。现有的开放集全景分割基准仅关注单张图像或单一视角，而全景跟踪基准则假设封闭集分类体系。因此，这些基准无法评估未知对象能否在同步多相机序列中被一致地分割和跟踪。我们提出WayPOP，一个基于真实Waymo PVPS序列构建的全景开放集跟踪基准，并通过Objaverse中多样化的分类体系外3D资产进行增强。插入的对象被放置在3D场景中的固定位置，并利用标定过的车载相机在自车和周围交通移动时进行渲染，从而提供时间一致且跨视角一致的全景标注以及辅助的LiDAR距离观测。WayPOP包含约670个精选资产，实例化为980条独特的未知对象轨迹，在21,300张相机图像中生成53,452个未知对象掩膜标注。我们的评估协议定义了从视角无关的开放集全景分割到完整的全景开放集全景跟踪的任务层级，并使用已知/未知PQ和(w)STQ指标进行评估。我们对具有时间和跨相机关联能力的代表性开放集和开放词汇分割方法进行了基准测试。结果表明，当前方法在真正开放集场景中存在显著局限性，凸显了跨时间和跨视角的稳健未知对象定位与身份关联是主要开放挑战。
tldr: WayPOP introduces a panoramic open-set panoptic tracking benchmark built on Waymo PVPS sequences with inserted out-of-taxonomy 3D assets, enabling evaluation of unknown-object segmentation and association across multi-camera, multi-frame driving scenes.
tldr_zh: WayPOP 提出了一个基于 Waymo PVPS 序列的全景开放集全景跟踪基准，通过插入分类学之外的 3D 资产，评估未知物体在多相机、多帧驾驶场景中的分割与关联能力。

title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting
summary: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. We propose GRASP (Gradient Recovery from Archived Samples for Proposals), which combines sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement without requiring a differentiable simulator. GRASP-TO extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo by fitting local quadratic cost models to archived rollouts and using their gradients to guide Markov chain Monte Carlo rejuvenation. Metropolis-Hastings correction preserves the target distribution for each fixed proposal kernel, and a population analysis connects the recovered gradients to Gaussian smoothing. GRASP-MPC scales this optimizer to long demonstrations through warm-started receding-horizon planning. Experiments on dexterous hands and humanoids show accurate retargeting with a shared tracking objective and no task-specific contact rewards, including 92.8% success on 1352 bimanual OakInk2 demonstrations. The refined references improve PPO tracking in pen spinning and humanoid-object interaction. We also demonstrate dexterous manipulation and whole-body humanoid motion on real hardware.
summary_zh: 我们研究基于物理的人体示范重定向用于机器人学习：即在接触动力学条件下寻找能够再现参考运动的机器人控制策略。我们提出GRASP（从存档样本中恢复梯度以生成提议），该方法结合了基于采样的探索与梯度引导的精炼，且无需可微仿真器。GRASP-TO扩展了温和序贯蒙特卡洛方法，通过对存档的 rollout 拟合局部二次代价模型，并利用其梯度引导马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛更新。Metropolis-Hastings校正保持了每个固定提议核的目标分布，而种群分析则将恢复的梯度与高斯平滑联系起来。GRASP-MPC通过暖启动的滚动时域规划将该优化器扩展到长时程示范。在灵巧手和人形机器人上的实验表明，在共享跟踪目标且无需任务特定接触奖励的条件下，重定向具有较高准确性，包括在1352个双臂OakInk2示范中达到92.8%的成功率。精炼后的参考轨迹提升了PPO在转笔和人形物体交互任务中的跟踪性能。我们还展示了在真实硬件上的灵巧操作和全身人形运动。
tldr: GRASP introduces a sampling-based optimizer with gradient-guided refinement for physics-based motion retargeting, achieving accurate robot control from human demonstrations without differentiable simulators, and validated on dexterous hands and humanoids in simulation and real hardware.
tldr_zh: GRASP 提出了一种基于采样的优化器，结合梯度引导的细化，用于基于物理的运动重定向，在无需可微分模拟器的情况下，从人类演示中实现精确的机器人控制，并在灵巧手和人形机器人的仿真及真实硬件上得到验证。

title: Correct Robots Before They Make Mistakes: Proactive Human-in-the-Loop Intervention via Preference Learning
summary: This paper presents Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL), a framework for proactive policy correction and preference-based post-training. PHIL enables operators to preview policy-predicted future motion and intervene before anticipated undesirable actions. During takeover, PHIL continues querying the policy and displaying its predicted trajectories in the physical workspace through an extended reality (XR) interface. PHIL pairs rejected policy predictions with corrective action chunks subsequently executed from the same physical state over the same horizon, and preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these corrections. This paper evaluates PHIL on four real-world manipulation tasks using a diffusion policy and a pretrained vision-language-action policy. With five correction episodes per condition, PHIL increases mean success rates across the evaluated tasks and demonstration budgets from 44.0% to 70.3% for the diffusion policy and from 57.8% to 76.9% for X-VLA, compared with HG-DAgger. Separately, policies trained with proactive corrections show fewer unnecessary recovery behaviors in successful episodes. Project page: https://intuitive-robots.github.io/PHIL-page/.
summary_zh: 本文介绍了“人机协同前瞻干预”（Proactive Human-in-the-Loop, PHIL）框架，该框架用于策略的前瞻性修正及基于偏好的后训练。PHIL使操作员能够预览策略预测的未来运动，并在预期的不良行为发生之前进行干预。在接管过程中，PHIL持续查询策略，并通过扩展现实（XR）界面在物理工作空间中显示其预测轨迹。PHIL将被拒绝的策略预测与随后从相同物理状态、在相同时间跨度内执行的修正动作片段配对，并利用基于偏好的后训练促进策略倾向于采纳这些修正。本文在四个真实世界的机器人操作任务中，使用扩散策略和预训练的视觉-语言-动作策略对PHIL进行了评估。在每种条件下仅提供五次修正演示时，与HG-DAgger相比，PHIL将扩散策略在评估任务和示范预算下的平均成功率从44.0%提升至70.3%，将X-VLA的平均成功率从57.8%提升至76.9%。此外，采用前瞻性修正训练的策略在成功操作片段中展现出更少的多余恢复行为。项目页面：https://intuitive-robots.github.io/PHIL-page/。
tldr: This paper introduces PHIL, a proactive human-in-the-loop framework that lets operators preview and correct robot policy predictions before errors occur, using preference learning on paired rejected/corrected trajectories to improve policy performance in real-world manipulation tasks.
tldr_zh: 本文提出PHIL，一种主动式人在回路框架，允许操作员在错误发生前预览并纠正机器人策略预测，通过偏好学习对成对的拒绝/纠正轨迹进行训练，以提升真实世界操作任务的性能。

title: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain
summary: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. Effectiveness is demonstrated using nonlinear programming to plan motions on various terrain topologies. We also explore dynamic trajectory generation by embedding high-level requirements in the cost function and the initial guess. Preliminary feasibility tests were conducted over non-coplanar terrains, both in simulation and on the real robot ErgoCub.
summary_zh: 本文提出了一种轨迹规划器，用于人形机器人在复杂、可参数化地形上执行动态运动，该规划器基于接触隐式全身优化框架。该规划器无需预设接触序列即可生成可行运动，同时充分考虑机器人的完整动力学与运动学特性。为了在台阶、坡道及其他地形上规划双足运动，我们提出了一种数学模型，用光滑曲面近似地面几何形状。机器人与地面之间的刚性相互作用通过新型接触约束进行建模，从而将应用范围从平坦水平面扩展至任意光滑曲面。我们利用非线性规划在不同地形拓扑上规划运动，验证了该方法的有效性。此外，我们还通过在代价函数和初始猜测中嵌入高层需求，探索了动态轨迹生成。初步可行性测试已在非共面地形上进行，包括仿真验证及真实机器人ErgoCub上的实验。
tldr: This paper presents a contact-implicit whole-body trajectory optimization framework for humanoid robot locomotion on parameterizable uneven terrain, generating dynamic motions without predefined contact sequences and validating on the real ErgoCub robot.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于仿人机器人在可参数化不平坦地形上行走的接触隐式全身轨迹优化框架，无需预定义接触序列即可生成动态运动，并在真实ErgoCub机器人上进行了验证。

title: ELA: End-to-End Latent Action Policy Learning from Video Demonstrations
summary: Robot imitation learning is limited by the scarcity of action-labeled data, while action-free demonstrations such as videos are abundant. Recent latent-action methods learn action-relevant representations from observation transitions, but they do not optimize latent actions for downstream control, leading to latent representations that are difficult for policies to model and difficult to accurately decode into continuous robot actions. This paper introduces ELA, an end-to-end framework for learning from video demonstrations via latent actions jointly optimized for policy learning and action decoding. ELA jointly trains a latent action model, latent action policy, and action decoder, enabling policies to leverage abundant video data with only a handful of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show that ELA consistently outperforms prior latent action baselines. Moreover, it integrates seamlessly with existing imitation learning methods through lightweight 4M-parameter action decoders, requiring no changes to policy architectures or training objectives. Additional materials can be found on: https://end2end-latent-action.github.io/
summary_zh: 机器人模仿学习受限于动作标签数据的稀缺性，而无动作标注的演示数据（如视频）则十分丰富。近年来提出的潜在动作方法从观测转移中学习与动作相关的表征，但并未针对下游控制优化潜在动作，导致学习到的潜在表征难以被策略建模，且难以准确解码为连续的机器人动作。本文提出ELA，一种端到端框架，通过联合优化策略学习与动作解码的潜在动作，从视频演示中进行学习。ELA联合训练潜在动作模型、潜在动作策略和动作解码器，使策略能够利用丰富的视频数据，仅需少量带动作标签的机器人演示即可实现高效学习。在仿真和真实世界操作任务上的实验表明，ELA持续优于以往的潜在动作基线方法。此外，ELA通过轻量化的4M参数动作解码器即可无缝集成到现有模仿学习方法中，无需改变策略架构或训练目标。更多材料请参见：https://end2end-latent-action.github.io/
tldr: ELA is an end-to-end framework that jointly trains a latent action model, policy, and action decoder to learn from video demonstrations, enabling efficient policy learning with minimal action-labeled data for manipulation tasks in simulation and real world.
tldr_zh: ELA是一个端到端框架，联合训练潜在动作模型、策略和动作解码器，从视频演示中学习，只需少量带动作标签的机器人数据即可实现高效操作策略学习，并在仿真和真实世界任务中取得优异表现。

title: MESA: An Evaluation Framework for Compositional, Semantic, and Spatial Generalization in Robotics
summary: Despite growing interest in foundation models for robotic manipulation, systematic evaluation of their capabilities remains elusive. Existing benchmarks are either narrow and saturated, offering little signal on SOTA methods, broadly scoped, providing diversity at the cost of controlled experimentation, or require training on large, messy open-source datasets. We introduce MESA, an evaluation framework designed for precise, reproducible measurement of language-conditioned policy generalization. MESA provides five evaluation suites that isolate in-distribution performance and four distinct axes of generalization: spatial configuration, object instance, object category, and subtask composition, enabling researchers to diagnose where and why policies fail, not just whether they fail. To populate these suites at scale, we develop MESA-Gen, a pipeline for task and demonstration generation built by improving MimicGen. We instantiate the framework on two platforms and release both: the single-arm MESA suite, and BiMESA, the first large-scale benchmark for bimanual generalization. We evaluate seven baseline methods spanning diffusion policies, VLM-based approaches, and pretrained VLAs, finding that the strongest model achieves only 52% on MESA and 49% on BiMESA, providing meaningful signal while leaving ample room for progress. MESA rankings are broadly consistent with RoboArena scores, suggesting that MESA captures method-level differences relevant beyond simulation. Project website: https://pairlab.github.io/MESA.
summary_zh: 尽管机器人操作领域的基础模型日益受到关注，但对其能力的系统评估仍然难以实现。现有基准要么范围狭窄且已趋饱和，无法为当前最先进方法提供有效信号；要么范围宽泛，以牺牲受控实验为代价换取多样性；要么需要在大规模、杂乱的开源数据集上进行训练。我们提出MESA，一个旨在精确、可复现地度量语言条件策略泛化能力的评估框架。MESA提供五个评估套件，分别隔离分布内性能与四个不同的泛化维度：空间布局、物体实例、物体类别和子任务组合，使研究者不仅能够判断策略是否失败，还能诊断其在何处以及为何失败。为了规模化构建这些套件，我们开发了MESA-Gen，一个基于对MimicGen改进的任务与演示生成流水线。我们在两个平台上实例化该框架并同时发布：单臂MESA套件，以及BiMESA——首个大规模双臂泛化基准。我们评估了涵盖扩散策略、基于视觉语言模型的方法和预训练视觉-语言-动作模型的七种基线方法，发现最强的模型在MESA上仅达到52%的准确率，在BiMESA上为49%，这提供了有意义的区分信号，同时为未来进展留下了充足空间。MESA的排名与RoboArena分数总体一致，表明MESA能够捕获超越仿真环境、与真实场景相关的方法级差异。项目网站：https://pairlab.github.io/MESA。
tldr: MESA is an evaluation framework for language-conditioned robotic manipulation, isolating in-distribution performance and four axes of generalization (spatial, instance, category, composition), with a scalable generation pipeline and benchmarks for single-arm and bimanual policies.
tldr_zh: MESA 是一个用于语言条件机器人操作评估的框架，旨在隔离分布内性能和四种泛化轴，并提供可扩展的生成流程以及单臂和双臂基准。

title: Ctrl-F: Force as an Interface for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Humanoid motion tracking has scaled to general policies that reproduce diverse human motion, but the resulting behavior is in free-space: the tracker knows where the body should be, not how it should interact with the environment. Other work makes the object part of the objective, yet abstracts that interaction to contact or geometry, which leaves the demanding cases under-explored. We argue that force is a natural command channel between motion imitation and object interaction, one that specifies not just where to make contact but how hard. We present Ctrl-F, a hierarchical motion-force framework that augments motion tracking with an explicit force command, a 3-D force at each designated contact body such as a hand or a foot. The hierarchical framework comprises: (1) A unified motion-force controller tracks the reference motion while applying the commanded force to the world. (2) A high-level force planner that issues a force command online based on object state and proprioception observations. In simulation and on hardware, Ctrl-F completes loco-manipulation that demands large, sustained interaction force and adjusts its command online as the load changes, both out of reach of a force-blind tracker. On hardware, Ctrl-F demonstrates hand-based dragging, pushing, and lifting, as well as foot-based kicking, successfully manipulating boxes weighing up to 20kg in pushing and kicking tasks where the force-blind baseline fails, while adapting online to additional loads introduced mid-task.
summary_zh: 人体运动追踪已扩展到能够再现多样化人体运动的通用策略，然而由此产生的行为仅限于自由空间中：追踪器知道身体应处于何处，却不知道身体应如何与环境交互。其他研究将物体纳入目标函数，但将这种交互抽象为接触或几何关系，从而对要求苛刻的案例探索不足。我们认为，力是运动模仿与物体交互之间的自然命令通道，它不仅指定接触的位置，还指定接触的力度。我们提出了Ctrl-F，一个层级式运动-力框架，通过显式的力命令（在指定接触体如手或脚上的三维力）增强运动追踪。该层级框架包括：(1) 一个统一的运动-力控制器，在向世界施加命令力的同时追踪参考运动；(2) 一个高层力规划器，基于物体状态和本体感觉观测在线发出力命令。在仿真和硬件实验中，Ctrl-F完成了需要大幅持续交互力的腿臂操控任务，并根据负载变化在线调整其命令，而这些均超出了无视力的追踪器的能力范围。在硬件上，Ctrl-F展示了基于手的拖拽、推动和提举，以及基于脚的踢动，成功操控了重达20公斤的箱子，在推动和踢动任务中，无视力的基线方法失败，而Ctrl-F同时还能在线适应任务中途引入的额外负载。
tldr: Ctrl-F introduces a hierarchical motion-force framework that augments humanoid motion tracking with explicit 3-D force commands, enabling loco-manipulation tasks requiring sustained interaction force, such as pushing and kicking heavy boxes, both in simulation and on hardware.
tldr_zh: Ctrl-F 提出了一种分层运动-力控制框架，将人形运动跟踪与显式 3D 力命令相结合，从而在仿真和硬件上实现需要持续交互力的定位操作任务，例如推动和踢重箱子。

title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
summary: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.
summary_zh: 从视频中学习通用的动作表征，需要对不同执行方式下保持一致、同时不受具身形态和外观变化影响的动力学进行建模。现有的潜在动作模型从视觉转换中推断动作，但其表征往往将底层动作与无关的视觉变化纠缠在一起，限制了跨具身形态的迁移能力。我们提出了DreamX，将预训练的视频扩散模型重新用作通用潜在动作学习器。我们的方法从视频模型丰富的时空特征中提取紧凑的潜在动作，将每个潜在视频帧压缩$\boldsymbol{300}$倍（$\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$个令牌）。此外，通过利用视频模型的生成先验，这些潜在动作能够捕获与动作相关、且与视觉外观解耦的动力学信息。由此产生的潜在空间可作为跨具身形态（人类和机器人）、环境和动作参数化的共享动作接口。在LARY-Bench上，DreamX在潜在动作模型中达到了最先进的性能。此外，在一种设置下编码的动作在另一种设置中仍然有效：该潜在空间支持任意到任意的视频迁移以及跨不同具身形态和环境的零样本动作迁移。更进一步，这一共享接口还能在紧凑的潜在动作空间中实现策略学习，从而降低基于视频扩散的策略的计算成本。
tldr: DreamX repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner, extracting compact, appearance-invariant action representations that support cross-embodiment transfer and policy learning.
tldr_zh: DreamX 将预训练的视频扩散模型重新用作通用潜在动作学习器，提取紧凑且外观不变的动作表示，支持跨实体迁移和策略学习。

title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning
summary: Inverse kinematics (IK) converts end-effector pose commands into joint motion, and many vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely on it to act on a given arm and to transfer across embodiments. Precise IK remains laborious: redundancy and singularities complicate the inverse mapping, execution depends on hand-tuned controllers, and training data on physical robots are costly to collect. We present PolicyIK, a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy for high-precision IK. It updates joint-position references from pose feedback and observes its accumulated reference relative to the measured joints, so it can retain the offset that the position controller needs at rest. Two-scale pose errors with an error-dependent action gain resolve millimeter residuals while preserving large motions. Progress and dwell rewards teach it to both reach the tolerance and stay within it. In simulation, a single attempt by the trained PPO policy keeps the mean errors over the final second within 1 mm and 0.2° on 93.5% of held-out tasks, and a deployment protocol raises success to 98.9%. When trained directly on a physical arm with an off-policy RL learner, PolicyIK achieves higher reaching and holding success than all four classical IK controllers under the same time budgets. In simulated pick-and-place, PolicyIK executes the end-effector commands of the $π_{0.5}$ VLA policy with 95.7% success. These results show that reinforcement learning can provide high-precision inverse kinematics for robot arms. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/PolicyIK.
summary_zh: 逆向运动学（IK）将末端执行器的位姿指令转换为关节运动，许多视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略依赖它来操作给定的机械臂并跨实体迁移。精确的IK仍然费时费力：冗余和奇异性使逆映射复杂化，执行依赖手工调参的控制器，且物理机器人上的训练数据采集成本高昂。我们提出PolicyIK，一种用于高精度IK的目标条件强化学习策略。它根据位姿反馈更新关节位置参考值，并观测其累积参考值相对于测量关节的位置，从而能够在静止时保留位置控制器所需的偏移量。双尺度位姿误差结合误差相关的动作增益，在保留大范围运动的同时解决了毫米级残差问题。进度奖励与驻留奖励引导策略同时实现到达公差带并保持在公差带内。在仿真中，训练后的PPO策略单次尝试即可在93.5%的留出任务上使最后一秒内的平均误差保持在1 mm和0.2°以内，部署协议可将成功率提升至98.9%。当直接使用离策略强化学习算法在物理机械臂上训练时，在相同时间预算下，PolicyIK的到达与保持成功率均高于四种经典IK控制器。在仿真抓取-放置任务中，PolicyIK以95.7%的成功率执行$π_{0.5}$ VLA策略的末端执行器指令。这些结果表明，强化学习能够为机械臂提供高精度逆向运动学。代码见https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/PolicyIK。
tldr: PolicyIK presents a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy for high-precision inverse kinematics of robot arms, achieving sub-millimeter accuracy in simulation and on physical hardware, and improving the execution of VLA policy commands.
tldr_zh: PolicyIK 提出了一种基于目标条件强化学习的高精度机械臂逆运动学策略，在仿真和真实硬件上实现了亚毫米精度，并改善了 VLA 策略命令的执行。

title: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Imitation Learning
summary: Imitation learning policies in robotics are trained on datasets collected through costly real-world teleoperation. Often, the data-collection process is unguided, relying on the teleoperator's intuition, resulting in data that contributes little to overall policy performance. Recent work has shown that curating such unguided datasets can substantially improve policy performance, but these approaches operate by filtering existing datasets after collection and therefore do not prevent the acquisition of uninformative data. In this work, we propose GUILD, a novel Guided Data Collection (GDC) method that actively reasons about which data should be collected to maximize downstream policy performance.
