VIPBench enables the evaluation of speaker models against human perception on real, cloned, and morphed speech, and our results motivate training speaker models directly on listener judgments.

title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
summary: What should ``verified'' mean when evaluating LLM-generated code? Many existing pipelines report a single verification number. We argue this collapses three distinct properties measured in a conditional audit sequence: verifier acceptance (Surface A), \emph{syntactic specification binding (Surface B: does the proof obligation bind to the spec?), and \emph{semantic specification fidelity} (Surface C: does the spec capture the informal requirement?). Two empirical demonstrations show the surfaces separate. \textbf{First ($A \neq B$), via Li@Opus (a same-model reproduction of \citet{li2025dafny}'s Dafny-as-intermediate-representation (IR) pipeline under Claude Opus 4.7) on three Python benchmarks}: it reaches \textbf{99.1\% verifier acceptance} on HumanEval while only \textbf{1.9\%} carry a certificate binding to a spec-defined predicate or function. \textbf{Second ($B \neq C$), via VCG on two Rust benchmarks}: we use VCG (which is our own in-house Dafny-as-intermediate pipeline) on Rust because the Rust target lets us enforce fully-verifiable output (every component ships as a Dafny certificate, ensures-binding gate passing by construction). Even inside that construction, \textbf{11.48\% (MBPP-Rust) and 14.82\% (VeriContest LC slice) of structurally-verified samples still fail hidden tests}. On the LC slice of VeriContest, \textbf{VCG's reported End2End rate is 7.79\% (535/6870).} The cited external rates are 5.51\% (GPT-5.5) and 1.88\% (single-shot Opus 4.7). These give descriptive differences of 2.3 percentage points and 4.14$\times$, respectively; task-budget, repair and harness differences prevent a matched-performance claim.

title: Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency: Test-Time Reasoning with Imperfect Generators and Verifiers
summary:
Large language models can solve many multi-step reasoning problems, but their reasoning remains brittle: plausible intermediate steps often lead to incorrect answers. Improving reasoning at test time requires balancing two imperfect signals: the generator, which provides diversity, and the verifier, which guides correctness. Existing approaches largely favor one side of this tradeoff. Verifier-weighted voting relies on trajectories sampled from the generator and cannot steer generation toward correct ones. By contrast, beam-style verifier-guided search can steer generation, but may over-concentrate on narrow trajectory sets and amplify verifier errors.
  We propose Verifier-Guided Self-Consistency (VGSC), a stochastic decoding framework that combines step-level correctness and future-outcome estimates to guide reasoning during generation. VGSC repeatedly proposes candidate next steps from the base language model and uses both signals in an acceptance/resampling procedure, while maintaining multiple trajectories for final answer-level self-consistency. We provide a probabilistic interpretation of VGSC as approximate sampling from a verifier-tilted trajectory distribution. Across multiple reasoning benchmarks, generator models, and verifier families, VGSC achieves higher average accuracy than representative baselines.

title: ViBench 2.0: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Software Building
summary: On Replit, our agentic engineering platform, users now build entire products without writing code, through successive feature requests to an agent. Yet existing coding benchmarks evaluate single, fully specified tasks, and many are near saturation. We introduce ViBench 2.0, a benchmark for long-horizon software building that we use to select our platform's models. Its 17 full-stack web products, modeled on widely used software, grow over 241 feature requests and are judged only when finished, as a user would judge them: a browser agent runs 544 test plans, and a build passes only if every plan does, under a grading protocol validated to keep this strict score reliable. Evaluating nine models, we find a reliability gap: the three strongest pass up to 98% of test plans yet deliver a fully working product in at most 65% of builds, and no open-weight model delivers one. The gap is closing fast: across three releases of one model family, pass@1 on the public products rises from 3% to 53% while the cost per build falls by more than half. We release eight products with the harness and grader, hold out nine, and report lessons from production use.

title: VirtualTrialHarness: Coordinating Agentic Operationalization of Virtual Trial Protocols Across Complex Clinical Schemas
summary: Virtual trials use routinely collected clinical data to evaluate treatment strategies, but translating a study protocol into an executable analysis requires determining how clinical concepts and study requirements should be represented in the available data and applied consistently across the workflow. These decisions depend on local data representations and operational conventions and can involve source selection, patient and encounter identity, linkage, and temporal interpretation. Here we introduce VirtualTrialHarness (VTHarness), an agent framework that coordinates virtual-trial operationalization by selecting reusable procedural skills for each workflow stage and uses explicit contracts to maintain consistent study decisions across stages. We also introduce VTBenchmark for evaluating source selection and cohort construction. Across three complex synthetic environments, VTHarness successfully produced all required cohort outputs matching the references in 95.1% of workflows after requirement clarification, compared with 60.4% using retrieval from the same procedural corpus. Procedural skills improved source recovery across three language models and increased source overlap with analyst code in 13 Mayo Clinic cases. Site-specific adaptation enabled reference-matched cohort execution across eight MIMIC-IV tasks. Within the Mayo Clinic Virtual Trials Program, the framework supported investigator review of cohort construction and endpoint analysis. These findings support coordinating procedural guidance with workflow decisions to improve virtual-trial implementation across complex clinical schemas.

title: Vision Paper: Why Distributed LLM Post-Training and Decentralized Alignment Are Now Essential
summary: This vision paper argues that distributed learning, including federated and decentralized, should become a first-class paradigm in LLM post-training, not merely a privacy add-on. Current methods like RLHF and DPO rest on an invisible assumption: preference data should be centralized. We contend this assumption is scientifically unjustified, practically unsustainable, and ethically problematic. As LLMs deploy into healthcare, law, finance, and multilingual communities, preference data originates from populations that cannot or will not centralize. We develop a three-pillar argument grounded in (1) privacy and data sovereignty, (2) pluralism and representational equity, and (3) robustness and scalability. We formalize key technical challenges unique to this intersection, reference drift, preference heterogeneity, and the DP-utility trade-off for contrastive losses, and propose concrete algorithmic directions, and sketch a research agenda. Our analysis shows distributed post-training is not only necessary but tractable, and ignoring it risks AI that is legally noncompliant, representationally narrow, and brittle at scale.

title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
summary: Machine learning models in radiotherapy are commissioned by testing them on cases with known answers, which may not reveal a shortcut that the test cases share with the training data. Frontier language models have recently been reported to read and write the raw weights of small neural networks, an ability called weight-space programming. The purpose of this study was to determine whether such a model, given only a clinical protocol and a network's weights, can audit and repair the network. Networks with 433 to 4,801 parameters were trained to screen head-and-neck planning requests against four rules. Flaws were planted through the training data: confounds that hid each rule, a 3 Gy shift in the cord threshold, and a hidden trigger. Claude Opus 5.5 audited each network blind, without tools, data or code execution, and every claim and repair was tested on about 420,000 requests. The language model named the broken rule in 16 of 18 flawed networks (95% CI 67% to 97%), including all 15 with a confound or a threshold shift. It repaired each of the 16 by changing a median of 3 parameters. Fine-tuning on protocol-labeled requests also repaired every network, but changed nearly every parameter. Each confound and shift it found was visible in single units, and a simple statistic chosen for each flaw type found the same flaws. It cleared 2 of 5 healthy networks without being forced and found 1 of 3 triggers. Testing against the protocol detected every flaw, and black-box testing found the confounds and the shift faster. The results indicate that, in small networks, weight-space programming can locate and repair flaws that silence an input or shift a threshold, but cannot yet certify that a network is correct.

title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
summary: While multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning (RL) excels on long-horizon tasks, its performance gains remain highly sensitive to interaction constraints. Evaluating across sampling breadth $K$ and interaction depth $T$ via $Pass@(K,T)$, we show that trajectory-level RL advantages depend on sufficient turn budgets, diminishing significantly when budgets tighten. Besides, agentic RL does not uniformly elevate single-step decision quality; rather, its strength concentrates in error recovery and long-horizon resilience. To mitigate the deployment risks caused by this budget dependence, we provide a preliminary discussion on the benefits and limitations of process supervision signals and introduce BudgetMix RL as an alternative that varies interaction budgets during training. Experiments demonstrate that BudgetMix RL achieves robust performance across diverse execution settings. Project Page: https://rethinking-agentic-rl.github.io/

title: When Are Two SAE Latents the Same Feature?
summary: Comparing sparse autoencoders (SAEs) requires connecting feature correspondence, differences between whole dictionaries, and uncertainty from finite evaluation data. We develop a framework that connects these tasks through an energy-weighted optimal-transport plan under a specified similarity geometry. The same plan defines a dictionary-level discrepancy, decomposes it into latent contributions, and quantifies how each latent's mass is distributed across counterparts. We characterize relationships between decoder, activation, and first-order causal similarities; idealized models clarify the interpretation of splitting and absorption. For fixed trained SAEs, we derive joint asymptotic inference for transport costs and fractions, accounting for activation similarities and both energy marginals estimated from the same documents. A joint document bootstrap gives asymptotically valid simultaneous confidence bands. Experiments across four language models locate cross-seed discrepancy and separate context-dependent changes.

title: When Does Risk-Controlled Throughput Forecasting Actually Control Risk? A Reproduction Study on LEO Satellite Link
summary: Risk-budgeted throughput forecasting converts a point forecast of LEO satellite capacity into a conservative bound whose overestimation rate is held at a user-specified budget, so that admission control can act on it safely. We reproduce the state of the art, BG-CFQS, on the three Starlink traces its authors used and on an independent fourth dataset, and report four findings. First, its risk guarantee is reproducible but conditional on the calibration split: under a random split we recover every published quantity, including risk-pass on 3 of 3 datasets, but under a contiguous temporal split, which is what a deployed terminal faces, it holds on 1 of 3. Second, independent of any split, the method cannot serve a risk budget below 0.15, the low end of its candidate quantile set. On all four datasets the achieved rate is identical at budgets of 0.05, 0.10 and 0.15, overshooting by 1.4x to 3.7x at the tightest. Third, static conformal calibration cannot improve a ranking, only shift an operating point; we confirm this exactly on latency spike detection, where online calibration improves AUPRC by up to 51%. Fourth, group-conditional online recalibration splits into two mechanisms. The online part replicates: it tracks the budget within 1% from 0.05 to 0.35, where static calibration is 16 to 21% off. The group-conditional part does not: on three of four datasets, conditioning on any available covariate, including measured serving-satellite geometry, is worse than not conditioning, and our attempt to predict which datasets benefit failed. What is new here is empirical, not algorithmic: we claim the findings, not the methods.

title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
summary:
Office documents are now routinely uploaded to large language models (LLMs) for processing. However, an LLM does not always see what a human sees, because it typically reads the text that an extractor produces from the document's underlying Office Open XML (OOXML) files. Depending on the implementation, extractors differ in which OOXML parts they read and how they interpret them, so their output can differ from what Office applications display. For example, by slightly shifting the positions of text boxes on a slide, an adversary can swap the order in which the model reads them while the slide looks unchanged. We show that this extraction divergence is an attack surface for LLM applications.
  In this work, we first measure what an adversary can exploit by analyzing the widely used extractors that LLM applications rely on. By combining static source code analysis with dynamic analysis, we identify 19 OOXML channels where extractors read content a human cannot see and 12 where they drop content a human can. We also find that widely used extractors ignore display formatting and reading order, so even visible content reaches the model in a different form. Building on these findings, we construct five attacks that lead the model to interpret a document differently from a human reviewer, without injecting any instruction. We test the attacks on four major chat assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Microsoft 365 Copilot) and four coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, and GitHub Copilot CLI), and every one of them is misled by at least one attack. Finally, we propose Prism, a lightweight defense that reconstructs the human view from the OOXML specification before passing the text to the model. Prism also generalizes to unseen attack payloads.

title: When Is One Query per Template Enough? Adapting Learned Cost Models to New Hardware
summary: A learned cost model that predicts query runtimes is trained on measurements from one machine. When the database moves to other hardware, its plans stay the same but their runtimes change, each by its own factor. We ask how to adapt such a model from k queries measured on the new machine: which queries to run, how to use their runtimes, and how many are enough. On PostgreSQL we timed the same plans of 1,162 TPC-H and TPC-DS queries in six environments: a laptop and a server, each with all its processors or pinned to one, the server also pinned to two, and the laptop also with a small buffer pool. No single factor describes the slowdown between two environments: most of its variance lies between query templates, so a speed factor stops improving after a few queries. A correction that fits separate lines for serial and parallel plans and adds an offset for every measured template brings the moved model, with one measured query per template, to an error (geometric mean over templates of the median Q-error) of 1.10 on TPC-H and 1.19 on TPC-DS, close to the same correction on a model trained on the new machine; fine-tuning a DACE-style neural cost model on the same queries gains at most 2%. On templates never measured, no correction we tried is on average more than 2% better than the speed factor. We then fixed hypotheses and timed new data. On TPC-H at ten times the scale the errors follow these results, but two of five repeated tests miss. On the Join Order Benchmark, whose queries differ widely within a template, the model errs by 2.36 even when retrained on the new machine, no correction gains much, and only the test on new templates holds; boosted trees and a neural model fit these queries better, and correcting the neural model works as well as fine-tuning it. We report every test as registered.

title: When can multi-fragment 2D/3D registration be trusted? Calibrated certification and uncertainty-driven view planning for pelvic fracture fluoroscopy
summary: Registering a segmented CT to fluoroscopy can locate every fracture fragment but can guide surgery only when trusted. After each shot, our closed loop registers all fragments, bounds their errors with a calibrated sandwich covariance, flags implausible or ambiguous ones, and stops or plans the next view. On simulated fluoroscopy of 60 held-out fracture CTs with realistic image uncertainty, 95% bounds covered 83% of unflagged fragments and 91% of those within 5mm, but from the second view on 14% failed by over 5mm, a third with bounds of at most 2mm. A fragment's shift when a view was added separated tightly bounded failures best (exploratory; AUC 0.94, bound 0.81). Requiring that the newest view moved no fragment beyond its bound, preferred post hoc, lowered false stops at 2mm from 23% to 6% overall, with 345 instead of 362 correct ones but more trajectories uncertified; delaying the stop did not, and other signals at equal acceptance left 10-15% false. With a segmentation error shared by all views (median Dice 0.89), 21% of this rule's stops were false against 10% without it (15 cases; exploratory). Minimax planning certified sooner than the clinical protocol without the check (4.20 versus 4.72 shots, Holm p <0.001), but no criterion reached the pre-specified endpoint, a true 2mm error, significantly sooner, even in the true basin. On real fluoroscopy of five intact pelves no 2mm certificate was false. Trust takes evidence across views, not only a calibrated local bound.

title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue
summary: For humans, referential disambiguation is a collaborative process involving clarification questions asked when they will meaningfully change the outcome. However, large language models (LLMs) have been shown to be biased toward premature answering, preferring definite single-turn responses over more clarification exchanges. In this paper, we study the problem of "strategic clarification" -- asking clarification questions in a reference game when their answers will narrow the set of candidate referents. We construct a controlled test environment from the SIMMC 2.1 dataset that records how many questions each ambiguous reference needs to be successfully resolved, and examine how baseline LLM behavior and common post-training methods ask clarifying questions vs. attempt to answer the referent. We also propose BACE (Belief-Aware Critic with Epistemic tracking), a lightweight action chooser method on top of a frozen LM backbone, and show that BACE more consistently chooses the optimal number of clarifying questions than methods such as GRPO and ArCHer.

title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man
summary: Training an agent to play Pac-Man with only up, down, left and right actions raises a basic question: when performance is poor, what should be improved? Difficulty can arise from reading the screen or from choosing actions over a long sequence. We examine these problems in a Qwen3.5-9B-based agent through separate perception checks and primitive-policy reinforcement-learning studies. In the policy study, which uses textual boards to remove image transcription from the decision interface, completion on eight held-out mazes increased from 0% before this optimization to 80.2% at a selected checkpoint, with three extra lives. The perception checks show that accurate static screenshot reading can coexist with errors during interaction. A separate policy comparison also shows that further optimization can accompany worse action choices. Together, these findings motivate concrete checks for post-training: evaluate perception in use, distinguish training success from full-game validation, and examine decisions and later performance rather than relying on one selected score. The study provides empirical lessons for improving future agent training and evaluation.

title: Where Search Agents Go Off the Rails: Graph-Grounded Step-Level Verification
summary: Search-augmented reasoning systems can reach correct answers while making errors in intermediate steps. Reliable auditing must check whether evidence $D$ covers the question $Q$, reasoning $T$ addresses $Q$, and $T$ is grounded in $D$. We introduce GraphRail, which represents requirements, evidence, and reasoning as structured claims and compares them without a generative judge or gold answer. Across three multi-hop QA benchmarks and three reasoning frameworks, GraphRail improves error recall over generative verifiers while remaining stable under stochastic extraction. Its diagnoses can also guide online reasoning, providing a traceable way to detect and correct intermediate errors.

title: Which One Is Sounding? Binaural Sounding Instance Disambiguation for Audio-Visual Segmentation
summary: Existing audio-visual segmentation methods mainly predict sound-related regions or category masks and often fail to identify the sounding instance when multiple same-class candidates coexist. Recent audio-visual instance segmentation methods address instance-level prediction but rely largely on motion and cross-frame association, which may become unreliable under sparse observations or inconspicuous motion. To this end, we introduce binaural audio, whose interaural differences encode source-direction information, to provide spatial constraints for distinguishing the sounding instance among same-class visual candidates. We propose Binaural Sounding Instance Disambiguation for Audio-Visual Segmentation (BiSID-AVS), which progressively refines category-level candidate responses into a mask of the true sounding instance. BiSID-AVS first grounds category-consistent candidate regions through audio prompting, then projects binaural cues into an image-plane spatial response map, and finally refines the true sounding instance through dual-level spatial conditioning at the feature and decoder levels. Experiments on the binaurally extended AVS-Synthetic benchmark and Habitat-AVS dataset for robotic indoor perception show that BiSID-AVS achieves the best performance on the multi-candidate subsets, improving instance-level mIoU by 35.19 and 41.21 percentage points, respectively, while substantially reducing false activation on non-sounding same-class regions.

title: Whiel: A Neurosymbolic Platform for Certified Relational Program Verification
summary: We present the Whiel (a contraction of Whi(le-R)el) system for Lean-certified reasoning about imperative relational programs. The system can encode containment and equivalence problems for Datalog, its extensions with negation, and the core fragment of graph query languages. It can also represent optimized or incremental evaluation algorithms that are not expressible in the original query language, as well as first-order specifications of integrity constraints, schema mappings, and views arising in data integration, exchange, and sharing. Whiel's program states are database instances, and its imperative structure enables compositional Hoare-style reasoning with first-order relational specifications, using prophecy variables and leveled invariants to support inductive arguments. Whiel supports neurosymbolic discovery of loop invariants whose verification conditions can be checked using the Vampire first-order theorem prover. Counterexamples are fed back into the neurosymbolic pipeline, while proposed solutions are translated into Lean proof certificates. To validate the Whiel system, we evaluate its performance on a curated benchmark suite. In summary, we envision the Whiel system as a tool for tackling mathematically demanding, typically undecidable problems involving complex query and constraint languages, with a high degree of trust in its output.

title: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox
summary: Generative models trained on the output of earlier models lose knowledge across generations, rare knowledge first. The remedies that work all bring in information from outside the loop, and the theory of model collapse treats that supply as given: a fixed archive, drawn from a fixed distribution. We argue that the supply is the problem, and that cultural evolution has the theory of it. We read model collapse as Rogers' paradox: a population that comes to rely on copying ends up no better off than one that never copied, because copies go stale unless someone keeps learning for themselves. We test the identification in three steps. First, Rogers' model, fitted only to fully synthetic training, predicts to within a few percentage points how much rare knowledge language models, from word trigrams to a pretrained transformer, retain under other mixtures of fresh data. Second, when the world itself changes, a lineage that copies its own past needs more fresh data to keep up the faster the world changes, as Rogers' model says it must and as analyses that assume a fixed target cannot; a lineage that restarts every generation from fixed pretrained weights is largely insulated, because those weights are knowledge that is never copied. Third, we close the loop: when the people who write a model's training data can ask the model instead of finding things out, the supply of fresh data becomes endogenous. At equilibrium, the model is exactly as reliable as it is costly for people to find out for themselves, the population is no better off than without the model, and every increase in the share of model-written text must be paid for by more people learning for themselves. Users who check what they are told and relearn when it is wrong break the paradox. Filters that select plausible text are conformist and accelerate collapse; only checks that carry new information act as critical learning.

title: Whose Transparency is it Anyway? Understanding Generative AI Transparency Needs and Gaps Across Stakeholders
summary: Transparency has become a central principle in AI governance, yet there is little agreement about what transparency means, for whom, and in what contexts. Drawing on interpretive flexibility within the Social Construction of Technology, this paper examines how different stakeholders understand and experience transparency in generative AI. This study draws from a global survey of 400 end-users, AI builders, and policymakers, complemented by a structured focus group with end-users, grounding the quantitative findings in qualitative insights from the group most underserved by current transparency practice. We present three key findings. First, all three groups share similar understandings of what transparency means and what it should afford, centered on ensuring accuracy and privacy. Second, gaps between the importance of transparency features and their perceived availability are substantially larger for end-users than builders, revealing how power shapes what gets built and who it serves. Only 28% of end-users report that current transparency practices reflect their needs very well, compared to 53% of builders and 49% of policymakers. Third, transparency is situationally constructed, priorities shift with context and task structure, with role-specific frames activating when context demands them and receding when it does not. We argue that meaningful AI transparency requires moving beyond a one-size-fits-all solution, including current emphases on AI disclosure and static documentation, toward pluralistic transparency infrastructures that reflect the needs of diverse users and stakeholders.

title: Whose Values Are Generated? Measuring Visual Value Leakage in Multilingual Text-to-Image Generation
summary: Text-to-image (T2I) systems serve users across languages and cultural contexts. However, evaluations of cultural representation focus mainly on recognizable elements such as landmarks, clothing, and activities, overlooking the cultural values that generated images convey. To bridge this gap, we introduce VisionValueBench, a multilingual benchmark that operationalizes six of Hofstede's cultural value dimensions (e.g., individualism versus collectivism) to investigate how T2I systems frame neutral social situations through a particular cultural orientation. We find that value-neutral prompts, which admit diverse cultural interpretations, nonetheless yield images that favor particular value orientations, a phenomenon we call visual value leakage. We evaluate prompts varying in language and geographic cues across 960 social scenarios and six T2I configurations. Generated images consistently favor the same value orientations across all six dimensions, for example, equality over hierarchy (low power distance), individual autonomy over group obligation (individualism), and enjoyment over restraint (indulgence). Prompt language has limited influence on these orientations, whereas geographic cues shift some dimensions toward the associated cultural values while largely preserving the prevailing orientations. These findings reveal substantial homogeneity in the cultural values conveyed by T2I systems worldwide.

title: Within-Family EfficientNet Scaling under Fixed-Resolution Transfer Learning for Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Retinal Disease Classification
summary: Background/Objectives: CNNs perform well in retinal disease classification from spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), but whether EfficientNet's natural-image scaling hierarchy transfers to medical-image transfer learning at fixed resolution remains unclear. This study evaluates EfficientNet-B0-B7 for four-class SD-OCT classification and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. Methods: Eight ImageNet-pretrained variants (4.05-64.10M instantiated backbone parameters) were evaluated at 224x224 on the Kermany dataset. Grayscale images were replicated to RGB and processed using model-embedded preprocessing and augmentation. Training comprised frozen-backbone head training followed by partial fine-tuning. Metrics covered classification, discrimination, efficiency, and visual analyses. Results: Test accuracy varied non-monotonically from 95.93% (B0) to 96.95% (B1); B7 achieved 96.73%. B1 had the highest accuracy and Drusen F1 (0.8780), while B7 had Drusen F1 of 0.8720 and the highest Drusen recall (0.9177). Drusen had the lowest F1 across all variants and contributed 82.2% of the summed squared deviation in class-specific F1; class ranking remained Normal > CNV > DME > Drusen. The OCT accuracy ranking differed from the reported ImageNet hierarchy, where B7 ranked first. The accuracy-to-parameter ratio fell from 19.82 to 1.48 percentage points per million total parameters. The final train-test gap had a weak, non-significant association with test accuracy (r = 0.26, p = 0.53). Conclusions: Larger EfficientNet variants did not consistently improve SD-OCT classification. B1 achieved the highest accuracy and Drusen F1, whereas B7 showed a secondary accuracy recovery at greater model size and CPU latency, indicating task and protocol dependent scaling effects. As cross-partition duplicates have not been independently audited, results are conditional on the supplied split.

title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement
summary: A real photograph is often blurry, grainy, compressed, scratched, and low-resolution at the same time. Each defect has its own severity and its own place in the image. The corrections for these defects conflict with each other. Exist- ing models describe the whole image with one description, so they cannot say where each correction belongs. To solve this problem, we present Wonder 4, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model for image quality enhancement. It corrects several defects of a real photograph at the same time, each in the region where it occurs. Every block of the model holds a mixture of N = 13 experts. A router, trained with the model, sends every image patch to k = 5 of them. No degradation classifier, mask, prompt, detector, or task label is used. Another issue is that standard MoE training, taken from language models, pushes every expert toward equal use. Equal use applies every correction everywhere, even where it is not needed. We replace this rule with a bias that only sets a minimum share of use. Across all patches, an expert used less than this minimum gets higher router scores until it is selected again. An expert above the minimum is not changed, so no expert is forced to be used as often as the others. The bias needs no extra loss. The method adds no extra module and no extra processing step. We evaluate Wonder 4 on DIV2K and Flickr2K, against five published methods and three open-weight pipelines. It reaches the best LPIPS, DISTS, and NIQE on all three test settings (DIV2K x4, DIV2K x8, and Flickr2K x4).

title: XuanJian-DINOSAR: A SAR Foundation Model Based on Global and Local Semantic Consistency
summary: Self-supervised pre-training on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery enables transferable representations, but the optical-SAR domain gap and speckle perturbations limit representation stability. Most SAR foundation models use masked image modeling (MIM) through pixel reconstruction or structural feature prediction, which is sensitive to speckle or relies on predefined operators. Joint modeling of cross-view semantics and perturbation stability at corresponding spatial locations remains underexplored. We propose XuanJian-DINOSAR, a SAR foundation model based on global and local semantic consistency. We curate over 360K publicly available SAR target chips, detection images, and scene images spanning diverse targets, scenes, and sensors, and adapt an optically pre-trained DINOv2 model to SAR through self-supervised learning. The framework combines DINO global semantic self-distillation, iBOT local masked modeling, and KoLeo feature-distribution regularization to learn globally discriminative and locally structure-aware representations. We introduce a local semantic consistency branch tailored to SAR intensity statistics and coherent imaging characteristics. Shared geometric transformations produce spatially aligned teacher weak views and student strong views. Intensity transformations and Gamma multiplicative speckle perturbations are applied to student views, while a cosine consistency loss aligns patch tokens at corresponding locations, promoting stability under radiometric perturbations. This objective complements the cross-region and cross-scale semantic consistency of DINOv2 multi-crop training, jointly enforcing global and local semantic consistency. Experiments on multiple downstream classification and detection datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on most evaluation metrics, validating the generality and transferability of the learned representations.

title: You don't need long context
summary: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts. We further demonstrate that LLM performance does not collapse on long-horizon software engineering tasks even when taking at most one action per context, and based on that we outline the concept of semantic state space models (SSSMs). Our findings question the need for long-context language models.

title: Zero-Shot Coordination among LLM Agents
summary: We study zero-shot coordination (ZSC), where independently developed agents must coordinate at test time. While ZSC has been well studied in the RL literature, far less is known about the performance of LLM agents despite their increasing deployment in such settings. Existing work on LLM coordination often relies on specialised scaffolding that independently developed agents are unlikely to share in practice. Moreover, evaluations on complex environments (e.g., Hanabi) make it difficult to pinpoint the sources of coordination failure. In contrast, we focus on simple, general-purpose scaffolds in minimal environments designed to isolate specific coordination challenges. Our results show that even in these controlled settings, frontier LLM agents struggle to coordinate, largely due to limited understanding of the coordination problem and weak reasoning about their partner's beliefs. While LLMs introduce semantic information as an additional axis for coordination, they nonetheless fail to exploit this structure effectively. Towards this, we propose Coordination-friendly definitions (CFDs) as a principled approach for enabling robust coordination among LLM agents. Finally, we show that CFDs can be discovered automatically, removing the need for manual engineering. Code is available at https://github.com/ahayler/zsc-llm-agents.

title: Zuse: A Decision Model for European Languages
summary: Decision models read a document and return a probability for each of a fixed set of options instead of generating text. Several appeared in 2026, but none has published results outside English. We describe Zuse, three decision models (4B, 9B and 27B) that train a low-rank adapter and a pointer head on frozen open-weight bases, targeting 27 European languages, and use them to study how this design behaves across languages and tasks. On a broad European suite of 11 sources excluded from training, covering 9 task groups and 27 languages, a development set that also guided model selection, the 27B model reaches 87.5% accuracy with a pooled expected calibration error of 0.016, and 0.035 when weighted per source. Post-hoc analyses of these single-seed results give three findings. First, miscalibration is structured by task rather than language: on parallel reading and topic items in 26 languages the confidence gap varies about as much as sampling noise, while across sources it spans -0.07 to +0.09, with knowledge tasks overconfident and acceptability judgements underconfident at all three sizes, so one fitted temperature cannot correct both. Second, the share of decisions that can be automated at a 5% error budget follows chance-corrected skill (Spearman 0.97 over 33 source and model pairs) more closely than raw accuracy (0.91). Third, reach beyond the training languages is set by the base model: across 210 languages, changing the training run moved scores by at most about 2 points within a size, while languages outside the base's documented list trail by 23 to 28 points at every size. On English public suites Zuse is behind Jev and Kev, including Kev models on the same bases. We also report two pitfalls in building multi-source training data: label-word collision between topic schemes, and an injection augmentation that taught a shortcut. Zuse can be tried at https://bineric.com/zuse.

title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
summary: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. We curate and unify heterogeneous robot datasets to support spatial learning across diverse embodiments, tasks, and scenes. To accommodate this diversity, we introduce feature-dependent gates that adaptively aggregate visual embeddings from multiple VLA layers for spatial supervision. The teacher further exploits partially available depth and camera calibration alongside RGB observations, enabling effective use of heterogeneous geometric annotations. Probabilistic state dropout encourages reliance on visual cues and mitigates overfitting to demonstration trajectories. All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture.
summary_zh: 可靠的机器人操作需要三维空间中的语义理解与精确控制。然而，视觉-语言-动作（VLA）基础模型在很大程度上继承了二维视觉-语言预训练的视觉表征，而空间监督通常仅在任务特定适配阶段才被引入。因此，将空间理解发展为一种可迁移的基础模型能力，需要从更广泛的机器人经验中学习。我们提出了SLA，一种空间-语言-动作模型（Spatial-Language-Action Model），该模型将隐式空间对齐扩展到持续预训练阶段，并在下游后训练期间保持这种对齐。SLA从预训练的pi05策略初始化，联合优化动作预测以及中间视觉嵌入与来自冻结三维感知模型的空间表征之间的对齐。我们整理并统一了异构机器人数据集，以支持跨多种具身形态、任务和场景的空间学习。为适应这种多样性，我们引入了特征依赖门控，自适应地聚合来自多个VLA层的视觉嵌入以进行空间监督。教师模型进一步利用了部分可用的深度信息和相机标定参数，结合RGB观测，从而有效利用异构几何标注。概率性状态丢弃鼓励模型依赖视觉线索，并减轻对演示轨迹的过拟合。所有辅助组件仅在训练期间使用，从而允许直接复用预训练的VLA权重，并保持原有推理架构不变。
tldr: SLA scales spatial-language-action models by continually pre-training on heterogeneous robot data, using a frozen 3D perception model to supervise visual embeddings via feature-dependent gates and probabilistic state dropout, improving spatial understanding while preserving inference-time architecture.
tldr_zh: SLA 通过持续预训练，利用冻结的3D感知模型监督视觉嵌入，并采用特征相关门控和概率状态丢弃，在异构机器人数据上扩展空间-语言-动作模型，提升空间理解同时保持推理架构不变。

title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
summary: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.
summary_zh: 世界-动作模型适配预训练的视频生成器，而视觉-语言-动作模型则建立在预训练的视觉-语言骨干网络之上；两者都将策略架构和推理成本绑定到为生成而非控制设计的大型Transformer上。这些面向生成的设计选择在多大程度上影响控制性能，目前仍不清楚。在本工作中，我们提出了潜动作JEPA（La-JEPA），一种紧凑的世界-动作模型，其策略Transformer在预训练V-JEPA 2.1编码器的特征空间中从头训练。遵循Fast-WAM的思路，La-JEPA在训练期间联合预测未来特征与动作，推理时仅生成动作。在无具身预训练的策略中，La-JEPA在干净和随机化的RoboTwin 2.0场景以及指令正确的LIBERO-Plus上取得最优性能，同时参数量远少于最强的竞争策略。在相当性能下，其运行速度显著快于Fast-WAM，并且在LIBERO-Plus和RoboTwin 2.0上优于最接近的基于JEPA的方法——LeapBot-WA和JEPA-WAM，且无需其预训练策略主干。在四个真实机器人任务上，其平均成功率与pi0.5相当，并高于无具身预训练的基线。通过对La-JEPA背后设计选择的系统研究，我们证明JEPA特征优于视频VAE潜变量，在分布外场景中尤为明显；同时，训练时的未来预测选择即使推理时跳过未来预测，也会显著影响策略性能。我们修正了LIBERO-Plus的指令，因为官方发布的评估器会损坏大多数变体的指令，并重新评估了多个强开源基线。在无生成式预训练策略主干的情况下，La-JEPA优于且快于远大于自身的策略，这表明机器人基础模型可能受益于为控制而设计而非继承自生成的架构。
tldr: La-JEPA introduces a compact world-action model that trains a policy transformer from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA encoder, achieving state-of-the-art performance on robotic manipulation benchmarks with fewer parameters and faster inference than larger models.
tldr_zh: La-JEPA 提出了一种紧凑的世界动作模型，在预训练的 V-JEPA 编码器的特征空间中从头训练策略变换器，在机器人操作基准上以更少的参数和更快的推理速度取得了最先进的性能。

title: HITCH: Teaching a Vision-Language Model to Operate a Humanoid through a Whole-Body Harness
summary: Enabling vision-language models (VLMs) to control humanoid robots requires both reliable whole-body interfaces and knowledge of how to use the body that carries over across tasks. We present HITCH (Harness Interfaces To Command Humanoids), a harness in which perception returns the 3D position of any point the VLM selects in its image, and execution turns commands for the pelvis, torso, hands, walking, and gaze into whole-body motion with a learned tracker. We find that both measuring the scene and executing commands accurately raise task success. We then fine-tune a VLM on trajectories in which teacher policies solve five base tasks through HITCH, so that it learns how to operate the humanoid. Without task-specific trajectories, the fine-tuned model completes 51% of SIMPLE episodes and 42.5% of HumanoidArena episodes, and adding five trajectories per SIMPLE task raises its SIMPLE success to 95%. On a real G1, it carries a box and walks to a goal without real training data.
summary_zh: 使视觉-语言模型（VLMs）能够控制人形机器人，既需要可靠的全身接口，也需要掌握跨任务迁移的身体运用知识。我们提出了HITCH（Harness Interfaces To Command Humanoids）——一种操控装置，其中感知模块返回VLM在图像中选定的任意点的三维位置，执行模块则将针对骨盆、躯干、双手、行走和注视的指令，通过一个学习型跟踪器转化为全身运动。我们发现，准确测量场景与准确执行指令均能提升任务成功率。随后，我们在教师策略通过HITCH解决五个基础任务的轨迹上对VLM进行微调，使其学会操作人形机器人。在没有任务特定轨迹的情况下，微调后的模型在SIMPLE的50%情节和HumanoidArena的42.5%情节中完成目标，而在每个SIMPLE任务中增加五条轨迹后，其在SIMPLE中的成功率提升至95%。在真实G1机器人上，该模型在无真实训练数据的情况下，能够搬运箱子并走向目标。
tldr: HITCH presents a harness interface that lets a vision-language model control a humanoid robot by selecting 3D points in images and issuing whole-body commands, with fine-tuning on teacher trajectories enabling cross-task generalization and real-world deployment without real training data.
tldr_zh: HITCH 提出了一种挽具接口，使视觉语言模型能够通过选择图像中的 3D 点和发布全身指令来控制人形机器人，并通过在教师轨迹上进行微调，实现跨任务泛化和无真实训练数据的真实世界部署。

title: AffectiveVLA: Safe and Intent-Aware VLA Control for Human-Humanoid Social Interaction
summary: Social touch interactions, such as handshakes, fist bumps, and hugs, require humanoid robots to infer human intent, generate contact-rich motions, and maintain safe physical contact. We present AffectiveVLA, an intent-gated Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pipeline deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. A lightweight RGB-based model recognizes interaction intent from two onboard cameras and converts it into a language prompt for the VLA policy. Low-confidence predictions suppress motion execution, reducing unintended activations. During physical contact, interaction-specific compliance profiles adjust arm impedance, while an independent voice-triggered mechanism initiates a latched safe-stop procedure. Using VR teleoperation, we collected approximately 1,300 multimodal interaction episodes and fine-tuned four VLA models: GR00T, RLDX-1, Being-H0.5, and UnifoLM-VLA-0. On-robot evaluation identifies GR00T as the best-performing standalone model. Integrating intent recognition increases its macro-F1 score from 0.75 to 0.90, while the intent model achieves a p95 inference latency of 6.27 ms. These results demonstrate that explicit intent gating improves the reliability of VLA-based social interaction without compromising real-time operation.
summary_zh: 社交触摸互动，如握手、碰拳和拥抱，要求人形机器人推断人类意图、生成富含接触的运动，并维持安全物理接触。我们提出了AffectiveVLA，一种意图门控的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）流水线，部署在配备灵巧手的Unitree G1人形机器人上。一个轻量级基于RGB的模型从两个板载摄像头识别互动意图，并将其转换为VLA策略的语言提示。低置信度预测会抑制动作执行，从而减少非预期激活。在物理接触过程中，特定于互动类型的依从性配置调节手臂阻抗，同时一个独立的语音触发机制启动锁存的安全停止程序。通过VR遥操作，我们收集了约1，300个多模态互动片段，并微调了四个VLA模型：GR00T、RLDX-1、Being-H0.5和UnifoLM-VLA-0。机器人上的评估表明GR00T是性能最佳的独立模型。整合意图识别将其宏F1分数从0.75提升至0.90，而意图模型的p95推理延迟为6.27毫秒。这些结果表明，显式意图门控在不影响实时操作的前提下，提高了基于VLA的社交互动的可靠性。
tldr: AffectiveVLA is an intent-gated Vision-Language-Action pipeline for human-humanoid social touch, integrating lightweight intent recognition, compliance profiles, and a safe-stop mechanism, deployed on a Unitree G1 and fine-tuned with VR teleoperation data.
tldr_zh: AffectiveVLA 是一个面向人形机器人社交接触的意图门控视觉-语言-动作流水线，集成了轻量级意图识别、顺应性控制和安全停止机制，并在 Unitree G1 上部署与验证。

title: Concertina: Embodying Manipulation and Cognition in One Diffusion Vision-Language Model
summary:
Most vision-language-action (VLA) policies decouple manipulation from cognition by bolting an external action mechanism onto a vision-language model (VLM)--either quantizing actions into discrete tokens whose errors bear no stable correspondence to physical displacements, or delegating continuous trajectory generation to a separate action expert whose gradients compete with or are blocked from updating the VLM backbone. We argue that manipulation and cognition should instead be embodied in the same model, shifting from a decoupled VLA to an Embodied Vision-Language Model (eVLM). We introduce Concertina, an eVLM that places continuous trajectory representation, blockwise generation, and physical-coordinate supervision directly on the computation and parameter path of a shared diffusion VLM backbone. Each control timestep is encoded as one continuous latent action token in the backbone hidden space, and the shared Transformer reconstructs temporally ordered action blocks via the same corrupt-and-reconstruct operator used for multimodal pretraining. Active action projections account for only 0.21% of parameters in the 4.46B model with zero separate action-generator layers, compared with 16.5%-35.1% dedicated action-expert capacity in representative continuous VLAs. Using our proposed Action Interface Audit, we confirm that cross-time trajectory coupling emerges in the middle and late layers of the shared backbone rather than at the action interfaces. On standard benchmarks, Concertina achieves 98.15% average success on regular LIBERO, 85.9% on the 10,030-task LIBERO-Plus benchmark, and 4.142 average completed chain length on CALVIN ABC-D.
  Code: https://github.com/lose4578/Concertina Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/collections/Traly/concertina
summary_zh:
大多数视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略通过将外部动作机制附加到视觉-语言模型（VLM）上来实现操作与认知的解耦——要么将动作量化为离散令牌，其误差与物理位移之间缺乏稳定的对应关系，要么将连续轨迹生成委托给独立的动作专家，而后者的梯度与VLM主干更新相互竞争或被阻断。我们认为，操作与认知应内嵌于同一模型中，从解耦式VLA转向具身视觉-语言模型（eVLM）。我们提出Concertina，一种eVLM，将连续轨迹表示、分块生成和物理坐标监督直接置于共享扩散VLM主干的计算与参数路径上。每个控制时间步被编码为主干隐藏空间中的一个连续潜在动作令牌，共享Transformer通过多模态预训练中使用的同一“损坏-重建”算子重建时间有序的动作块。活跃的动作投影仅占4.46B模型中参数的0.21%，且不包含独立的动作生成器层，而代表性的连续VLA中专用动作专家容量占比为16.5%–35.1%。利用我们提出的动作接口审计（Action Interface Audit），我们确认跨时间的轨迹耦合出现在共享主干的中间层和后期层，而非动作接口处。在标准基准测试中，Concertina在常规LIBERO上达到98.15%的平均成功率，在包含10,030个任务的LIBERO-Plus基准上达到85.9%，并在CALVIN ABC-D上实现4.142的平均完成任务链长度。  
代码：https://github.com/lose4578/Concertina Hugging Face：https://huggingface.co/collections/Traly/concertina
tldr: Concertina introduces an Embodied Vision-Language Model (eVLM) that unifies manipulation and cognition by encoding continuous trajectories as latent action tokens within a shared diffusion VLM backbone, eliminating separate action generators and achieving strong performance on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN benchmarks.
tldr_zh: Concertina 提出了一种具身视觉语言模型（eVLM），通过将连续轨迹编码为共享扩散 VLM 主干中的潜在动作令牌，统一了操作与认知，消除了单独的动作生成器，并在 LIBERO、LIBERO-Plus 和 CALVIN 基准上取得了强劲性能。

title: Spatial-UMI-Dream: Scaling World Action Models with Metric Geometry for UMI Manipulation
summary: The Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) enables scalable demonstration collection independently of a specific robot. However, its moving, close-range gripper cameras entangle camera and object motion without a stable external view, leaving the metric geometry needed for precise manipulation implicit in RGB. We introduce Spatial-UMI-Dream, a 5B spatial World Action Model (WAM) pretrained on 605 hours of RGB-D UMI data through two-stage training -- world-only adaptation followed by joint world-action learning -- to jointly predict future RGB, fisheye-aligned metric depth, and actions. Stereo-derived depth makes scene scale and spatial relationships explicit within a unified dual-gripper RGB-D representation. Furthermore, evaluating UMI policies requires testing whether UMI's robot-independent demonstration collection translates into policy generalization across robot embodiments, alongside robustness to environmental changes. We introduce RoboTwin-UMI, a twenty-task simulation benchmark built on RoboTwin with UMI wrist-mounted fisheye observations, enabling controlled, repeatable evaluation of UMI policies under environment and embodiment changes separately and jointly without additional fine-tuning. On RoboTwin-UMI, Spatial-UMI-Dream achieves 79.10% in-domain success and 72.15% under combined embodiment and environment shifts, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline in each setting by 4.65 and 10.30 percentage points, respectively. It also exhibits the smallest success-rate drop under embodiment transfer among the evaluated policies. In a matched pretraining ablation, RGB-only pretraining leads to a 5.75-percentage-point decrease in in-domain success compared with RGB-D pretraining. Across six real-world tasks, Spatial-UMI-Dream achieves 85.0% average success, exceeding the strongest baseline by 24.2 percentage points. Project page: https://weiduoyuan.com/spatial-umi-dream/
summary_zh: 通用操作接口（UMI）实现了独立于具体机器人的可扩展示范采集。然而，其移动的近距夹爪摄像头将相机运动与物体运动耦合在一起，缺乏稳定的外部视角，从而使得精确操作所需的度量几何信息隐含在RGB图像中。我们提出了Spatial-UMI-Dream，一个5B规模的空间世界动作模型（WAM），通过在605小时RGB-D UMI数据上的两阶段训练——先进行纯世界自适应，再进行世界-动作联合学习——来联合预测未来RGB图像、与鱼眼相机对齐的度量深度以及动作。由立体视觉导出的深度信息在统一的双夹爪RGB-D表示中明确了场景尺度与空间关系。此外，评估UMI策略需要检验UMI的机器人无关示范采集能否转化为策略跨机器人本体的泛化能力，同时还需考察其对环境变化的鲁棒性。我们引入了RoboTwin-UMI，一个基于RoboTwin构建的二十任务仿真基准，配备UMI腕戴式鱼眼相机观测，能够在环境变化和本体变化分别及联合设置下对UMI策略进行受控、可重复的评估，且无需额外微调。在RoboTwin-UMI上，Spatial-UMI-Dream在域内任务中取得了79.10%的成功率，在本体与环境联合迁移下取得72.15%的成功率，分别超过最强评估基线4.65和10.30个百分点。在所有被评估策略中，它在本体迁移下也表现出最小的成功率下降幅度。在匹配的预训练消融实验中，与RGB-D预训练相比，仅使用RGB预训练使域内成功率下降了5.75个百分点。在六个真实世界任务中，Spatial-UMI-Dream实现了85.0%的平均成功率，超过最强基线24.2个百分点。项目页面：https://weiduoyuan.com/spatial-umi-dream/
tldr: This paper introduces Spatial-UMI-Dream, a 5B spatial World Action Model pre-trained on 605 hours of RGB-D UMI data that jointly predicts future RGB, metric depth, and actions. It also presents RoboTwin-UMI, a 20-task simulation benchmark for evaluating UMI policies under embodiment and environment shifts, achieving strong real-world and simulated results.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了Spatial-UMI-Dream，一个基于605小时RGB-D UMI数据预训练的50亿参数空间世界动作模型，联合预测未来RGB、度量深度和动作；并构建了RoboTwin-UMI，一个20任务仿真基准，用于评估UMI策略在实体和环境变化下的表现，在真实和仿真环境中均取得了优异结果。

title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
summary: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. Some approaches rely on human teleoperation and wearable capture devices, which require at least an hour of human time to produce an hour of data. We present HALO, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes. The corpus scales with compute rather than human labor. HALO acquires a repertoire of physical skills, including sitting on chairs, navigating to named objects, stepping sideways through half-open doors, crouching and crawling beneath tables, and pushing boxes. It orchestrates these skills to solve composite, long-horizon tasks. Without ever seeing a real home during training, HALO transfers zero-shot to the physical world, achieving a 91% success rate across 360 trials in six unmapped real-world environments. See https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-halo/ for code and videos.
summary_zh: 人形机器人有潜力实现多种体力任务的自动化。然而，迈向通用人形自主性的进展仍受制于数据瓶颈：将像素和自由形式的语言映射到低级关节指令需要成对的监督数据，而目前尚不存在足够大规模的这种数据集。一些方法依赖人类远程操作和可穿戴捕捉设备，这些方法至少需要一小时的人工时间才能产出一小时的数据。我们提出了HALO，这是一套人形自主系统，由一条跨一千个程序化生成家庭环境合成视觉-语言-运动数据的流水线驱动。该语料库的扩展依赖于计算而非人力。HALO习得一系列物理技能，包括坐在椅子上、导航至指定物体、侧身穿过半开的门、蹲下并爬过桌底、以及推箱子。它编排这些技能以解决复合的、长时程任务。在训练期间从未见过真实家庭环境的情况下，HALO零样本迁移至物理世界，在六个未映射的真实环境中的360次试验中取得了91%的成功率。代码和视频请参见 https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-halo/ 。
tldr: HALO is a humanoid autonomy system that synthesizes vision-language-motion data in simulation across a thousand homes, enabling zero-shot transfer of physical skills to real-world environments with high success rates.
tldr_zh: HALO 是一个人形自主系统，通过在模拟的一千个家庭中合成视觉-语言-动作数据，实现了物理技能到真实世界的零样本迁移，成功率高达 91%。

title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. Yet manipulation often hinges on precisely the visual signals most vulnerable to this abstraction, e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes. This raises a fundamental question: should action policies inherit a fixed visual endpoint, or directly access evolving visual computation? We introduce NEO-VLA, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework. Images are tokenized by lightweight patch convolutional layers and evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone, allowing a flow-matching action expert to draw from instruction-conditioned visual representations at different depths. This simple change reveals a consistent pattern. Native architectures outperform encoder-based counterparts under controlled comparisons; full fine-tuning reduces but does not erase the gap, and additional scale alone cannot recover it. More strikingly, layer-wise probing shows that the action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation. Across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts, NEO-VLA consequently achieves stronger and more robust control. Together, these results suggest that embodied control benefits from access to visual representations across the computational hierarchy, rather than a fixed encoder output.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作模型通常建立在一个简单的假设之上：感知首先由视觉编码器压缩，动作推理随后才开始。然而，操作任务往往依赖于恰恰最易受到这种抽象化处理影响的视觉信号，例如局部几何结构、边界、深度以及细微的状态变化。这引出了一个根本性问题：动作策略应当继承固定的视觉端点，还是直接访问不断演化的视觉计算过程？我们提出了NEO-VLA，一种结构上无需编码器的视觉-语言-动作框架。图像通过轻量级补丁卷积层进行令牌化，并与语言在整个骨干网络中共同演化，使得流匹配动作专家能够在不同深度从指令条件化的视觉表示中进行提取。这一简单的改变揭示了一致的规律。在受控比较下，原生架构优于基于编码器的对应架构；全参数微调缩小了差距但并未消除差距，而仅靠增加规模也无法弥补这一差距。更引人注目的是，逐层探查表明，动作关键信号往往在最终视觉表示形成之前就已达到峰值。在各种操作场景和分布偏移条件下，NEO-VLA因此实现了更强且更鲁棒的控制性能。综合来看，这些结果表明，具身控制受益于跨计算层级访问视觉表示，而非依赖固定的编码器输出。
tldr: The paper proposes NEO-VLA, an encoder-free vision-language-action framework where image patches are tokenized and processed jointly with language, enabling the action expert to access visual representations at multiple depths. This architecture outperforms encoder-based counterparts across manipulation tasks and distribution shifts, suggesting that policies benefit from intermediate visual features.
tldr_zh: 本文提出NEO-VLA，一种无编码器的视觉-语言-动作框架，其中图像块被标记化并与语言共同处理，使动作专家能够访问不同深度的视觉表示。该架构在多种操作任务和分布偏移下优于基于编码器的模型，表明策略受益于中间视觉特征。

title: MOMASPLAT: Dynamic Novel-View Demonstration Augmentation for Mobile Manipulation
summary: Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint. This is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa), where robots rarely execute manipulation from the exact same base pose used during demonstration collection due to navigation uncertainty, localization drift, and environmental constraints. Recent approaches use novel-view synthesis (NVS) to augment demonstrations with unseen viewpoints, but they assume static scenes and therefore fail to re-render the manipulated object during the post-contact interaction phase, leaving the most critical parts of the demonstration unaugmented. We present MOMASPLAT, a novel-view demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that synthesizes full manipulation trajectories from unseen robot base poses, including dynamic object interactions. Our key insight is that standard MoMa data collection naturally provides the multiview observations needed to reconstruct both the static scene and the manipulated object in 3D. MOMASPLAT combines 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward 3D foundation models, and kinematics-based action retargeting to separately reconstruct the scene and manipulated object, render them from novel viewpoints, and generate geometrically consistent synthetic demonstrations paired with transformed actions. We evaluate MOMASPLAT on five real-world mobile manipulation tasks involving both rigid and articulated objects across three scenes, and validate the fidelity of its synthesized demonstrations against ground truth in simulation. MOMASPLAT substantially improves robustness to unseen base poses, more than doubling the average success rate of the strongest baseline and maintaining non-trivial success at large base displacements where all baselines fail, while reducing the need for largescale real-world data collection.
summary_zh: 通过模仿学习训练的视觉运动策略对相机视角的变化高度敏感。这一问题在移动操作中尤为突出，因为导航不确定性、定位漂移及环境约束等因素，机器人很少能在与演示采集时完全相同的基座位姿下执行操作。近期方法利用新视角合成技术来扩充包含未见视角的演示数据，但这些方法假设场景为静态，因此无法在接触后交互阶段重新渲染被操作物体，导致演示中最关键的部分未被扩充。我们提出MOMASPLAT，一种面向移动操作的新视角演示扩充框架，能够从未见的机器人基座位姿合成完整的操作轨迹，包括动态物体交互。我们的核心洞察在于，标准的移动操作数据采集过程天然提供了重建静态场景和被操作物体三维结构所需的多视角观测。MOMASPLAT结合三维高斯泼溅、前馈三维基础模型以及基于运动学的动作重定向，分别重建场景与被操作物体，从新视角渲染二者，并生成与变换后动作配对的几何一致合成演示。我们在涉及刚体和铰接物体的五个真实世界移动操作任务、三个场景中评估了MOMASPLAT，并在仿真中对照真实值验证了其合成演示的保真度。MOMASPLAT显著提升了对未见基座位姿的鲁棒性，将最强基线的平均成功率提高一倍以上，并在所有基线均失败的大幅基座位移条件下仍保持非平凡的成功率，同时降低了对大规模真实世界数据采集的需求。
tldr: MOMASPLAT augments mobile manipulation demonstrations with novel views using 3D Gaussian Splatting and feed-forward 3D foundation models to separately reconstruct static scenes and manipulated objects, enabling dynamic object interaction synthesis and kinematically retargeted actions, which substantially improves policy robustness to unseen base poses.
tldr_zh: MOMASPLAT 利用 3D 高斯泼溅和前馈 3D 基础模型，分别重建静态场景和操作对象，生成动态物体交互的新视角演示并重定向动作，从而显著提升移动操作策略对未见基座姿态的鲁棒性。

title: GPWM: Modeling the World as 3D Particle Motion
summary: We introduce GPWM, a Generative Particle World Model that predicts how 3D scenes evolve by generating the motion of particles and rigid bodies over time. Unlike video world models that generate scene appearance, GPWM operates directly in 3D physical space. A single representation and architecture cover rigid, deformable, cloth, and granular materials, in both passive physics and robotic interaction. GPWM is an object-aware multi-resolution transformer that combines flow matching with diffusion forcing to generate coherent physical trajectories far beyond its training horizon. We train and evaluate GPWM on ParticleWorlds, a 25.5-million-frame corpus spanning diverse geometries, materials, interactions, and robot embodiments. GPWM outperforms the best prior learned-dynamics baseline in each of six physical domains, reducing prediction error by 31% on average. Breaking from the domain-specific setting of prior methods, a single Unified GPWM models these heterogeneous regimes with one set of weights, largely outperforming per-domain baselines and even surpassing our own specialist models in two domains. GPWM further generalizes to unseen geometries, physical properties, object counts, and rollout horizons. Beyond prediction, GPWM enables contact-rich planning by learning a generative prior over joint actuator-object motion. Instead of searching over unconstrained actions, planning searches the model's latent noise for interactions that achieve a desired object-space goal. With the same world model, noise-space planning substantially outperforms action-space search on pushing and picking, where complex contact sequences are hard to discover. Executed open-loop in simulation, the resulting plans achieve goal-directed manipulation without reference action trajectories or goal-specific policies.
summary_zh: 我们推出了GPWM，一种生成式粒子世界模型，能够通过预测粒子和刚体随时间的运动来模拟3D场景的演变。与生成场景外观的视频世界模型不同，GPWM直接在3D物理空间中操作。一个统一的表示与架构即可覆盖刚体、可变形体、布料及颗粒材料，并适用于被动物理场景与机器人交互场景。GPWM是一种对象感知的多分辨率Transformer，结合流匹配与扩散强制技术，能够生成远超其训练时域范围的连贯物理轨迹。我们在ParticleWorlds上对GPWM进行了训练与评估，该数据集包含2550万帧，涵盖多样的几何形状、材料、交互及机器人形态。在六个物理领域中，GPWM均优于先前最优的学习型动力学基线模型，平均预测误差降低31%。与先前方法针对特定领域建模不同，统一的GPWM以单一权重集建模这些异构场景，大幅超越各领域独立基线模型，甚至在其中两个领域中超过了我们自己的专家模型。此外，GPWM还能泛化至未见过的几何形状、物理属性、物体数量及推演时域。除预测外，GPWM还通过学习联合执行器-物体运动的生成先验，实现了接触丰富的规划能力。规划过程不再搜索无约束的动作空间，而是在模型的潜在噪声空间中搜索实现目标物体空间状态所需的交互。在相同的世界模型下，噪声空间规划在推动和抓取任务上显著优于动作空间搜索，这些任务中复杂接触序列难以发现。在仿真中开环执行时，所得到的规划能够实现目标导向的操作，而无需参考动作轨迹或特定目标策略。
tldr: GPWM is a generative particle world model that predicts 3D scene evolution by generating particle and rigid-body motion, using a multi-resolution transformer with flow matching and diffusion forcing. It shows superior performance across diverse physical domains and enables contact-rich planning via noise-space search for robotic manipulation.
tldr_zh: GPWM是一种生成式粒子世界模型，通过生成粒子和刚体的运动来预测3D场景演化，采用结合流匹配和扩散强制机制的多分辨率Transformer，在多个物理领域表现优异，并支持通过噪声空间搜索实现接触丰富的机器人操纵规划。

title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
summary: Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC). We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control. The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions. RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently. The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. Comparing two interfaces, we find that a richer visual interface adds only 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost. Failures stem mostly from choosing a poor manipulation strategy or executing a good one imprecisely, rarely from misunderstanding the scene, and agents incorrectly claim success on 24% to 39% of attempted subtasks. Agents can also improve without human input: one successful demonstration in context raises Astra's score from 53.5% to 73.0% on a five-task subset, and a prompt the agent writes and revises itself reaches 72.0%. Code, videos and full traces are available at roboarcade.org.
summary_zh: 多模态能力的提升使智能体能够直接充当机器人策略，我们将这一设定称为智能体机器人控制（ARC）。我们推出了RoboARCade，一个跨越三种具身形态的长时程操作任务基准，旨在测试智能体在精准控制中的情境适应能力、记忆和推理能力。这些任务建立在现有的开源基准之上，通过扩大初始条件范围使其更具挑战性。RoboARCade易于使用和扩展：所有任务均在同一仿真后端MuJoCo上运行，每个任务都是自包含的数据包，智能体通过可互换的接口连接，因此新任务、新智能体和新接口可以独立添加。该基准拉开了领先智能体之间的差距：GPT-6 Astra达到49.8%，而Claude Fable 5.1为43.6%，仍有较大提升空间。对比两种接口，我们发现更丰富的视觉接口仅增加1.5至6.8个百分点的得分，但成本却是原来的1.7至2.3倍。失败主要源于选择了较差的操控策略或对良好策略执行不够精确，很少是因为对场景的误解，且智能体在24%至39%的尝试子任务中错误地声称成功。智能体也能在没有人工输入的情况下改进：在上下文中提供一次成功演示，可使Astra在五个任务的子集上得分从53.5%提升至73.0%，而由智能体自行编写和修订的提示词则达到72.0%。代码、视频和完整轨迹可在roboarcade.org获取。
tldr: RoboARCade is a benchmark for agentic robot control, featuring long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments in MuJoCo, designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning. It reveals gaps in current VLA agents and provides a flexible framework for evaluation.
tldr_zh: RoboARCade是一个用于智能体机器人控制的基准测试，包含MuJoCo中三种具身形态的长期操作任务，旨在测试上下文适应、记忆和推理能力。它揭示了当前VLA智能体的不足，并提供了一个灵活的评估框架。

title: Reinforcing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety via Negative-Aware Planning in a Unified World-Action Model
summary: World-action models (WAMs) jointly model future traffic states and driving actions for end-to-end autonomous driving in intelligent transportation systems. However, their action learning remains dominated by expert-trajectory imitation, leaving unsafe alternatives close to expert trajectories insufficiently constrained. To improve WAM robustness in safety-critical scenarios, we propose NegWAM, a safety post-training framework for unified WAMs that learns explicit safety boundaries from near-expert failure trajectories. NegWAM constructs negative trajectories that are geometrically close to the expert trajectory yet carry safety risks, uses them as repulsive anchors to steer predictions away from dangerous behavior, and encodes them as scene-conditioned rider tokens to learn scene--trajectory compatibility. During training, NegWAM jointly optimizes the flow-matching and near-expert negative objectives, while the auxiliary rider branch is discarded at inference, incurring no additional overhead. On NAVSIM v2, NegWAM achieves 40.4 EPDMS on navhard, a 4.1% relative improvement over the strongest compared scorer-free WAM baseline, and achieves 93.3 EPDMS on navtest. These results demonstrate that NegWAM achieves strong performance in safety-critical scenarios while preserving routine-driving performance. Zero-shot closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM further demonstrates cross-benchmark generalization. The code is available at https://github.com/Zizizi-hao/NegWAM.
summary_zh: 世界动作模型（WAMs）联合建模未来交通状态与驾驶动作，用于智能交通系统中的端到端自动驾驶。然而，其动作学习仍以专家轨迹模仿为主导，导致接近专家轨迹的不安全备选方案未能得到充分约束。为提升WAM在安全关键场景中的鲁棒性，我们提出NegWAM——一种面向统一WAM的安全后训练框架，可从近专家失败轨迹中学习显式安全边界。NegWAM构建与专家轨迹几何接近但存在安全风险的负轨迹，将其作为排斥锚点引导预测远离危险行为，并将其编码为场景条件化骑手令牌以学习场景-轨迹兼容性。训练过程中，NegWAM联合优化流匹配与近专家负目标，而在推理阶段丢弃辅助骑手分支，不引入额外开销。在NAVSIM v2上，NegWAM在navhard基准上达到40.4 EPDMS，相较于最强无评分器WAM基线相对提升4.1%，并在navtest上达到93.3 EPDMS。这些结果表明，NegWAM在安全关键场景中实现了强性能，同时保持了常规驾驶性能。在HUGSIM上的零样本闭环评估进一步验证了跨基准泛化能力。代码已开源：https://github.com/Zizizi-hao/NegWAM。
tldr: NegWAM is a safety post-training framework for unified world-action models in end-to-end driving, which constructs near-expert negative trajectories to learn explicit safety boundaries and improves safety-critical performance without extra inference overhead.
tldr_zh: NegWAM 是一种用于端到端驾驶统一世界动作模型的安全后训练框架，通过构造接近专家的负轨迹来学习明确的安全边界，在不增加推理开销的情况下提升安全关键场景的性能。

title: STEP: Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction for Perceptive Humanoid Locomotion
summary: For perceptive humanoid locomotion, the relevance of terrain geometry depends on the robot's body state and how both evolve under its actions. Existing work has advanced terrain-aware sensory fusion and cross-modal prediction, improving how visual and proprioceptive information is combined and related. However, feature aggregation alone does not specify which cross-modal relationships should be learned, while prediction between simultaneous observations does not explicitly constrain their action-dependent evolution. We present Spatiotemporal Training with Explicit Prediction (STEP), a one-stage framework that jointly supervises cross-modal relationships and action-dependent state evolution within a shared control representation. Multiple learned queries aggregate depth and proprioceptive tokens into a compact policy state. Bidirectional masked prediction uses each visible modality to predict latent features of the omitted modality, explicitly supervising terrain-body relationships. An action-conditioned predictor maps the current policy state and executed action to the next fused state, with an exponential-moving-average target defined directly in the policy representation space. Simulation comparisons show overall improvements in terrain traversal over evaluated fusion alternatives and ablations, while depth-dropout and delay experiments demonstrate the benefits of both predictive objectives under degraded visual input. Deployed on a 23-DoF Noetix E1 humanoid with onboard sensing, STEP succeeds in 98 of 100 hardware trials across stairs, a 40\,cm platform, a 70\,cm gap, stepping stones, and backward stair traversal without rearward terrain visibility.
summary_zh: 面向具身智能的人形机器人运动，地形几何的相关性取决于机器人自身状态以及两者在其动作作用下的演化方式。现有工作已推进了地形感知的传感器融合与跨模态预测，改善了视觉与本体感觉信息的结合与关联方式。然而，仅靠特征聚合无法指定应学习哪些跨模态关系，而对同步观测之间的预测也未显式约束其动作依赖的演化过程。我们提出了一种带显式预测的时空训练方法（STEP），这是一个单阶段框架，在共享控制表示中联合监督跨模态关系与动作依赖的状态演化。多个可学习的查询将深度特征与本体感受特征聚合为紧凑的策略状态。双向掩码预测利用每种可见模态预测被省略模态的潜在特征，从而显式监督地形—身体关系。一个以动作条件化的预测器将当前策略状态与所执行动作映射至下一融合状态，并在策略表示空间中直接定义指数移动平均目标。仿真对比表明，与所评估的融合替代方案及消融实验相比，该方法在地形穿越方面总体表现更优，同时深度信息丢弃与延迟实验验证了在视觉输入退化情况下两种预测目标的优势。该方法已部署于具备机载感知的23自由度Noetix E1人形机器人，在楼梯、40厘米平台、70厘米间隙、踏脚石以及无后方地形可见性的倒走楼梯穿越共100次硬件试验中取得了98次成功。
tldr: STEP is a one-stage framework for perceptive humanoid locomotion that jointly supervises cross-modal relationships between depth and proprioception via bidirectional masked prediction and action-conditioned state evolution, improving terrain traversal in simulation and achieving 98/100 success on a real 23-DoF humanoid.
tldr_zh: STEP 是一个用于感知人形机器人行走的单阶段框架，通过双向掩码预测联合监督深度与本体感觉的跨模态关系，并经行动条件预测状态演化，在仿真中提升地形穿越性能，并在真实 23 自由度人形机器人上实现 98/100 的成功率。

title: Terrain-Indexed Motion Priors and Geometric Support for Extreme Humanoid Parkour
summary: We present a progressive imitation framework that learns terrain-appropriate humanoid parkour skills and subsequently adapts their hand--knee support. Human demonstrations provide traversal behaviors, but their contact patterns need not suit a robot's proportions or the available support surfaces. Our framework changes the role of demonstrations across three stages: privileged imitation produces physically executable robot references; terrain-indexed adversarial motion priors guide skill acquisition; and geometric support guidance with a reduced motion-prior weight enables contact adaptation. Candidate-based precontact attraction and actual-contact evaluation guide support without prescribing a contact sequence. The deployed policy selects behaviors from onboard depth, proprioception, and velocity commands without an external skill label. On the Noetix E1, the policy achieves 96.34\% hybrid success in simulation and transfers without real-world policy fine-tuning, completing 29 of 30 individual obstacle trials and four of five hybrid courses. Support-adaptation ablations show higher traversal success for the complete adaptation stage on the tested terrains, while qualitative observations show changes in contact placement. These results support acquiring skills from demonstrations before relaxing their influence to accommodate robot-specific support configurations.
summary_zh: 我们提出了一种渐进式模仿框架，用于学习适合地形的类人机器人跑酷技能，并随后调整其手膝支撑方式。人类演示提供了穿越行为，但其接触模式未必适配机器人的身体比例或可用的支撑表面。该框架在三个不同阶段中调整了演示的作用：特权模仿阶段生成物理上可执行的机器人参考动作；基于地形索引的对抗性运动先验指导技能习得；结合降低运动先验权重的几何支撑引导实现接触适应。基于候选的接触前吸引与实际接触评估共同引导支撑，而无需预设接触序列。部署后的策略仅依赖机载深度感知、本体感觉和速度指令选择行为，无需外部技能标签。在Noetix E1平台上，该策略在仿真中实现了96.34%的混合成功率，并且无需真实世界策略微调即可直接迁移，在30次单障碍物试验中完成29次，在5条混合路线中完成4条。支撑适应消融实验表明，在测试地形上，完整适应阶段具有更高的穿越成功率，同时定性观察结果显示了接触位置的变化。这些结果支持先通过演示获取技能，再放宽其影响以适应机器人特定支撑配置的训练范式。
tldr: This paper introduces a progressive imitation framework for humanoid parkour that learns terrain-appropriate skills from demonstrations and adapts hand-knee support via geometric guidance, achieving successful sim-to-real transfer without fine-tuning.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种渐进式模仿框架，用于人形机器人跑酷，从演示中学习地形适应的技能，并通过几何引导调整手膝支撑，实现了无需微调的仿真到现实迁移。

title: Time-Indexed Skill Success Models for Latency-Aware Skill Selection and Timing in Dynamic Manipulation
summary: Robots that manipulate moving objects act on observations that are outdated when the chosen skill starts, and the best skill can change within a few hundred milliseconds. Skill competence models, however, predict success for a launch at the moment of observation. We propose time-indexed skill success models, which predict whole-task success when a skill is launched after a given delay. Trained on rollouts branched at a grid of launch delays, they let a receding-horizon planner select both the skill and its launch time under fixed or random latency. In a MuJoCo study in which a UR5e captures a sliding puck with three skills, the planner exceeded a static competence model by 2.8 to 6.2 percentage points at 100 to 300 ms of latency, including when that model was evaluated on point or sampled forecasts of the launch state. Across five complete runs (three training seeds and two distribution shifts), all 80 paired 95% intervals against four baselines excluded zero. On delayed launches, the time-indexed model was calibrated (expected calibration error 0.009 against 0.239), and pausing the world during latency overstated success by up to 23 points. On a real UR5e that captures a rolling ball after 0.2 s of injected latency, a static model trained in a hardware-matched simulator predicted 99% success on a prespecified subset of 35 delayed launches that it rated at least 0.8. Of these, 63% succeeded (95% interval 46 to 77%), and the time-indexed model predicted 56%. In this single-skill, predictable regime, a matched physics-based forecast was also well calibrated.
summary_zh: 摘要：操控移动物体的机器人在选定技能启动时，所依据的观测信息已经过时，而最佳技能可能在数百毫秒内发生变化。然而，技能能力模型是在观测时刻预测启动时的成功率。我们提出了时间索引技能成功模型，该模型在技能经过给定延迟后启动时，预测整个任务的成功率。该模型在按延迟启动时间网格进行分支的 rollout 数据上训练，使得滚动时域规划器能够在固定或随机延迟下，同时选择技能及其启动时间。在一项 MuJoCo 研究中，UR5e 机械臂通过三种技能捕获滑动的冰球，在 100 至 300 毫秒延迟下，该规划器比静态能力模型高出 2.8 至 6.2 个百分点，包括当该模型基于启动状态的点预测或采样预测进行评估时也是如此。在五次完整运行（三种训练种子和两种分布偏移）中，与四个基线相比，所有 80 个配对 95% 置信区间均不包含零。在延迟启动情况下，时间索引模型具有良好的校准性（期望校准误差为 0.009，而对比模型为 0.239），并且在延迟期间暂停世界会高估成功率多达 23 个百分点。在真实 UR5e 机械臂上，在注入 0.2 秒延迟后捕获滚动球的实验中，一个在硬件匹配模拟器中训练的静态模型，对于预设的 35 次延迟启动中评分不低于 0.8 的子集，预测成功率为 99%。其中，实际成功率为 63%（95% 置信区间为 46% 至 77%），而时间索引模型预测成功率为 56%。在这种单技能、可预测的场景下，基于物理的匹配预测也具有良好的校准性。
tldr: This paper introduces time-indexed skill success models that predict task success for skills launched after a delay, enabling a receding-horizon planner to select skills and launch times under latency. Experiments in MuJoCo and on a real UR5e show improved success rates over static competence models in dynamic manipulation tasks.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了时间索引技能成功模型，用于预测延迟后启动技能的任务成功率，使滚动时域规划器能在延迟下选择技能和启动时间。在MuJoCo和真实UR5e上的实验表明，在动态操作任务中，该模型相较于静态能力模型提高了成功率。

title: GuidedWAM: Training-Free Energy Guidance for World Action Models in Autonomous Driving
summary: World action models (WAMs) for autonomous driving couple the driving policy and the visual world model in a single generative network whose objectives are fixed post-training. Conditioning on a new driving objective requires retraining.
