We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baselines. The basic harness supplies no grasping, pushing, or placing skills; the agent develops its own strategies, such as searching for hidden objects, using objects as tools, and calibrating its cameras. With the addition of a persistent memory store, the agent can also learn from experience: an augmented harness with a memory representation that is carried across episodes lowers the failure rate on RoboDojo bimanual manipulation tasks by 4.6x relative to zero-shot deployment. Our analysis suggests that AMPs are substantially more general and robust than specialist manipulation policies, providing a promising foundation for robot manipulation.
summary_zh: 近期关于机器人操作的研究主要集中于基于示范训练的专业化策略。我们证明，通用人工智能模型能够比视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA）和世界-动作模型（WAM）等专业化策略更可靠地控制操作器。我们系统性地分析了智能体操作策略（AMP），其中通用人工智能模型直接控制操作器，并随着任务推进实时调整其动作。我们提出了AMP1，一个参考框架，可在单臂、双臂和移动操作场景中无需修改直接运行。AMP1在RoboLab-120和CaP-Gym基准测试中取得了最先进的结果，且无需任何示范或任务特定训练。在RoboLab-120上，AMP1零样本成功率达到85.6%，而领先的VLA和WAM策略分别为49.2%和42.9%。在涵盖十二项任务和三种机器人实例的108次真实世界试验中，该智能体在104次中实现了零样本成功，相较于强VLA和WAM基线，失败率分别降低了20倍和15倍。该基础框架不提供任何抓取、推动或放置技能；智能体自行发展策略，例如搜索隐藏物体、利用物体作为工具以及校准自身摄像头。通过添加持久记忆存储，智能体还能从经验中学习：一个带有跨回合记忆表示的增强框架，在RoboDojo双臂操作任务中，相较于零样本部署，将失败率降低了4.6倍。我们的分析表明，AMP比专业操作策略具有显著更强的通用性和鲁棒性，为机器人操作提供了有前景的基础。
tldr: This paper proposes Agentic Manipulation Policies (AMPs), which use generalist AI models to directly control manipulators, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks and outperforming specialist VLA and WAM policies by a large margin.
tldr_zh: 本文提出代理操控策略（AMPs），利用通用AI模型直接控制机械臂，在RoboLab-120和CaP-Gym基准上实现了零样本的最先进性能，大幅超越专用的VLA和WAM策略。

title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
summary: Scenario-based simulation is central to evaluating autonomous-driving policies, but a scenario scripted before execution (i.e., with predetermined, fixed actor routes and speeds) may not preserve its intended interaction once the tested ego policy responds in closed loop. Scripted scenarios cannot adapt to unanticipated ego behavior, while learned traffic actors may remain reactive without reliably realizing a particular scenario intent. We introduce a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the joint traffic state and adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment for creating a specific scenario intent. At each step, the orchestrator solves a constrained optimization problem that preserves the intended interaction while limiting interventions and maintaining traffic feasibility. We further distinguish scenario realization from policy failure, allowing a test to first be judged based on whether the intended interaction occurred and then by how the ego policy responded. Experiments in the CARLA simulator across multiple scenario families and driving policies show that orchestration realizes targeted interactions more reliably than scripted and learned actor-level baselines, particularly under variations in initial conditions and ego behavior. These results support closed-loop scenario orchestration as a tool for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.
summary_zh: 基于场景的仿真对于评估自动驾驶策略至关重要，但执行前预先编写的场景（即预设了固定的参与者路线和速度）在测试的自我策略以闭环方式响应后，可能无法保持其预期的交互。脚本化场景无法适应未预料的自我行为，而学习型交通参与者可能保持反应性，却无法可靠地实现特定的场景意图。我们引入了一种场景编排器，它持续监控联合交通状态，并通过重新定时、重新规划路线和角色重新分配来调整非自我参与者，以实现特定的场景意图。在每一步中，编排器求解一个约束优化问题，该问题在保持预期交互的同时，限制干预次数并维持交通可行性。我们进一步区分场景实现与策略失败，使测试首先根据预期交互是否发生进行判断，然后根据自我策略的响应方式进行评估。在CARLA模拟器中跨多个场景族和驾驶策略的实验表明，与脚本化和学习型参与者级基线相比，编排能够在初始条件和自我行为变化的情况下更可靠地实现目标交互。这些结果支持将闭环场景编排作为受控且可复现策略评估的工具。
tldr: This paper introduces a scenario orchestrator for closed-loop evaluation of autonomous driving policies, which adapts non-ego actors in real-time via constrained optimization to reliably realize scenario intents despite varying ego behavior, improving over scripted and learned baselines in CARLA simulations.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于自动驾驶策略闭环评估的场景编排器，通过约束优化实时调整非自车角色，以在自车行为变化时可靠实现场景意图，在CARLA仿真中优于脚本化和学习型基线。

title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
summary: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation. Despite recent progress, reliably executing these tasks remains challenging because performance depends on complex robot-object and object-environment interaction dynamics. Existing approaches address this challenge either through model-based methods, which often require accurate dynamics models, or through learning-based methods, which reduce this requirement but typically assume a fixed or predefined initial grasp. However, different geometrically stable grasps can lead to substantially different downstream manipulation performance. Therefore, we propose Grasp-TAGS, a task-aware grasp selection framework for goal-conditioned large-object rearrangement. We train a unified PPO-based reinforcement learning policy across multiple initial grasp configurations and distill the learned critic into a lightweight grasp utility network that ranks candidate grasps using only the candidate grasp configuration and goal information. At inference time, we select the grasp with the highest predicted downstream utility for the downstream policy to complete the task, before even making a contact. Experiments demonstrate that Grasp-TAGS improves rearrangement success over both fixed single-grasp policies and random grasp selection, achieving an average success rate of 89.84% compared with 79.87% for the best-performing single-grasp policies, an improvement of 9.97 percentage points. Grasp-TAGS also reduces final orientation errors across all evaluated objects. For more qualitative results, refer to the supplementary webpage: https://rpm-lab-umn.github.io/Grasp-TAGS-web-page/
summary_zh: 移动操作（Loco-manipulation）要求移动机械臂在长时程范围内协调运动与操作，是在服务机器人和仓库自动化等应用中实现大物体重新排列的关键能力。尽管近期取得了进展，但由于性能依赖于复杂的机器人-物体及物体-环境交互动力学，可靠地执行这些任务仍然具有挑战性。现有方法要么采用基于模型的方法来应对这一挑战，但这类方法通常需要精确的动力学模型；要么采用基于学习的方法，虽降低了对模型精度的要求，但通常假设抓取是固定或预定义的初始抓取。然而，不同的几何稳定抓取可能导致下游操作性能显著不同。为此，我们提出 Grasp-TAGS，一种面向目标条件大物体重新排列的任务感知抓取选择框架。我们在多种初始抓取配置下训练一个统一的基于 PPO 的强化学习策略，并将学得的评论家网络蒸馏为一个轻量级抓取效用网络，该网络仅利用候选抓取配置和目标信息即可对候选抓取进行排序。在推理时，我们在产生任何接触之前，即为下游策略选择具有最高预测下游效用的抓取配置以完成任务。实验表明，Grasp-TAGS 在重新排列任务上的成功率优于固定单一抓取策略和随机抓取选择，平均成功率达到 89.84%，而性能最优的单一抓取策略仅为 79.87%，提升了 9.97 个百分点。此外，Grasp-TAGS 在所有评估物体上均降低了最终方向误差。更多定性结果请参见补充网页：https://rpm-lab-umn.github.io/Grasp-TAGS-web-page/
tldr: Grasp-TAGS introduces a task-aware grasp selection method that uses a distilled critic network from a multi-grasp PPO policy to rank grasps before contact, improving long-horizon loco-manipulation success and accuracy.
tldr_zh: Grasp-TAGS 提出了一种任务感知抓取选择方法，利用多抓取PPO策略中蒸馏出的评价者网络在接触前对抓取进行排序，从而提升长时程移动操作的成功率和精度。

title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
summary: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. A computer-use agent (CUA) can then perform embodied tasks through the same screenshots and keyboard and mouse actions that it uses to operate ordinary software. Using a single CUA design and changing only the software, our entries win first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions, without any competition-specific agent tuning. These results suggest that the skills CUAs learn on software, such as visual grounding, precise clicking, and exploration, already carry over to embodied tasks, giving CUAs a far broader scope in embodied AI than previously realized. We therefore advocate that computer-use agents can be embodied generalists. Further, we advocate that, by following the training strategy that made computer-use agents general, embodied AI can converge on a single general model as well, ushering in a new era of general embodied AI. Website: https://pranjal2041.github.io/cua-embodied
summary_zh: 在人工智能的诸多领域中，通用模型已逐渐取代手工设计的方法和专用架构。我们认为，具身AI正迎来类似的转变。我们的核心主张是，具身任务可以被形式化为与数字软件的交互。具体而言，我们构建了能够在屏幕上渲染智能体对物理环境视图的软件，并提供在环境中执行操作的控件。这样一来，计算机使用智能体（CUA）便可以通过其操作普通软件时所使用的截屏、键盘和鼠标动作，来完成具身任务。仅采用单一的CUA设计，且仅更换软件，我们的方案便在四场ECCV研讨会竞赛中分别斩获一、二、三和第六名的奖项，而无需针对具体竞赛进行任何智能体调优。这些结果表明，CUA在软件上习得的技能，如视觉定位、精准点击和探索，已能迁移到具身任务中，使得CUA在具身AI领域的适用范围远超此前认知。因此，我们主张计算机使用智能体能够成为具身通才。更进一步，我们主张，通过遵循使计算机使用智能体实现通用化的训练策略，具身AI同样能够收敛于单一通用模型，从而开启通用具身AI的新纪元。网站：https://pranjal2041.github.io/cua-embodied
tldr: This position paper argues that computer-use agents, which interact with software through screenshots and keyboard/mouse actions, can serve as embodied generalists by rendering physical environments on a screen and controlling them via software. The authors demonstrate this by winning prizes across multiple ECCV embodied AI competitions using a single CUA design without task-specific tuning.
tldr_zh: 本文提出，通过将物理环境渲染到屏幕上并用键盘鼠标操作，计算机使用智能体（CUA）可以充当具身通用智能体。作者使用单一CUA设计在多项ECCV具身AI竞赛中获奖，无需针对特定任务调整。

title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
summary: Tendon-driven continuum robots can reach through constrained spaces, but contact along their bodies is invisible to the sensors at their motors. We show that this is a structural limitation rather than a tuning problem: the map from contact forces to tendon measurements has a null space of dimension at least seven, so no estimator that leaves the contact support free can locate contact. When the obstacle geometry is known, however, non-penetration and complementarity make the contact force locally identifiable, and we prove that the resulting system with unknown contact inputs is locally exponentially strongly detectable. We present a constrained moving horizon estimator (MHE) that encodes these conditions and runs in real time as one quadratic program per sample, and we give a local, mode-wise robust stability result for it. In a finite- element benchmark of a two-section robot pressing and sliding on a wall, the estimator located contact to 0.9 mm and estimated contact force to 0.22 N, compared with 65 mm and 0.72 N for a tuned extended Kalman filter (EKF) with state projection. The estimator tolerated millimeter- level errors in the obstacle position and unmodeled wall friction, under which the projected EKF failed. Under randomized model mismatch over 40 trials, including unmodeled tendon friction, it remained better in force and location in every trial. Without contact, the MHE offered no advantage over the EKF, which confirms that its benefit comes from the contact constraints. This report extends a letter submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters with complete proofs and additional experiments.
tldr: This paper proves a structural identifiability limit for contact estimation on tendon-driven continuum robots and proposes a constrained moving horizon estimator that leverages known obstacle geometry to achieve highly accurate contact localization and force estimation in real time.
tldr_zh: 本文证明了肌腱驱动连续型机器人接触估计的结构性可辨识极限，并提出了利用已知障碍物几何的约束移动视界估计器，实现了实时高精度接触定位和力估计。

title: AdaptivePnP: Fast Auto-Tuned Plug-and-Play for Deconvolution
summary: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods reconstruct images by alternating a data-fitting step with an image denoiser. Their performance depends on two parameters: the step size $γ$ and the measurement noise level $σ$. In practice, $γ$ is often tuned by grid search over validation images and must be retuned whenever the problem setting changes, and $σ$ is assumed known or estimated separately. We propose AdaptivePnP, a PnP framework that jointly estimates $σ$ and $γ$ at every iteration from the data-fitting residual. To do so, we apply the PnP virtual model to the data-fitting proximal map and show that the residual is zero-mean Gaussian with covariance parameterized by $γ$ and $σ$. However, when one parameter is much larger than the other, the residual carries little information about the smaller one and using the maximum likelihood (ML) estimator can degrade the PnP iterations. We therefore introduce the identifiable maximum likelihood (IML) estimator, which restricts the ML estimator to an identifiable window in which the normalized Cramér--Rao bound of every parameter is bounded by a user-specified tolerance. For the virtual model, this window is an interval of ratios $ρ= γ/σ$, so computing the IML estimate reduces to a one-dimensional search over $ρ$. We apply AdaptivePnP to two standard PnP methods, yielding algorithms that require neither a tuned $γ$ nor a known $σ$. On image deblurring and super-resolution, AdaptivePnP matches or outperforms PnP baselines tuned with the true $σ$. Code is available at https://github.com/hdubasullivan/AdaptivePnP.

title: BEV3SR: Evidence-Aware 3D Spatial Reasoning from Video
summary: 3D spatial reasoning from video remains challenging for VLMs because videos provide sequential, view-local observations rather than persistent metric scene records. Many questions must be answered in a query-specified perspective rather than the observed camera viewpoint, and prompting with a fixed set of RGB views may miss sparse or occluded visual cues. To address these gaps, we introduce BEV3SR, a training-free and backbone-agnostic framework for RGB-D videos with camera parameters. BEV3SR turns video observations into queryable metric bird's-eye-view (BEV) scene memory and formalizes each query into an evidence-aware spatial task. The Spatial Task Formalizer specifies the query's reference frame, spatial constraints, objective, and evidence requirement. The evidence requirement determines the appropriate reasoning pathway. A query treated as requiring geometric evidence is handled by the Geometric Reasoner, which deterministically computes the answer using the metric BEV records in the query-specified reference frame. Otherwise, a query treated as requiring visual evidence is passed to the Visual Evidence Aligner, which uses BEV-indexed object records and their associated supporting views to retrieve object-consistent and scene-context RGB frames for VLM grounding. Within a standard 16-frame budget, BEV3SR consistently improves different VLM backbones across multiple 3D scene QA benchmarks, delivering large gains on spatially intensive questions and significant improvements on open-ended scene QA. These results demonstrate that BEV3SR offers an effective, efficient, and interpretable framework for explicit 3D spatial reasoning from video.

title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
summary: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. We present BitDecoding-FP4, an algorithm--system co-design for accurate and efficient native FP4 KV decoding. We mitigate three error sources: Dual-Residual Query Quantization splits queries into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; and Outlier-Aware Key Quantization combines static smoothing, Hadamard rotation, and scale search to suppress key outliers under token-wise scaling. At the system level, we remove the softmax bottleneck via transposed softmax with fused probability quantization and stacked query MMA on paged KV caches. Across dense and MoE models with GQA and MLA, BitDecoding-FP4 stays within 0.5 points of BF16 KV accuracy with NVFP4 (1 point with MXFP4), and tracks BF16 KV in RL training rollouts. In end-to-end serving on NVIDIA B300 with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, it delivers 2.4-3.0$\times$ higher peak serving throughput than BF16 KV. The implementation is available at https://github.com/OpenBitSys/BitDecoding-FP4.

title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
summary: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a method for constructing robust CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) from LLM reasoning traces. ARCs show on-par performance with frontier LLMs across a range of difficult mathematical and scientific tasks, are fully explainable, continually trainable, robust to input perturbations, and 16-291x cheaper to invoke than the source model.

title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
summary: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. Combining the two through agentic systems offers a route towards comprehensive radiology reporting, but published systems are tied to one modality or body part. We describe a radiology agentic framework that standardizes how an orchestrator calls modular tools to produce a structured report, and use it to measure what such a system can do with the tools from FDA-cleared radiology AI devices. Report generation is simulated on a large multi-modality report corpus, with the orchestrator given either a catalog of finding classes consolidated from the cleared devices, each available on the modalities it is cleared for, or an unlimited catalog in which any class can be requested, and planning either from the clinical indication or from the target report. Tool outputs are simulated from the reference report, so the comparison isolates tool availability and orchestration from tool error. With the cleared catalog and the indication alone, the orchestrator recovers under a third of the clinically actionable findings; recovery improves substantially with the unlimited catalog, and further when the plan is written from the target report. Attributing every missed finding to a cause shows that most are classes no cleared device offers for the study's modality, and that a third are classes or tools that were offered and not called. Adding the most frequently missing tools closes most of the gap to the unlimited catalog on held-out reports, whereas a smaller orchestrator with the unlimited catalog gives up the whole gain. Tool availability and effective orchestration are thus complementary constraints on comprehensive AI-assisted radiology reporting.

title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. One potential solution is to monitor for reward hacking and penalize it when detected; however, training against a monitor could lead to evasive behavior, and our general understanding of how to apply monitors effectively during training is limited. To study how best to use monitors to mitigate reward hacking, we introduce and open source three realistic environments where Qwen3-4B reward hacks: a coding environment hackable via test overwriting, a medical chat environment hackable via sycophancy, and a biography generation environment hackable via hallucination. We first focus on the coding environment, where we find that: (1) models can learn to evade highly accurate monitors by exploiting systemic flaws in probes and LLM judges; (2) monitors that leak more learning signal during RL suppress reward hacking but are more often evaded; and (3) including easier problems in training can decrease reward hacking. We apply our findings to build better reward hacking monitors for the medical chat and biography generation environments that improve upon naive baselines to reduce reward hacking rates across seeds to before-training levels in some interventions. Our results demonstrate that our takeaways translate to new settings and that better monitor intervention designs are possible.

title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
summary: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which large language model agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 1.4x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
summary: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. The core intuition is that inter-model agreement on semantics is informative about truth, and that an LLM-as-judge can provide higher-fidelity pairwise assessments than traditional string- or embedding-based metrics. We operationalise this intuition with (i) controlled summary generation from diverse models; (ii) a LLM evaluator that compares pairs of summaries and emits structured judgments; and (iii) a calibrated aggregation rule that combines supportive evidence while penalising only corroborated contradictions.

title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
summary: The pigs were bleeding. That was the point of the experiment: could airway pressure reveal hemorrhage before it became critical? In the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, the de facto benchmark for Time Series Classification (TSC), the same recordings ask a different question: "which of 52 pigs produced this trace?". The dataset PigAirwayPressure is not an outlier. Although the archive is the standard benchmark, whether its tasks resemble the problems TSC is meant to solve has rarely been examined. We find that several datasets are repurposed from their original task, built from toy setups, or have flawed test splits. We further question how representative the archive's ordered non-temporal sequences (e.g. spectra, shape outlines) are of real TSC, and the potential downsides from the decomposition of multivariate problems. Our findings call for more careful interpretation of archive-wide scores and greater attention to deployment-relevant evaluation. The audit is at https://github.com/automl/ucr-provenance-audit.

title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
summary: Many multimodal alignment problems require mapping a source modality into a fixed space defined by a target modality, where the target space is not merely an intermediate embedding but is used directly for downstream analysis. In this setting, successful alignment should preserve both the global structure of the target distribution and the instance-level correspondence observed in paired source--target training data. Existing objectives typically address only part of this goal: contrastive losses encourage relative similarity, distribution-matching losses improve marginal agreement, and pointwise regression fits each source sample to its paired target without explicitly modeling target-space path geometry. We propose FlowAlign, a flow-guided target-space alignment method that repurposes conditional flow matching as a training-time alignment signal rather than an inference-time transport model. FlowAlign uses the learned flow field to guide the alignment of source-side representations with the fixed target space, encouraging them to preserve paired correspondence while remaining compatible with the global target-space structure. We further provide theoretical analysis showing how FlowAlign helps improve paired correspondence by controlling endpoint accuracy and capturing local target-space geometry. Experiments on synthetic data, paired single-cell multiome benchmarks, and image--text alignment demonstrate that FlowAlign improves instance level correspondence while preserving target-space structure across different modality settings.

title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
summary: Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context. Yet the dominant paradigm in multi-person 3D motion prediction remains deterministic, with existing methods producing a fixed number of outputs per agent. In contrast, we present a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse future motions for multiple agents, modeling both global trajectories and root-relative poses. A B-spline reparameterization compresses the generative state space while enforcing temporal smoothness, and a dual-stream transformer conditions each agent's predictions on observed neighbor motion for interaction-aware forecasting. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on CMU-Mocap (UMPM) and 3DPW, outperforming deterministic baselines on joint position error, pose error, and final displacement error despite producing a full predictive distribution. We additionally establish the first motion prediction baseline on WorldPose, a large-scale professional soccer dataset, where social conditioning demonstrably concentrates predictive uncertainty along interaction-constrained directions.

title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
summary:
Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. However, extracting meaningful information often requires extensive manual review and clinical expertise. Automated surgical scene descriptions could reduce this burden by leveraging recurring surgical activities and prior knowledge.
  Methods: We propose GRAC (Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning), a framework that represents surgical scenes as graphs capturing relationships among instruments, actions, and anatomical structures. Given an input scene graph, GRAC learns to retrieve relevant graph-caption pairs from training data. It compares instrument-tissue interactions between retrieved examples and the input scene, using comparison features to condition retrieved-caption representations during generation.
  Results: On the EndoVis-18 benchmark, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.88, compared with 4.23 for SGT and 3.36 for the strongest conventional Transformer baseline. Exact instrument-action-target triplet-set accuracy reached 52.6%, compared with 32.7% for SGT and 26.2% for the strongest conventional baseline. These results demonstrate improvements in language quality and factual agreement. On TORS, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.06, compared with 3.80 for the strongest baseline.
  Conclusion: GRAC demonstrates that combining structured surgical scene representations with retrieved examples improves surgical scene captioning and produces more contextually meaningful descriptions.

title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
summary: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions. We port GLP to ESM-2 activations (UniRef50) and evaluate it at two host scales (ESM-2-8M and -650M), both as a lens for protein representations and as a prior for editing them. Generation quality scales smoothly with depth and compute. As a lens, single GLP "meta-neurons" are the strongest probes of discrete Swiss-Prot concepts at both hosts, beating InterPLM's released SAE features, and lead on continuous properties at 8M though not at 650M; falsification tests show this is mostly concentration, not new information. As an editing prior, the on-manifold correction makes DiffMean steering of three biochemical properties effective and restores on-manifoldness, but only in isolation: re-embedding the sequences actually produced after several rounds of decoding, the structural plausibility is compromised. This is mainly reproduced in additional SAE-based clamping structural steering experiments, where only Helix motif succeeds. The naturalness failure is traced to the rewriting coverage and the decoder rather than the prior, highlighting what the method must clear before it can serve for both discovery-by-editing and discovery-by-exploration. Trained GLPs are released on huggingface.co/collections/HPAI-BSC/glprot.

title: Graded convolutional networks: scale invariance without the scale and robustness to unknown blur
summary: The Gaussian jet of an image is a graded vector space: a dilation by $λ$ multiplies derivatives of order $k$ by $λ^{-k}$. Local graded convolutions are exactly homogeneous differential operators, and a local feature is dilation-invariant if and only if it factors through the scale-normalized jet or, without the scale, through the retraction onto the weighted sphere of the grading. Under unknown Gaussian blur the retraction changes only by a change of scale, whereas the scale-normalized jet acquires a grading factor that no radial normalization removes. At the zero jet the retraction separates image families that radial normalizations and continuous classifiers cannot. Networks built on the retraction are universal for invariant features. On MNIST such a network keeps 88.4% accuracy under a two-pixel blur, against 66.2% for the same network on scale-normalized derivatives; in Lindeberg's Gaussian derivative network the retraction raises accuracy at that blur from 91.5% to 95.1%.

title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
summary: The extent to which demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs, using pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to systematically map information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race. Across 69 organ-demographic combinations, demographic attributes were broadly recoverable, with pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group, and 0.662 for self-reported race, and substantial variation across organs. Demographic-class balancing produced relatively small changes in performance, while evaluation within diagnosis-text clusters showed modest attenuation. Under training with diagnosis-based grouping, demographic-associated signals remained detectable across multiple organs, including sex in gastric tissue (AUROC 0.865), age group in breast (0.816), and self-reported race in skin (0.728). Literature-guided analysis of these settings generated candidate histomorphological and contextual explanations for further investigation. Together, these findings provide a systematic map of demographic-associated information in routine histopathology, informing investigations of its sources, assessments of potential shortcut learning, and the development of more interpretable computational pathology models.

title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
summary: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years. This chapter gives an introduction and summary to the use of ML methods to optimize lattice field theory without introducing any uncontrolled approximations. We focus on those directions which are clearly established as of late 2025, marking the 50th anniversary of the beginning of the study of lattice gauge theory. This chapter is a contribution to the online book ``Lattice QCD at 50 years,'' (LQCD@50), edited by Tanmoy Bhattacharya, Maarten Golterman, Rajan Gupta, Laurent Lellouch, and Steve Sharpe.

title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
summary: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.

title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
summary: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood. We analyze majority-vote supervision for TTRL with online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and decompose its error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. Because population-majority bias is generally unidentifiable without external supervision, we focus on mitigating the downstream effects of finite-rollout variation. We propose \emph{Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO (PC-Dr.DPO)}, which conditions within-prompt robust reweighting on observed vote reliability to make updates from sampling-sensitive prompts more conservative. We further introduce a cache-based mechanism to reduce self-supervised forgetting during online adaptation. Across six mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and five model backbones, PC-Dr.DPO matches or outperforms the strongest TTRL baseline in 24 of 30 settings.

title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
summary: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR aboard the International Space Station. GEDI observations have geolocation errors of about 10 m, which cause misalignment with other remote sensing data and reduce the accuracy of downstream tasks. Matching GEDI ground elevations against high-resolution digital terrain models (DTMs) from airborne LiDAR is one way to correct these errors, but such DTMs exist in few regions. To widen this method's applicability, we super-resolved a more widely available low-resolution DTM and used it for the matching. Our question is whether a super-resolved DTM yields the same correction as a 1 m-resolution airborne LiDAR DTM and, if not, why. In steep forests of western Japan, we super-resolved an existing 10 m-resolution DTM to 1 m. Improving its accuracy required fusion with a global 30 m-resolution DTM from a different source. Using the resulting DTM, we corrected GEDI observation positions first by a single shift per ground track, then per observation. For most tracks, the shifts nearly matched those from the airborne LiDAR DTM, likely because DTM errors canceled out across many observations. Per-observation corrections, however, did not match. At a single observation, the error does not cancel out and is too large for the correction. This error likely originates mainly from the input DTM. Therefore, even without a 1 m-resolution DTM, a roughly 10 m-resolution DTM, fused with a global DTM and super-resolved to 1 m, should yield track-wise corrections nearly matching those from a 1 m-resolution DTM.

title: The Cost of Coverage: Conformalising Native Forecast Uncertainty for GB Wind Power
summary: Uncertainty bands on wind forecasts help inform reserve sizing and commitments, but often fail to deliver their stated coverage. We apply conformal prediction to native bands to see what it adds and what it costs, comparing six forecasters, from ARIMA to a tabular foundation model, at two wind farms in Great Britain (GB) under operational conditions. We show that calibration repairs empirical marginal coverage with little or no Winkler Score penalty, but this apparent success conceals under-coverage in high winds. Calibrating by forecast wind regime turns marginal coverage into regime-level coverage, cutting day-ahead out-of-band volume in high winds by over 40% relative to pooled calibration while narrowing bands overall.

title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
summary: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos. We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback for agent training and inference. We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards. Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages. Experiments show that Video-Coder achieves significant gains, improving Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0. We hope this work can serve as an open foundation for coding agents in video generation, and we fully open-source our data, models, and code

title: ZeoBench: A Benchmark for Self-Supervised Learning on 3D Zeolite Representations
summary: Zeolites are an important class of porous crystalline materials with broad applications in gas storage, separations, and catalysis. Although hundreds of thousands of experimentally realized and hypothetical zeolite structures are known, identifying materials optimized for a target application remains challenging because property labels are expensive to obtain and available only for limited structure-molecule pairs. While prior work has demonstrated that 3D neural representations can predict zeolite properties effectively, it remains unclear which representation-learning strategies are most effective in the low-data regime relevant to materials discovery. We present ZeoBench, a benchmark for self-supervised learning on dense 3D representations of all-silica zeolites, and evaluate the resulting features on six existing downstream adsorption-property prediction tasks, across a range of training set sizes. Our study compares self-supervised 3D pretraining on volumetric zeolite data, adaptations of image-pretrained 2D ConvNets and vision transformers to 3D via multiview and channel-inflation strategies, and 3D ConvNets pretrained on out-of-domain volumetric datasets, alongside hand-crafted descriptors and supervised baselines. Using our pretraining and evaluation framework, we find self-supervised 3D representations outperform existing methods and achieve state-of-the-art performance across both in-domain label regimes and for the unseen domain of metal organic frameworks. Learned representations consistently outperform hand-crafted descriptors, and convolutional architectures are generally more effective than vision transformers in this setting. These results establish ZeoBench as a practical benchmark for 3D representation learning in zeolites and provide guidance for data-limited adsorption property prediction.

title: ForeAct: Geometry-Guided Action Learning from World Representations
summary: Robotic manipulation requires representations that capture both scene geometry and its evolution during interaction. Existing approaches have largely treated these two aspects separately. World action models capture such dynamics by coupling action prediction with future video generation, but their reliance on iterative diffusion or rectified-flow inference leads to high computational cost, while their representations lack explicit spatial structure. Explicitly modeling scene geometry typically requires auxiliary modules that increase both parameter count and computational cost. Conversely, geometry-centric policies primarily recover observed spatial structure and often lack explicit supervision for anticipating future geometric changes during interaction. To address these limitations, we introduce ForeAct, which repurposes a pretrained video world model as a single-pass representation backbone for low-latency control. ForeAct directly processes the clean latent of the current observation in one forward pass, eliminating future-frame synthesis and iterative denoising while retaining the backbone's pretrained spatiotemporal priors. Rather than introducing a separate geometry backbone, ForeAct uses learnable tokens supervised by next-frame relative depth to shape the shared video representation through bidirectional self-attention. This compact interface turns the spatial knowledge already encoded in the backbone into a future-aware representation for action generation, with little parameter overhead. The lightweight geometry readout is used only during training and removed at deployment, enabling low-latency, geometry-aware control without depth input or an external geometry backbone. Without additional large-scale pretraining, ForeAct achieves 96.6% average success on LIBERO, 63.5% on SimplerEnv-Bridge, and a 74.4% success rate across 90 real-world rollouts.
summary_zh: 机器人操作需要一种能够同时捕捉场景几何结构及其在交互过程中演变的表征方式。现有方法在很大程度上将这两个方面分开处理。世界动作模型通过将动作预测与未来视频生成相结合来捕捉此类动态，但其对迭代扩散或纠偏流推理的依赖导致计算成本高昂，同时其表征缺乏显式的空间结构。显式建模场景几何通常需要辅助模块，这会同时增加参数量和计算开销。相反，以几何为中心的策略主要恢复观测到的空间结构，且往往缺乏对交互过程中未来几何变化的显式监督。为解决这些局限，我们提出了ForeAct，该方法将预训练的视频世界模型重新用作单次前向传播的表征主干，以实现低延迟控制。ForeAct在单次前向传播中直接处理当前观测的干净潜在表示，省去了未来帧合成和迭代去噪过程，同时保留了主干网络预训练得到的时空先验。ForeAct并未引入独立的几何主干，而是使用由下一帧相对深度监督的可学习令牌，通过双向自注意力机制塑造共享的视频表征。这一紧凑接口将主干网络中已编码的空间知识转化为面向动作生成的未来感知表征，且参数量开销极小。轻量级几何读取模块仅在训练阶段使用，部署时移除，从而实现了无需深度输入或外部几何主干的低延迟、几何感知控制。在不进行额外大规模预训练的情况下，ForeAct在LIBERO上取得96.6%的平均成功率，在SimplerEnv-Bridge上达到63.5%，并在90次真实世界 rollout 中实现了74.4%的成功率。
tldr: ForeAct repurposes a pretrained video world model as a single-pass representation backbone for low-latency robotic control, using learnable tokens supervised by next-frame relative depth to shape the shared video representation for action generation. It achieves high success rates on LIBERO, SimplerEnv-Bridge, and real-world rollouts without needing depth input or an external geometry backbone.
tldr_zh: ForeAct 将预训练的视频世界模型重新用作低延迟机器人控制的单次前向表示骨干，通过由下一帧相对深度监督的可学习标记来塑造共享视频表示以生成动作。在 LIBERO、SimplerEnv-Bridge 和真实世界 rollout 上取得了高成功率，且无需深度输入或外部几何骨干。

title: Zero-Shot VLA Adaptation with Retrieved Guidance
summary: Pre-training large parametric "Vision-Language-Action" (VLA) models on large demonstration datasets has recently yielded promising results for general-purpose manipulation. However, these models still struggle under even small domain shifts relative to the training data, such as changes in camera viewpoint, background, object identity, or robot morphology. Motivated by the success of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in language models, we pursue retrieval to boost VLA performance. Specifically, we seek to leverage retrieval from domain-mismatched, "in-the-wild" demonstration datasets like DROID to guide a VLA's behavior in a new target domain. To achieve this, we introduce RAGu, which overcomes robotics-specific challenges for RAG: (1) It incorporates simple geometric calibration to transform source demonstrations into the target setup and reduce cross-domain differences. (2) It uses a coarse-to-fine retrieval strategy that selects, from a large pool of pre-warped candidates, the trajectory most compatible with the base VLA. (3) It guides the VLA's flow-matching inference procedure rather than seeking to retrain the base model or expand its limited context window. We evaluate RAGu across real-world, simulation, sim-to-real transfer, and cross-embodiment humanoid manipulation. We find it improves real-world VLA success rates from 20% to 80% and outperforms the closest-related baselines in sim. Project website: raguvla.github.io
summary_zh: 在大型示范数据集上预训练大规模参数化“视觉-语言-动作”（VLA）模型，近期在通用操作任务中取得了令人鼓舞的成果。然而，这些模型在面对与训练数据相比即使是微小的领域偏移时，仍表现不佳，例如相机视角、背景、物体身份或机器人形态的变化。受检索增强生成（RAG）在语言模型中取得成功的启发，我们探索利用检索来提升VLA的性能。具体而言，我们旨在利用来自领域不匹配的“野外”示范数据集（如DROID）的检索结果，来引导VLA在新目标领域中的行为。为实现这一目标，我们提出了RAGu，它克服了RAG在机器人领域面临的特定挑战：（1）引入简单的几何校准，将源域示范转换到目标设置，以减少跨域差异；（2）采用由粗到细的检索策略，从大量预变形候选中选择与基础VLA最兼容的轨迹；（3）引导VLA的流匹配推理过程，而非重新训练基础模型或扩展其有限的上下文窗口。我们在真实世界、仿真、仿真到真实迁移以及跨形态人形操作中评估了RAGu。我们发现，它将真实世界中VLA的成功率从20%提升至80%，并在仿真中超越了最相近的基线方法。项目网站：raguvla.github.io
tldr: RAGu introduces a retrieval-augmented generation framework for zero-shot VLA adaptation, using geometric calibration, coarse-to-fine retrieval, and flow-matching guidance to improve manipulation success under domain shifts.
tldr_zh: RAGu 提出了一种用于零样本 VLA 适应的检索增强生成框架，通过几何校准、粗到细检索和流匹配引导，在域偏移下提升操作成功率。

title: Breaking survivorship bias in driving world models
summary: World models allow autonomous vehicles to imagine the consequences of candidate actions before execution, but their reliability depends on the futures represented in their training data. We identify a survivorship bias in driving world models: because the futures recorded in prevailing driving datasets almost always end safely, existing models often imagine benign outcomes even when a collision is imminent. We introduce a neutral world model (NWM) that learns both routine and safety-critical futures from a mixture of routine driving and real accident videos with a bounding-box-guided objective. The NWM more faithfully anticipates imminent collisions, while maintaining a low false collision rate and competitive generation quality in routine driving. We further use the model as an imagination engine for decision-making. Given multiple ego trajectories, the NWM predicts the future associated with each candidate, and a reward function evaluates these imagined outcomes before selecting an action. On challenging NAVSIM scenarios, this procedure selects the better trajectory more reliably than the baseline world model. Zero-shot experiments with real-world pedestrian dummy crossing data collected using an autonomous research vehicle further demonstrate transfer to unseen sensor observations. These results show that correcting survivorship bias enables world models to more faithfully reason about futures and support safety-critical decision-making in autonomous driving.
summary_zh: 世界模型使自动驾驶车辆能够在执行候选动作之前预想其后果，但其可靠性取决于训练数据中所表征的未来情景。我们发现驾驶世界模型中存在一种生存者偏差：由于主流驾驶数据集中记录的未来情景几乎总是以安全收尾，现有模型即使在碰撞迫在眉睫时也往往预想出良性结果。我们提出了一种中性世界模型（NWM），该模型通过边界框引导的目标函数，从常规驾驶视频与真实事故视频的混合数据中学习常规未来情景与安全关键未来情景。NWM能够更准确地预判即将发生的碰撞，同时在常规驾驶中保持较低的误报碰撞率和具有竞争力的生成质量。我们进一步将该模型用作决策的想象力引擎。给定多条自车轨迹，NWM预测每条候选轨迹对应的未来情景，并由奖励函数在选定动作之前评估这些预想结果。在具有挑战性的NAVSIM场景中，该流程比基线世界模型更可靠地选出更优轨迹。使用自动驾驶研究车辆采集的真实行人假人穿越数据的零样本实验进一步验证了该模型对未见传感器观测的泛化能力。这些结果表明，修正生存者偏差使世界模型能够更准确地推理未来情景，并支持自动驾驶中的安全关键决策。
tldr: This paper identifies and addresses survivorship bias in driving world models by training a neutral world model on a mixture of routine and accident videos, enabling more faithful collision anticipation and improved decision-making in autonomous driving.
tldr_zh: 本文识别并解决了驾驶世界模型中的幸存者偏差，通过混合常规和事故视频训练中性世界模型，使其能更准确地预测碰撞并改善自动驾驶决策。

title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
summary: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. We introduce DexForesight, a framework that learns spatial foresight implicitly by injecting dynamics-aware world representations into the latent space of a dexterous policy. During training, DexForesight learns an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline scene depth, kinematic hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories. The world model predicts 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes, capturing both articulated hand dynamics and scene changes under demonstrated actions, including the motion of fingers occluded from the cameras. We then freeze the world model and align policy queries with its predictive world queries, transferring the learned spatial dynamics into policy latents and using them to condition action generation. At deployment, only the policy is retained, operating on RGB observations, language, and robot state without depth input or explicit future prediction. On 11 DexJoCo simulation tasks, DexForesight improves the overall success rate of the base policy from 49.4% to 60.5%. On three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks, DexForesight achieves 58.3% success, compared with 50.0% for the strongest baseline.Project page https://dexforesight.github.io/
summary_zh: 灵巧操作需要对周围场景和机器人手部具备丰富的空间前瞻能力。现有的世界-动作模型通常通过显式的未来预测来获取此类预测性知识。我们提出了DexForesight框架，该框架通过将动力学感知的世界表示注入灵巧策略的潜空间，以隐式方式学习空间前瞻能力。在训练阶段，DexForesight从离线场景深度、运动学手部几何和示教轨迹中学习一个以动作条件化的空间世界模型。该世界模型预测3D手部点运动及视觉特征变化，捕捉演示动作下的关节手部动力学和场景变化，包括被相机遮挡的手指运动。随后，我们冻结世界模型，并将策略查询与其预测性世界查询对齐，将学习到的空间动力学迁移到策略潜空间中，并以此调节动作生成。在部署阶段，仅保留策略，直接基于RGB观测、语言和机器人状态运行，无需深度输入或显式未来预测。在11项DexJoCo仿真任务中，DexForesight将基线策略的总体成功率从49.4%提升至60.5%。在三项真实机器人灵巧操作任务中，DexForesight达到了58.3%的成功率，而最强基线为50.0%。项目页面：https://dexforesight.github.io/
tldr: DexForesight implicitly learns spatial foresight by aligning a policy's latent space with an action-conditioned world model trained on offline scene depth and kinematic hand geometry, improving dexterous manipulation success across simulation and real robots.
tldr_zh: DexForesight通过将策略的潜在空间与在离线场景深度和运动学手部几何上训练的动作条件世界模型对齐，隐式地学习空间预见能力，提高了仿真和真实机器人上的灵巧操作成功率。

title: MOSU2: Long-range Navigation System with Multi-modal Scene Understanding
summary: Robots that travel long distances through public outdoor spaces must do more than avoid obstacles: they must remain on terrain suited to their mobility and decide when to proceed, yield, or detour around pedestrians, cyclists, vehicles, traffic signals, and temporary restrictions. These decisions are difficult because their correctness often depends on how a scene evolves, such as whether an approaching car is slowing or a cyclist will cross the robot's path. Vision-language models (VLMs) can interpret such cues, but they reason over images that lack metric geometry and motion. Supplying this evidence at every step is too slow for real-time navigation, and hand-crafted triggers cannot anticipate the open-ended variety of outdoor situations. We present MOSU2, a long-range navigation system with two-stage trajectory selection, in which first-stage contextual reasoning determines when additional evidence is needed and what to retrieve. Only when an interaction remains unresolved does the first stage trigger the second stage to retrieve geometric and dynamic information and align it with scene context to make navigation decisions. Building on MOSU, MOSU2 follows routes from GPS-based route planning and filters candidate trajectories through multi-modal traversability analysis before selecting a trajectory to move the robot. In real-world experiments spanning stop gestures, construction sites, crosswalks, and roads shared with vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians, MOSU2 raises mean navigation success from 61.8% to 94.2% and condition-detection accuracy from 72.2% to 91.4% over its single-image predecessor, at about 2.2 times its mean decision latency. Project website: https://jinggm.github.io/mosu2/
summary_zh: 在公共场所长距离行驶的机器人不仅要避开障碍物，还必须保持在适合其机动性的地形上，并决定何时前进、让行或绕行行人、自行车、车辆、交通信号灯及临时限制。这些决策颇具难度，因为其正确性往往取决于场景的动态演变，例如迎面驶来的汽车是否在减速，或骑车人是否会横穿机器人的路径。视觉语言模型（VLM）能够解读此类线索，但其推理所基于的图像缺乏度量几何和运动信息。在每一步都提供这些证据对于实时导航而言过于缓慢，而手工设计的触发条件无法预判室外场景中开放式的多样情形。我们提出MOSU2，一种采用两阶段轨迹选择的长距离导航系统，其中第一阶段的情境推理决定何时需要额外证据以及需要检索什么内容。仅当交互尚未解决时，第一阶段才触发第二阶段检索几何和动态信息，并将其与场景情境对齐以做出导航决策。MOSU2在MOSU的基础上，遵循基于GPS的路线规划，并在选择移动机器人的轨迹之前，通过多模态可通行性分析对候选轨迹进行筛选。在涵盖停车手势、施工现场、人行横道以及与车辆、自行车和行人共用的道路的真实世界实验中，MOSU2相比其单图像前身，将平均导航成功率从61.8%提升至94.2%，条件检测准确率从72.2%提升至91.4%，而平均决策延迟约为前者的2.2倍。项目网站：https://jinggm.github.io/mosu2/
tldr: MOSU2 is a long-range navigation system that uses a two-stage trajectory selection approach, where first-stage contextual reasoning with VLMs triggers second-stage retrieval of geometric and dynamic information only when needed, improving navigation success and condition-detection accuracy in real-world outdoor experiments.
tldr_zh: MOSU2 是一种远程导航系统，采用两阶段轨迹选择方法，第一阶段使用 VLM 进行情境推理，仅在需要时触发第二阶段获取几何和动态信息，在真实世界室外实验中提高了导航成功率和条件检测准确率。

title: CrossLiDAR: Controllable Multi-Sensor LiDAR Sequence Generation
summary: High-fidelity LiDAR simulation remains a bottleneck for scalable development and validation of autonomous systems. Existing generators can synthesize realistic scans, but they are typically constrained to a single sensor configuration, offer limited control over structure and geometry, and drift in long-horizon 4D generation. We present CrossLiDAR, a unified transformer-based framework capable of generating controllable and spatio-temporally consistent multi-sensor LiDAR sequences. Our approach leverages a rectified flow objective with a Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT) backbone, within a compact latent space of range images. To support multiple LiDAR sensors, an Inter-sensor Module enables interaction across sensors, while a ControlNet-style branch provides structural conditioning (e.g., BEV priors or 3D bounding boxes). For modeling the temporal consistency, CrossLiDAR generates short $N$-frame sequences and extends them autoregressively to improve long-horizon coherence. Our model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average improvement of 29.56\% in JSD and 15.36\% in MMD evaluated on nuScenes and the Waymo Dataset. CrossLiDAR bridges the gap to modern autonomous-driving simulation by enabling calibration-consistent multi-sensor LiDAR rollouts over long horizons for controllable, scenario-based testing.
summary_zh: 高保真LiDAR仿真仍是自主系统规模化开发与验证的瓶颈。现有生成器虽能合成逼真的扫描数据，但通常受限于单一传感器配置，对结构与几何的控制能力有限，且难以在长时间跨度的4D生成中保持一致性。我们提出CrossLiDAR，一个统一的基于Transformer的框架，能够生成可控且时空一致的多传感器LiDAR序列。该方法采用基于修正流目标与多模态扩散Transformer（MM-DiT）骨干网络，在紧凑的距离图像潜空间中进行生成。为支持多种LiDAR传感器，跨传感器模块实现了传感器间的交互，同时ControlNet风格的分支提供结构条件注入（如BEV先验或3D边界框）。在时序一致性建模方面，CrossLiDAR生成短片段\(N\)帧序列，并通过自回归方式扩展，以增强长时程连贯性。我们的模型显著优于最先进基线，在nuScenes和Waymo数据集上JSD平均提升29.56\%，MMD平均提升15.36\%。CrossLiDAR通过实现标定一致的多传感器LiDAR长时程展开，填补了现代自动驾驶仿真中的空白，为可控、基于场景的测试提供了支撑。
tldr: CrossLiDAR introduces a unified transformer-based framework for controllable, multi-sensor LiDAR sequence generation, using a rectified flow objective with Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformer and ControlNet-style conditioning to achieve state-of-the-art performance on nuScenes and Waymo.
tldr_zh: CrossLiDAR 提出了一个统一的基于 Transformer 的框架，用于可控的多传感器 LiDAR 序列生成，利用 rectified flow 目标、多模态扩散 Transformer 和 ControlNet 风格的条件化，在 nuScenes 和 Waymo 数据集上取得了最先进的性能。

title: From Festival Video to the Stage: A Sim-to-Real Ladder for Long-Horizon Expressive Whole-Body Dance on a Commercial Humanoid
summary: We present a pipeline for transferring Awa Odori, a traditional Japanese festival dance, from monocular video to a commercial Unitree G1 EDU humanoid. The pipeline combines human mesh recovery, kinematic retargeting, reinforcement learning for motion tracking in simulation, and onboard deployment via ONNX. Training ran on a single RTX 5070 GPU. An eleven-version deployment ladder evaluated on hardware examines three interventions. We detect and repair silent corruption of deployment artifacts, model state-estimator drift during training, and edit the reference motion to support stable execution and a controlled ending. The final policies achieved three consecutive rope-free completions of a 43-second routine, a 46-second performance with automatic handoff, and a continuous 9.7-minute rope-free performance composed from the captured motion. In a live handover, a single remote request let the robot start from and return to the manufacturer's walking controller on stage, with a measured torque-free window of 45-140 ms. We report the training dynamics and hardware outcomes and discuss failure boundaries involving compliant flooring and occlusion in monocular capture.
summary_zh: 我们提出了一套流水线，用于将日本传统节日舞蹈“阿波舞”从单目视频迁移至商用Unitree G1 EDU人形机器人。该流水线整合了人体网格恢复、运动学重定向、基于强化学习的仿真运动跟踪，以及通过ONNX实现的本机部署。训练在单张RTX 5070 GPU上完成。在硬件上评估的十一版部署阶梯检验了三项干预措施。我们检测并修复了部署工件的静默损坏，在训练过程中对状态估计器漂移进行了建模，并编辑了参考运动以支持稳定执行和控制性收尾。最终策略成功完成了连续三次无绳索的43秒套路表演、一次带自动交接的46秒演出，以及一次由采集动作拼接而成的连续9.7分钟无绳索表演。在一次现场交接中，单次远程请求使机器人能够从制造商自带的行走控制器启动并在舞台上返回该控制器，实测无扭矩窗口为45至140毫秒。我们报告了训练动态和硬件结果，并讨论了涉及柔性地板和单目采集遮挡的失败边界。
tldr: This paper presents a complete sim-to-real pipeline for transferring a traditional Japanese dance from monocular video to a commercial humanoid robot, addressing issues like artifact corruption, state-estimator drift, and reference motion editing, and achieving long-duration, rope-free hardware performances.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一条完整的从单目视频到商用人形机器人的仿真到现实迁移流水线，用于迁移传统日本舞蹈，解决了工件损坏、状态估计器漂移和参考运动编辑等问题，并在硬件上实现了长时间、无绳索的表演。

title: HARP-Bench: Benchmarking Robot Manipulation Around Active Humans
summary: Recent robot manipulation benchmarks have enabled systematic evaluation of general-purpose robot policies across diverse objects, scenes, instructions, and embodiments. However, most existing benchmarks still assume that the robot is the only active agent and that task semantics are determined primarily by the instruction and object state. This assumption overlooks a common source of real-world variation: humans actively sharing the workspace. In such settings, humans may reveal an implicit goal, complete part of the task, temporarily change object availability, or constrain safe robot motion while working nearby. We introduce HARP-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating robot manipulation policies in workspaces shared with active humans. HARP-Bench treats human activity as part of the manipulation problem, rather than as background scene variation. It organizes human-present manipulation into four conditions: Cueing, Contribution, Interruption, and Co-presence. These conditions are instantiated through everyday manipulation tasks, including paired human-present variants for controlled comparison with standard manipulation. HARP-Bench also provides a demonstration-generation pipeline for dynamic human-present settings. We evaluate VLA models, imitation-learning methods, and heuristic policies on HARP-Bench. Human-present variations challenge current policies, and higher task success does not consistently improve safety. Quantitative failure analysis identifies manipulation and recovery as the dominant remaining challenges. Training with HARP-Bench demonstrations improves human-present performance in simulation. A real-world study on one task family shows improved performance under human contribution, but not interruption, providing initial evidence of the data's utility and identifying limits of transfer. Code is available at https://github.com/UMass-Embodied-AGI/harp.
summary_zh: 近期关于机器人操作领域的基准测试，已经能够对通用型机器人策略在多样化物体、场景、指令及实体配置上的表现进行系统性评估。然而，大多数现有基准测试仍假设机器人是唯一的活动主体，且任务语义主要由指令和物体状态决定。这一假设忽视了现实世界中一个常见的变化来源：人类主动共享工作空间。在此类情境下，人类可能透露出隐含的目标、完成部分任务、临时改变物体的可获取性，或在附近工作时限制机器人的安全运动范围。为此，我们引入了HARP-Bench，这是一项专为评估在与活跃人类共享的工作空间中运行的机器人操作策略而设计的基准测试。HARP-Bench将人类活动视为操作问题的一部分，而非背景场景的变动。它将涉及人类在场的操作任务划分为四种情形：提示（Cueing）、贡献（Contribution）、打断（Interruption）和共存（Co-presence）。这些情形通过日常操作任务具体实现，并包含了配对的人类在场变体，以便与标准操作进行对照比较。HARP-Bench还提供了一套面向动态人类在场场景的演示生成流程。我们在HARP-Bench上评估了视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型、模仿学习方法及启发式策略的表现。人类在场的变体对当前策略构成了挑战，而更高的任务成功率并不总能转化为更好的安全性。定量失败分析指出，操作与恢复能力仍是主要的挑战所在。利用HARP-Bench演示数据进行训练，能够提升模拟环境中人类在场场景下的表现。针对一个任务族进行的真实世界研究表明，在人类贡献的情形下性能有所提升，但在打断情形下则未见改善，这初步证明了数据的实用性，同时也揭示了迁移的局限。相关代码已公开于 https://github.com/UMass-Embodied-AGI/harp。
tldr: HARP-Bench introduces a benchmark for evaluating robot manipulation policies in workspaces shared with active humans, categorizing human-present manipulation into four conditions and showing that current VLA and IL policies struggle with safety and adaptability in these settings.
tldr_zh: HARP-Bench 提出了一个基准，用于评估在人类主动共享工作空间中的机器人操作策略，将人类在场操作分为四类条件，并表明当前的 VLA 和 IL 策略在这些场景中的安全性和适应性存在不足。

title: Efficient VLA Inference via Retrieval-Based Speculation and Hardware Acceleration
summary:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to understand and execute complex instructions, but their autoregressive (AR) action generation introduces significant latency on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Speculative decoding can accelerate AR-based inference by parallelizing action generation and verification; however, existing approaches rely on costly draft models, which are inefficient on edge platforms.
  In this paper, we propose Zora, a hardware-software co-design framework for accelerating AR-based VLA inference. Specifically, Zora introduces a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based draft model that exploits robotic dynamics without additional neural draft models. We further reduce batch verification overhead through a kinematics-guided action-acceptance strategy and a KV-cache-sharing attention mechanism. To address the retrieval overhead introduced by RAG-based drafting, we co-design dedicated hardware support, Zora core, to address the memory irregularity in RAG-based drafting. We evaluate Zora on four VLA models with the LIBERO benchmark. Zora retains comparable accuracy while achieving up to 3.4$\times$ speedup with software-only optimization and up to 7.6$\times$ speedup with hardware support over GPUs.
summary_zh:
视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型使机器人能够理解并执行复杂指令，但其自回归（AR）动作生成在资源受限的机器人平台上引入了显著延迟。推测解码可通过并行化动作生成与验证来加速基于自回归的推理；然而，现有方法依赖成本高昂的草稿模型，在边缘平台上效率较低。

本文提出Zora，一种用于加速基于自回归的VLA推理的软硬件协同设计框架。具体而言，Zora引入了一种基于轻量级检索增强生成（RAG）的草稿模型，利用机器人动力学特性，无需额外的神经草稿模型。我们进一步通过运动学引导的动作接受策略和键值缓存共享注意力机制，降低了批量验证的开销。为解决RAG式草稿生成引入的检索开销，我们协同设计了专用硬件支持——Zora核心，以应对RAG式草稿生成中的内存不规则性问题。我们基于LIBERO基准在四种VLA模型上对Zora进行了评估。Zora在保持相当精度的同时，在仅软件优化下实现了最高3.4倍的加速，在硬件支持下相比GPU实现了最高7.6倍的加速。
tldr: Zora is a hardware-software co-design framework that accelerates autoregressive VLA inference on edge robots via a retrieval-augmented draft model, kinematics-guided acceptance, KV-cache sharing, and dedicated hardware, achieving up to 7.6x speedup on LIBERO.
tldr_zh: Zora 是一个软硬件协同设计框架，通过检索增强草稿模型、运动学引导的接受策略、KV缓存共享和专用硬件来加速边缘机器人上的自回归VLA推理，在LIBERO上实现最高7.6倍加速。

title: Control-Aware Command Generation for Asynchronous Control and Action Inference with Vision-Based Policies towards Fast Execution
summary: Vision-based control policies, including vision-language-action models, have enabled robots to perform increasingly complex tasks. However, their execution speed is often limited by the high computational cost of action inference. In this work, we investigate what can be achieved at the control level without modifying the underlying policy learning process. We introduce an asynchronous inference and control framework that enables fast task execution while maintaining smooth and stable robot motions. By formulating the generation of continuous target positions from discontinuous model predictions as a tracking control problem, our method makes asynchronous inference practical for real robots. We further accelerate execution through adaptive action skipping based on the variance of predicted positions. Experiments with Action Chunking Transformer and OpenVLA-OFT on a bimanual robot demonstrate substantial speedups while preserving high task success rates.
summary_zh: 基于视觉的控制策略，包括视觉-语言-动作模型，已经使机器人能够执行日益复杂的任务。然而，其执行速度往往受到动作推理高计算成本的限制。在本研究中，我们探讨了在不修改底层策略学习过程的情况下，在控制层面能够实现何种改进。我们引入了一种异步推理与控制框架，该框架能够在实现快速任务执行的同时，保持机器人运动的平滑与稳定。通过将不连续的模型预测转换为连续目标位置的生成问题，并将其建模为跟踪控制问题，我们的方法使异步推理在实际机器人上得以切实应用。我们进一步基于预测位置的方差采用自适应动作跳过机制，以加速执行过程。在双臂机器人上使用动作分块变换器（Action Chunking Transformer）和OpenVLA-OFT进行的实验表明，该方法在显著提升速度的同时保持了较高的任务成功率。
tldr: The paper introduces an asynchronous control and action inference framework for vision-based robot policies, using tracking control to generate continuous targets from discontinuous predictions and adaptive action skipping to speed up execution without modifying the policy learning process. It demonstrates substantial speedups on a bimanual robot with ACT and OpenVLA-OFT while maintaining task success rates.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于基于视觉的机器人策略的异步控制和动作推理框架，通过跟踪控制生成连续目标位置并采用自适应动作跳过加速执行，无需修改策略学习过程，并在双机械臂上验证了显著加速和任务成功率保持。

title: ObjectWorld: Scaling Object-Centric World Models with A Large-Scale 3D Full-Object Flow Dataset
summary: Generative world modeling from large-scale visual data offers a promising path toward scalable robot manipulation. This calls for an intermediate representation that can be supervised at scale and remains actionable for downstream control. We propose 3D full-object flow, an object-centric motion representation that assigns dense 3D trajectories to points across the complete surface of a target object, including its occluded regions. By extending visible-surface object flow to the full object geometry, this representation makes complete object motion explicit and applies uniformly to both rigid and deformable objects. To realize the potential of this representation at scale, we introduce a 1210-hour full-object flow dataset that addresses the scarcity of large-scale supervision for complete 3D object motion. The dataset integrates diverse real-world videos and physical simulations, with a scalable annotation pipeline for recovering full-object motion from real-world observations and quality metrics for systematically assessing annotation quality. We then train a world model that takes an image and a task description as input and predicts dense full-object flow over the reconstructed object geometry. Experiments show reliable annotation quality, data-scalable flow prediction, and effective downstream manipulation across novel scenes and robot embodiments. Project website with additional results and videos: https://nus-lins-lab.github.io/ObjectWorld/.
summary_zh: 生成世界模型从大规模视觉数据中为可扩展的机器人操作提供了一条很有前景的路径。这需要一种中间表示，既能在大规模数据上进行监督学习，又能对下游控制保持可操作性。我们提出了三维全物体流（3D full-object flow），这是一种以物体为中心的运动表示，为目标物体完整表面上的点赋予密集的三维轨迹，包括其被遮挡的区域。通过将可见表面物体流扩展到完整的物体几何结构，该表示使完整的物体运动变得明确，并统一适用于刚体和可变形物体。为了在大规模上实现该表示的潜力，我们引入了一个1210小时的全物体流数据集，以解决完整三维物体运动的大规模监督数据稀缺的问题。该数据集整合了多样化的真实世界视频和物理仿真，并配备了一个可扩展的标注流程，用于从真实世界观测中恢复完整的物体运动，以及用于系统评估标注质量的质量指标。随后，我们训练了一个世界模型，该模型以图像和任务描述为输入，并在重建的物体几何结构上预测密集的全物体流。实验表明，该模型在标注质量上可靠，流预测可随数据规模扩展，并且在新场景和不同机器人形态下均能实现有效的下游操作。包含更多结果和视频的项目网站：https://nus-lins-lab.github.io/ObjectWorld/。
tldr: ObjectWorld proposes 3D full-object flow as an object-centric motion representation and introduces a large-scale 1210-hour dataset to train world models that predict dense full-object flow from images and task descriptions, enabling scalable robot manipulation across novel scenes and embodiments.
tldr_zh: ObjectWorld 提出三维全物体流作为物体中心的运动表示，并构建了 1210 小时的大规模数据集，用于训练世界模型，使其能从图像和任务描述中预测稠密全物体流，从而支持新颖场景和机器人形态下的可扩展操作。

title: BAT-WAM: Bridging Action and Touch in World-Action Models for Dexterous Hands
summary: Dexterous manipulation with world action models (WAMs) relies on hand configuration and contact information, yet joint-state and whole-hand tactile observations may be partially or entirely missing. RGB images provide scene context and hand-object geometry but are insufficient to reliably recover these missing modalities. We further observe a correlation between hand state and tactile information. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BAT-WAM, a framework that bridges visual, joint-state, and tactile representations for WAMs. BAT-WAM learns separate codebooks and decoders for the tactile and action streams. An RGB-conditioned continuous latent bridge connects the two streams for bidirectional learning, while visual information serves as continuous context. Under the HTBench evaluation protocol, BAT-WAM reduces the root mean squared error (RMSE) of tactile reconstruction by 34.73% under fully masked conditions and 38.84% under partially masked conditions, relative to an image-conditioned HandTouch checkpoint. For future tactile prediction conditioned on target-time RGB and historical actions, it reduces mean RMSE by 85.56% relative to OpenWAM with HandTouch. Real-robot experiments further show that BAT-WAM consistently outperforms related WAM baselines in dexterous manipulation. Generalization experiments on unseen objects and scenes also demonstrate substantial improvements over baseline models. These findings support joint modeling of visual context, hand state, and touch as a representation approach for multimodal WAMs.
summary_zh: 基于世界动作模型（WAMs）的灵巧操作依赖于手部构型与接触信息，然而关节状态和全手触觉观测可能部分或完全缺失。RGB图像提供了场景上下文及手-物几何信息，但不足以可靠地恢复这些缺失模态。我们进一步观察到手部状态与触觉信息之间存在相关性。受此观察启发，我们提出BAT-WAM，一个为WAMs桥接视觉、关节状态与触觉表示的框架。BAT-WAM为触觉流和动作流分别学习独立的码本与解码器。一个以RGB为条件的连续潜变量桥接网络连接两条流以实现双向学习，同时视觉信息作为连续上下文。在HTBench评估协议下，与以图像为条件的HandTouch检查点相比，BAT-WAM在全掩蔽条件下将触觉重建的均方根误差（RMSE）降低了34.73%，在部分掩蔽条件下降低了38.84%。对于以目标时刻RGB和历史动作条件化的未来触觉预测，其平均RMSE相对于OpenWAM结合HandTouch降低了85.56%。真实机器人实验进一步表明，BAT-WAM在灵巧操作中始终优于相关的WAM基线模型。针对未见物体和场景的泛化实验也显示出相对于基线模型的显著改进。这些发现支持将视觉上下文、手部状态与触觉进行联合建模，作为多模态WAMs的一种表示方法。
tldr: BAT-WAM introduces a framework that bridges visual, joint-state, and tactile representations in world action models, improving tactile reconstruction and future prediction for dexterous manipulation, with real-robot validation.
tldr_zh: BAT-WAM 提出了一种在世界动作模型中桥接视觉、关节状态和触觉表示的框架，改善了灵巧操作的触觉重建和未来预测，并通过真实机器人实验验证。

title: From Game Generation to Game Playing: Fully Automated Ability Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Training vision-language-action (VLA) models to follow gameplay instructions across diverse games is limited by the cost of collecting demonstrations. We introduce a framework that automatically generates game environments and expert demonstrations. An LLM-powered agent uses game-building tools to construct executable environments and tasks targeting specified skills. Programmatic experts then use privileged simulator state to generate aligned instructions, rendered observations, and keyboard and mouse actions. We train our game policy, Script2Play, by post-training a 4B vision-language model with behavior cloning on 150.3 hours of synthetic Minecraft and Roblox gameplay, without human gameplay demonstrations or reinforcement learning. Evaluation on multiple public game benchmarks demonstrates that Script2Play follows gameplay instructions effectively and generalizes across game engines, highlighting the effectiveness of targeted synthetic supervision.
summary_zh: 训练视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在多样化游戏中遵循游戏指令的能力，受限于收集示范数据的成本。我们提出了一种框架，能够自动生成游戏环境和专家示范。一个由大语言模型驱动的智能体利用游戏构建工具，针对指定技能构建可执行的环境和任务。随后，程序化专家利用特权模拟器状态生成对齐的指令、渲染观测以及键盘和鼠标操作。我们通过在后训练阶段对40亿参数的视觉-语言模型进行行为克隆，使用了150.3小时的合成《我的世界》和《罗布乐思》游戏数据，训练了我们的游戏策略模型Script2Play，全程无需人类游戏示范或强化学习。在多个公开游戏基准上的评估表明，Script2Play能够有效遵循游戏指令，并跨游戏引擎实现泛化，凸显了针对性合成监督的有效性。
tldr: This paper introduces a framework that automatically generates game environments and expert demonstrations to train a vision-language-action model, Script2Play, for gameplay instruction following, demonstrating generalization across game engines without human data.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一个自动生成游戏环境和专家演示的框架，用于训练视觉-语言-动作模型Script2Play，使其能遵循游戏指令并跨游戏引擎泛化，无需人工数据。

title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
summary: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.
summary_zh: 近期基于前沿多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的具身智能体研究，围绕MLLM开发了配套的工程框架，例如集成后训练策略及递归自我改进循环的框架。然而，这些额外机制是否超越了MLLM自身的原生能力，仍未得到充分探究。我们提出SimplEvo，旨在探索在直接控制下，MLLM仅凭其以自写文本记忆保留执行经验，能够实现多大的性能提升。该方法无需权重更新、后训练策略或特权信息。MLLM仅依据一次示范，即撰写一份与坐标无关的任务记忆。在严格的训练-测试协议下，它仅在训练片段上构建有界的工作记忆，并在每个片段结束后，依据关于流程、完成情况及恢复的教训对其进行优化。两种记忆在测试阶段均保持不变。在EBench基准上，SimplEvo将GPT-6-Astra在直接控制下的成功率（SR）从46.7%提升至81.7%，并以69.63%的SR和75.32的得分位居RoboDojo排行榜首位。与同时存储过往视觉帧的记忆相比，SimplEvo仅凭文本记忆即可达到相近的SR，且所用令牌更少。在记忆固定不变的情况下，SimplEvo还能泛化至未见过的布局及随机化场景配置。此外，该工作记忆具有跨模型迁移性：由GPT-6-Astra生成的记忆，可被较弱的MLLM直接复用，并在无需自身任何适配的情况下提升其性能。
tldr: This paper introduces SimplEvo, a memory-based method that improves the success rate of multimodal large language models on embodied agent tasks by writing and iteratively refining text-only task memories from demonstrations and training episodes, without weight updates or privileged information.
tldr_zh: 本文提出SimplEvo，一种基于记忆的方法，通过从演示和训练情节中编写并迭代优化纯文本任务记忆，在无需权重更新或特权信息的情况下，提高了多模态大语言模型在具身智能任务上的成功率。

title: Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration
summary: Autonomous UAV exploration is increasingly used for large-scale surveying and inspection in inaccessible or disaster-affected environments, where onboard memory and computational resources are often severely constrained. Most existing UAV exploration systems maintain globally queryable geometric map representations for motion planning and exploration decision-making, causing memory consumption and spatial-query costs to increase with the explored area. Robot-centric local mapping bounds dense-map memory and computation but discards global task context needed for long-horizon exploration.We present FLAVOR, a hierarchical spatio-temporal framework that confines dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while retaining compact global observation and task context. At the observation level, lightweight LiDAR-keyframe visibility records preserve ray-wise evidence for frontier reasoning. At the task level, unresolved frontiers beyond the local-map extent are retained as compact pending tasks associated with odometry anchors. A sparse topological graph connects these anchors through retained routes for future revisits.Upon returning to a task region, FLAVOR reconstructs the frontier and exploration viewpoint from observations, while the topological route is instantiated and validated against the current local map before execution. Dense-map capacity remains fixed as exploration expands, with exploration-dependent memory growth confined to compact observation and task context.FLAVOR achieves 31.98--41.88% shorter exploration time and a 94--99% smaller map memory footprint than the best baseline that completes all three simulated scenes. In real-world deployments, it reduces this footprint by 92.67% in the forest and 62.42% at the construction site relative to an explicit point-cloud ikd-tree while preserving long-term task continuity under constrained onboard resources.
summary_zh: 自主无人机勘探越来越多地用于在无法进入或受灾环境中进行大规模测量和检查，而这类环境中机载存储和计算资源往往受到严重限制。现有的大多数无人机勘探系统为运动规划和勘探决策维护全局可查询的几何地图表示，导致内存消耗和空间查询成本随勘探面积增加而增长。以机器人为中心的局部地图限制了稠密地图的内存和计算，但丢弃了长时间勘探所需的全局任务上下文。我们提出了FLAVOR，一种分层时空框架，将稠密度量几何限制在以机器人为中心的局部地图中，同时保留紧凑的全局观测和任务上下文。在观测层面，轻量级LiDAR关键帧可见性记录保留了用于前沿推理的逐射线证据。在任务层面，超出局部地图范围未解决的前沿被保留为与里程计锚点关联的紧凑待处理任务。稀疏拓扑图通过这些锚点经由保留路径连接，以支持未来重访。当返回任务区域时，FLAVOR从观测中重建前沿和勘探视点，同时拓扑路径在执行前被实例化并针对当前局部地图进行验证。随着勘探范围扩展，稠密地图容量保持固定，与勘探相关的内存增长仅限于紧凑的观测和任务上下文。与完成所有三个仿真场景的最佳基线相比，FLAVOR实现了31.98-41.88%的勘探时间缩短，以及94-99%的地图内存占用减少。在实际部署中，相较于显式点云ikd-tree，其在森林环境中将内存占用减少92.67%，在建筑工地减少62.42%，同时在受限机载资源下保持了长期任务连续性。
tldr: FLAVOR introduces a hierarchical spatio-temporal map representation for UAV exploration, using robot-centric local dense maps plus compact global observation and task context (LiDAR keyframes, pending frontiers, sparse topological graph) to keep memory bounded while achieving faster exploration and drastically reduced memory footprint in large-scale 3D tasks.
tldr_zh: FLAVOR 提出了一种用于无人机探索的层次化时空地图表示，通过机器人中心局部稠密地图和紧凑的全局观测与任务上下文（LiDAR 关键帧、待处理边界、稀疏拓扑图）在保持记忆受限的同时实现更快的探索和大幅降低的存储占用。

title: Off-Policy RL with Online Inference Tuning: My Solution to the CoRL 2026 RoboEval Challenge
